Digital work is widely integrated, whereas automated work remains limited. Both show links to psychosocial risks and resources. Legal regulations, organizational support, and individual strategies may mitigate adverse impacts. Future research should clarify mechanisms, broaden outcome assessment beyond burnout, and evaluate preventive measures amid rapid technological change.

title: Adaptive dual-programming magnetic soft robot with lifelike behavior.
text: Magnetic soft robots with embodied intelligence of multimodal motions, environmental perception, and functional decoupling depend on ingenious material arrangement and programmable morphing information introduction. While some efforts have been made, achieving lifelike behaviors for soft robots in system-level strategy remains a notable challenge. Here, we present dual-programming hydrogel-based soft robots (DHSRs) that couple magnetic and anisotropic programming through the spatial arrangement of patterned magnetic skeletons into responsive and structural hydrogel bodies. These DHSRs exhibit programmable exquisite and multicurved structures in three-dimensional (3D) space, environment-adaptive deformation behaviors proved by switching from random jumping on land to regular swimming in water of a fish-like soft robot, and further locomotion-function decoupling capabilities of region-selective cargo delivery in an integrated "locomotion-perception-action" workflow. Our strategy in biomedical potential is exemplified by a ring-like pH-responsive DHSR for gastric ulcer therapy, which integrates multimodal locomotion (rolling, tumbling, and rotating), adaptive matching, and microneedle-mediated penetration. By collaborating with a capsule endoscopy system, we explore the possibility of a wireless and painless diagnostic-therapeutic platform in a pig model. This strategy endows the robot with perception and multitask execution capabilities, highlighting a promising route for the intelligent evolution of soft robots across diverse application domains.

title: The surgeon in the loop: automation bias and human-AI interaction in robotic surgery.
text: Artificial intelligence systems for intraoperative surgical guidance are approaching clinical deployment, yet no study has quantified automation bias (defined as the tendency to over-rely on automated recommendations) in the context of surgical decision-making. As these systems enter operative workflows, the surgeon's ability to recognize and override incorrect AI guidance becomes a critical safety requirement. To measure the extent to which surgeons modify incision plans after exposure to AI-labeled visual guidance and to determine the rate at which incorrect AI suggestions are accepted. A two-phase controlled experiment was conducted among 19 surgeons (10 residents, 2 fellows, 7 attendings). Participants drew incision lines on 20 static frames from robotic cholecystectomy videos, first without guidance (Phase 01) and then with a mock AI overlay (Phase 02). Overlays were either correct (derived from expert consensus) or deliberately incorrect (shifted toward unsafe anatomy) at an approximately 70:30 ratio. No actual AI model was used. The primary outcome was mean perpendicular distance (MPD) between Phase 01 and Phase 02 lines. Secondary outcomes included AI-corridor adherence, over-reliance and under-reliance rates, behavioral accuracy, and confidence shift. Across 231 paired observations, MPD did not differ significantly between correct (75.5 pixels; SD, 33.4) and incorrect (71.1 pixels; SD, 31.7) overlay conditions (P = .35). Directional analysis revealed that surgeons accepted incorrect AI suggestions in 60.6% of incorrect-overlay frames (43/71), with a specificity for rejecting incorrect guidance of only 39.4% (28/71). Correct suggestions were accepted 76.9% of the time (123/160). Overall behavioral accuracy was 65.4%. Self-reported confidence increased significantly after AI exposure (Δ = + 0.65; P < .001). Surgeons accepted approximately 3 of every 5 incorrect AI recommendations. As intraoperative AI systems approach deployment, surgeon oversight cannot be assumed to neutralize algorithmic error; it must be empirically measured, deliberately designed for, and prospectively validated.

title: Artificial intelligence for vascular minimally invasive surgery: techniques, clinical integration, and challenges.
text: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS), including endovascular and robot-assisted procedures, is widely used for vascular pathologies but remains limited by technical complexity, cognitive workload, and postoperative complications. Artificial Intelligence (AI) may help address these challenges through predictive analysis, decision support, image analysis, and automation. A structured Google Scholar search was conducted from February 21, 2025, to January 1, 2026, and updated through September 2026. Peer-reviewed studies applying AI to vascular MIS were included, with additional targeted searches addressing clinical translation, deployment, regulation, and ethical considerations. Thirty primary studies were analyzed, including eight on machine learning, nine on deep learning, four on natural language processing, and nine on robotics or reinforcement learning. Machine learning supported risk stratification and outcome prediction, deep learning enabled imaging and segmentation applications, natural language processing facilitated clinical information extraction, and robotic systems supported navigation and procedural assistance. AI demonstrates substantial potential across the vascular MIS pathway, but broader clinical adoption requires stronger validation, prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, health-economic evaluation, and careful consideration of regulatory, liability, and accessibility challenges.

title: Software-based concordance analysis of a predictive surgical planning model for target gap achievement in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
text: In robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA), achieving soft-tissue balance requires repeated intraoperative plan adjustment and remains experience-dependent. Predictive models may support planning, but their clinical value depends on whether model-generated plans approximate predefined target gaps within the robotic workflow. This study assessed the software-based concordance between model-generated plans and predefined target gaps in robotic-assisted TKA. The predefined target gaps were planning set points established within the robotic software rather than measured intraoperative gaps. This retrospective software-based concordance study included 209 complete-case knees undergoing robotic-assisted TKA. A machine-learning-based predictive model generated a bone-resection plan, which was imported into the robotic planning software to calculate software-derived medial and lateral gaps in extension and flexion. These software-derived gaps were compared with predefined target gaps, which were planning set points rather than measured values and were 18 mm in 819 of 836 gap-level observations (98.0%). The primary analysis focused on target gap deviation, defined as the software-derived gap minus the predefined target gap. As a benchmark, the deviation of the preadjustment gaps from the same targets was used as a preadjustment reference. A total of 836 gap-level observations were analyzed. The overall mean target gap deviation was -0.142 mm (SD, 1.411 mm), with a mean absolute error of 1.016 mm. Overall, 77.6% of software-derived gaps were within ±1 mm of target, and 93.4% were within ±2 mm. Bland-Altman analysis showed a small overall bias of -0.142 mm, with 95% limits of agreement from -2.91 to +2.62 mm. At the knee level, only 43.1% of knees had all software-derived gaps within ±1 mm of target. Gap-level deviations ranged from -7 mm to +5 mm, and 16.3% of knees (34/209) had at least one gap with an absolute deviation > 2 mm. Compared with the preadjustment reference (MAE 2.002 mm, 49.4% within ±1 mm), the model substantially reduced deviation (MAE 1.016 mm, 77.6% within ±1 mm, p < 0.001). In this software-based concordance analysis, the predictive planning model generated surgical plans whose robotic software-derived gaps approximated predefined target gaps with a mean absolute deviation of approximately 1 mm. The model-generated plan reduced target-gap deviation relative to the initial preadjustment plan within this target-conditioned workflow. However, because the targets were near-uniform (98.0% at 18 mm) and all measurements were software-derived, compartment-specific bias, moderate whole-knee consistency (43.1%), and occasional outlier deviations indicate that the model should be used as a surgeon-supervised decision support tool rather than as an autonomous planner. Prospective validation against measured intraoperative and postoperative gaps is required before clinical effectiveness can be claimed.

title: Dual-channel periodic event-triggered sensing and control for wheeled mobile robots based on an extended state observer.
text: This paper presents a dual-channel periodic event-triggered sensing and control scheme for wheeled mobile robots subject to unknown dynamics and external disturbances. A line-of-sight guidance law generates the reference linear and angular velocities. Two periodic event-triggered mechanisms regulate transmissions over the sensor-to-controller and controller-to-actuator channels, respectively. Extended state observers driven by the triggered velocities estimate the lumped disturbances, based on which an anti-disturbance control law is developed. Stability analysis establishes input-to-state stability of the closed-loop system, while periodic evaluation of the triggering conditions inherently excludes Zeno behavior. Simulation results demonstrate satisfactory path-following performance under intermittent information transmission while effectively reducing sensor-to-controller and controller-to-actuator transmissions.

title: CDK4 maintains cytoskeletal homeostasis by restraining actomyosin contractility.
text: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4) is best known for its canonical role in cell-cycle control, yet how CDK4 activity intersects with cellular architecture remains poorly defined. Here, we uncover a non-canonical function of CDK4 in maintaining cytoskeletal mechanical homeostasis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) cells. We show that CDK4 phosphorylates the RhoA-targeting RhoGAP Myo9b at serine 1935, enhancing its GAP activity and restraining RhoA-ROCK-pMLC-dependent actomyosin contractility. Loss or inhibition of CDK4 alters cell morphology, disrupts actin organization, and increases contractility. Elevated contractility in CDK4-deficient cells induces collapse of the intermediate filament network, characterized by Vimentin reorganization and mitochondrial redistribution, indicating a higher-order defect in cytoskeletal architecture. Furthermore, CDK4 expression negatively correlates with pMLC levels in both mouse TNBC tumors and human breast cancer samples, supporting the physiological relevance of this pathway. Together, these findings identify CDK4 as a regulator of cellular mechanical stability, integrating actin dynamics, intermediate filament integrity, and organelle positioning, and reveal an unexpected role for CDK4 beyond cell-cycle regulation.

title: Magnetically Actuated Continuum Robots: From Engineering to Clinical Translation.
text: Magnetically actuated continuum robots (MACRs) have emerged as a promising approach for minimally invasive surgery. By using external magnetic fields to apply torques and forces at the instrument tip, MACRs move actuation outside the patient, thus reducing the mechanical complexity of the robot. This architecture enables miniaturization, improved compliance, and improved steering capabilities, especially for navigating intricate intravascular or endoluminal pathways. Despite substantial progress in functional materials, robotic archetypes, and magnetic field generation platforms, effective clinical translation requires holistic consideration of surgical workflows, intraoperative localization, and operator interaction. Integrating these engineering advances into routine clinical practice remains an ongoing challenge. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of recent advances in MACRs from a clinical perspective, highlighting technologies that accelerate their translation into minimally invasive surgery. The fundamental working principles of MACRs are first outlined, followed by a task- driven categorization of robotic designs. The emerging strategies for intraoperative localization and motion control at varying levels of autonomy are then evaluated. Furthermore, representative applications across physiological systems are summarized. Finally, key challenges are highlighted to elucidate current technological boundaries and provide a roadmap for future research.

title: Event-triggered pinning control on projective-lag synchronization of coupled switched delayed networks under DoS attacks.
text: In industrial network applications, drive-response systems may encounter issues such as denial-of-service attacks, communication delays and parameter switching, which can even undermine their stability or synchronization. However, few effective methods currently exist to address the synchronization problem of switched systems under the coupled influence of these practical factors. Based on this, this paper proposes a novel event-triggered pinning impulsive controller to achieve projective lag synchronization for driving-response coupled switched delayed neural networks (CSDNNs) subject to DoS attacks. Firstly, according to the communication delay and security of switched neural networks, a more general CSDNN model with communication delays and DoS attacks is constructed. Secondly, an efficient event-triggered pinning impulsive controller is established by considering the influence of network scale and control cost. It is worth mentioning that periodic event sampling and continuous event sampling are adopted depending on whether DoS attacks occur, which can effectively avoid Zeno behavior and reduce the control cost. Hence, by introducing a proper Lyapunov-Krasovskii function, the synchronization problems of the pinned nodes and the others for the CSDNNs are respectively discussed and sufficient conditions are obtained under certain assumptions. Meanwhile, the coupling relations among some nodes can be eliminated to increase the network's flexibility according to the pinning control. Finally, the proposed synchronization theory is verified through numerical simulations and a robotic arm experiment, demonstrating its efficacy in addressing real-world automation challenges under network constraints and security threats, thereby bridging the gap between theory and practice.

title: Fluid-driven robotic micromanipulation for assembloid fabrication.
text: The assembly of cellular spheroids into spatially organized assembloids represents a transformative paradigm for modeling complex biological systems. However, the lack of standardized fabrication strategies fundamentally limits the precision and reproducibility of these models, hindering their widespread application. Here, we present a robotic micromanipulation platform-Fluid-Driven Tweezer with Visual Servo Control (FDT-VSC). By integrating multidimensional visual perception with microfluidic control, our system enables the gentle and programmable assembly of diverse cellular spheroids. Leveraging this platform, we achieve the bottom-up construction of structurally defined, heterogeneous multicellular tissues, and the programmed orchestration of multilineage models that recapitulate the complex microenvironments of early organogenesis. Crucially, the system improves consistency during the scalable fabrication of tumor-stroma assembloids, supporting reliable drug screening. These results demonstrate that FDT-VSC advances assembloid-based applications across modular tissue engineering, developmental biology, and drug discovery.

title: Multilocus Characterization of Podosphaera fragariae Causing Strawberry Powdery Mildew in Lima, Peru: Evidence from ITS, GAPDH, and RPB2 Phylogeny.
text: Powdery mildew associated with Fragaria × ananassa Duch. has recently been reinterpreted as a species complex comprising Podosphaera fragariae in Eurasia and P. shepherdiae in the Americas; however, molecular data for South American populations remain scarce, and the few South American specimens sequenced to date have been assigned to P. shepherdiae. In this study, the causal agent of powdery mildew on strawberry cultivar 'Sabrina' grown in Lima, Peru, was characterized through morphological analysis, pathogenicity tests, and multilocus phylogenetic inference based on ITS, GAPDH, and RPB2. The fungal material examined developed mycelial colonies typical of powdery mildew and consistently reproduced the symptoms observed in the field. Morphologically, the pathogen exhibited characteristics consistent with Podosphaera sect. Sphaerotheca, including ellipsoidal conidia with conspicuous fibrosin bodies, chained conidiogenesis, and Fibroidium-type lateral germination. Sequences were obtained for ITS, GAPDH, and RPB2. The concatenated ITS+GAPDH+RPB2 phylogeny resolved two major lineages corresponding to P. fragariae (95%) and P. shepherdiae (98%), placing the Peruvian isolate PUCP-Pa001 within the P. fragariae clade with high statistical support and close affinity to Eurasian accessions. These results provide the first multilocus evidence of P. fragariae on cultivated strawberry in the Americas and support the hypothesis of an anthropogenic introduction associated with the international movement of propagative material. Furthermore, the study demonstrates the value of multilocus approaches for resolving cryptic taxa within Erysiphaceae and provides the first South American reference sequences for this pathogen, supporting future epidemiological and phytosanitary research on powdery mildews associated with Fragaria in South America.

title: Systems biology prioritizes drug candidates for an interferon-response-high monocyte state in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus.
text: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is an age-associated neurological disorder characterized by gait disturbance, cognitive impairment, and urinary dysfunction. Although cerebrospinal fluid dynamics are central to its pathophysiology, the contribution of peripheral immune alterations remains poorly understood. We characterized an interferon-response-high monocyte state observed in iNPH and evaluated computational compound prioritization. We used a fixed set of marker criteria to characterize the IFN-response-high monocyte state. We then compared monocyte clusters 5 and 0 and used 150 upregulated and 150 downregulated genes to screen compounds in LINCS. We tested whether candidate rankings changed with different state definitions, comparison groups, gene-list sizes, clustering settings, and inclusion of all patients. We also repeated the queries after excluding each donor while retaining the original cell-state labels and compared the results with 100 expression-matched random gene signatures. External blood datasets and paired blood-ventricular CSF samples provided additional context. The marker rule classified 3,195 of 22,197 canonical monocytes as IFN-response-high. The cluster contrast identified 1,231 FDR-significant genes. Of 1,376 THP1 compounds, 138 met the operational criteria of normalized connectivity score (NCS) <-0.5 and WTCS FDR <0.05. Rosuvastatin and roflumilast ranked first and 14th in the primary screen and first and 15th in the integrated robustness ranking. Rosuvastatin met the operational criteria in all 11 core analyses; roflumilast did so in 10, returning NCS = 0 at resolution 0.7. Both met the criteria across all nine donor omissions. In exploratory comparisons performed after candidate selection, both observed scores were more negative than those from all 100 sampled expression-matched signatures. The blood-derived program was detectable in ventricular-CSF candidate monocytes, although unequal cell recovery limited inference about compartmental enrichment. This study characterizes an interferon-response-high classical-monocyte state observed within an iNPH cohort and nominates compounds with predicted inverse connectivity for experimental testing. Computational support was more consistent for rosuvastatin than for roflumilast. These findings support further investigation of peripheral innate immune states observed in an iNPH cohort and provide experimentally testable hypotheses for therapeutic repurposing.

title: Beyond the value of reproductive value.
text: Research Highlights: Lebreton, J.-D., & Oli, M. K. (2026). Reproductive value as a key concept in ecology and evolutionary biology. Journal of Animal Ecology. https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2656.70343. Ecologists are good at counting things. Yet individuals are not interchangeable in what they contribute to a population's future. Lebreton and Oli's synthesis of reproductive value (RV) shows that this deceptively simple idea connects demographic theory, life-history evolution, spatial ecology, epidemiology and conservation. Indeed, RV provides a common currency for asking not simply how many individuals occupy a population, but where its demographic future resides. Here, I highlight this unifying perspective and argue that new technologies could take RV from a predominantly class-based quantity towards a dynamic, individualised and spatially explicit description of populations. Combining demographic models with biologging, automated monitoring, genomic information and ecological digital twins could reveal reproductive value at resolutions Fisher himself could scarcely have imagined. I further suggest that RV could enrich community-stability theory by weighting species' fluctuations by their contribution to future population persistence, thereby connecting population resilience, biodiversity insurance and ecosystem stability.

title: Longevitomics as the Science of the Longevitome: Towards a Unified Systems Science of Healthy Longevity.
text: The twenty-first century has transformed longevity research through genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome science, digital phenotyping and artificial intelligence. Yet healthy longevity remains difficult to explain because its determinants are commonly studied as separate molecular layers, mechanisms or biomarkers. Here, we introduce Longevitomics as an integrative systems framework for understanding, modeling and predicting healthy longevity and define the Longevitome inspired by the Latin expression vita longa (long life) as the dynamic architecture of biological, environmental and behavioral determinants that collectively shape psychosomatic resilience across the life course. We position this proposal in relation to the Hallmarks of Aging, geroscience, biological-age biomarkers, multi-omics and systems medicine. Longevitomics is not intended to replace these established frameworks or to constitute another molecular "ome." Rather, it provides a systems-level framework in which mechanistic hallmarks, multi-omic layers, physiological phenotypes, exposures and adaptive responses can be integrated longitudinally. We further consider how network analysis, causal inference, machine learning and digital-twin approaches may enable reconstruction of individual Longevitome trajectories and support a transition toward predictive and personalized longevity medicine.

title: The road ahead for stem cell therapies in type 1 diabetes.
text: Type 1 diabetes results from autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells. Although exogenous insulin remains the standard treatment, it does not restore physiological glucose regulation. Differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells into β-cells offers a scalable alternative to cadaveric islet transplantation and has progressed rapidly over the past decade, resulting in nine clinical trials at various stages of completion. Despite this progress, durable graft function remains constrained by two major challenges: the absence of key islet microenvironment components, such as vasculature, extracellular matrix and supporting cell types and continued vulnerability to autoimmune and alloimmune rejection. This review considers emerging technological approaches to overcome these barriers. Bioengineered niches, including multilineage organoids, functionalized hydrogels, decellularized matrices and bioprinting, aim to recreate the native islet microenvironment, while synthetic biology approaches, such as hypoimmune gene editing, CRISPR-based transcriptional control and stimulus-responsive survival circuits, seek to enhance grafts' resilience. Computational and single-cell approaches, including gene regulatory network analysis and digital twin frameworks, are beginning to provide predictive tools for benchmarking differentiation quality and forecasting graft outcomes. Together, these complementary strategies, potentially tailored to individual patients, represent a realistic path towards safer, more effective and durable β-cell replacement therapies for type 1 diabetes.

title: Dual-feature selectivity enables bidirectional coding in visual cortical neurons.
text: Sensory neurons are traditionally viewed as feature detectors that respond with an increase in firing rate to preferred stimuli while remaining unresponsive to others. Here, we identify a dual-feature encoding strategy in macaque visual cortex, wherein many neurons in areas V1 and V4 are selectively tuned to two distinct visual features-one that enhances and one that suppresses activity-around an elevated baseline firing rate. By combining neuronal recordings with functional digital twin models-deep learning-based predictive models of biological neurons-we were able to systematically identify each neuron's preferred and non-preferred features. These feature pairs served as anchors for a continuous, low-dimensional axis in natural image similarity space, along which neuronal activity varied approximately linearly. Within a single visual area, visual features that strongly or weakly activated individual neurons also had a high probability of modulating the activity of other neurons, suggesting a shared feature selectivity across the population that structures stimulus encoding. We show that this encoding strategy is conserved across species, present in both primary and lateral visual areas of mouse cortex. Dual-feature selectivity is consistent with recent anatomical evidence for feature-specific inhibitory connectivity, complementing the feature-detector principle through circuit mechanisms in which selective excitation and inhibition may together enhance the representational capacity of the neuronal population.

title: Development of a Digital Twin to Analyse Waiting Lists in a Sleep-Disordered Breathing Unit.
text: This study developed and validated a digital twin of patient flow and waiting list dynamics in a Sleep-Disordered Breathing Unit, based on a discrete-event simulation (DES) model in the context of growing diagnostic demand mainly driven by obstructive sleep apnoea. The stochastic model, implemented in MATLAB, reproduces six care stages (e-Consultation, face-to-face consultation, overnight pulse oximetry, respiratory polygraphy, polysomnography and follow-up consultation), using operational data from year 2024 for parameterisation and data from year 2025 for correlation and validation. Key performance indicators included mean waiting time and mean queue length per stage, with model fidelity assessed via Mean Absolute Error, Root Mean Squared Error and Relative Percent Difference (RPD), both by stage and globally across the full patient pathway. The model accurately reproduced the aggregate system workload, with a weighted RPD of 3.6% for mean queue length and 34.6% for mean waiting time. Respiratory polygraphy showed the best agreement in terms of service load (RPD 2.7%), whereas the follow-up consultation exhibited the largest discrepancies in waiting times (RPD 73.7%), likely related to prioritisation rules and organisational variability not explicitly modelled. Overall, this digital twin provides an operationally useful representation to support 'what-if' analyses of organisational scenarios aimed at reducing diagnostic delays, representing one of the first validated applications of DES model in a dedicated Sleep-Disordered Breathing Unit and provides a basis for future applications incorporating urgency stratification and prospective analysis.

title: Gadoxetic acid in China: a narrative review of the 15-year journey and the road ahead.
text: Since its pivotal introduction in 2011, gadoxetic acid has fundamentally revolutionized the landscape of hepatobiliary imaging in China, shifting the diagnostic paradigm from morphological assessment toward functional hepatocyte-level evaluation. This review comprehensively summarizes its 15-year clinical evolution within the Chinese healthcare system, exploring its pharmacological benefits, advanced applications, and future integration with data-driven frameworks. A systematic literature search was conducted across major electronic databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure, spanning from 2011 to 2026. The search targeted peer-reviewed articles, consensus statements, clinical guidelines, and high-impact reviews published in English and Chinese regarding gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Gadoxetic acid provides high sensitivity for early small hepatocellular carcinoma (sHCC) detection via specific OATP1B3 uptake. Beyond lesion detection, its quantitative mapping shows potential for estimating hepatic functional reserve (HFR) and risk stratification for post-hepatectomy liver failure. Crucially, the ongoing paradigm shift toward integrating radiomics and deep learning bridges macroscopic imaging and microscopic molecular biology, theoretically enabling a multi-dimensional profile of liver parenchyma and lesions within a single diagnostic session. However, a significant gap remains between retrospective predictive performance and clinical readiness, and these data-driven frameworks currently serve as supplementary investigational engines rather than standalone clinical decision-makers. Moving forward, integrating these high-dimensional signatures into constructs such as "digital twin" represents the next frontier. Furthermore, China's hepatitis B virus-dominant epidemiological cohorts, comprehensive multi-modal datasets, "Med-Engineering" fusion, and collaborative networks uniquely accelerate the development and preliminary validation of these models, offering valuable insights for global precision hepatology within China's healthcare system. Over the past 15 years, gadoxetic acid has evolved far beyond a conventional liver imaging tool in China. While clinical translation of advanced analytics requires rigorous, prospective multicenter validation to ensure safety, combining this functional imaging agent with data-driven frameworks represents a promising frontier to eventually optimize future radiology workflows and support personalized precision hepatology.

title: Biological state-guided oncology: a framework for dynamic precision cancer care through oncological state transitions.
text: Precision oncology has transformed cancer treatment through molecular profiling, but clinical decisions remain largely anchored to baseline assessments that incompletely capture evolving tumor biology and host conditions. This review proposes the Oncological State Transition (OST) framework as a conceptual approach to cancer as a dynamic process of evolving tumor and host biological states. We examine the biological basis of state transitions and the potential roles of longitudinal liquid biopsy, multi-omics, functional imaging, digital pathology, artificial intelligence, and digital twins in multimodal state assessment. Potential applications across prevention, surgery, systemic therapy, minimal residual disease surveillance, therapeutic resistance, and survivorship are discussed, together with challenges in clinical validation and implementation. OST provides a testable framework for integrating longitudinal multimodal information to estimate current biological states and potential future transitions. It emphasizes probabilistic state estimation and the distinction between biological and actionable transitions. Rather than replacing conventional staging or molecular classification, OST may complement precision oncology by supporting dynamic state assessment and adaptive decision-making. Prospective studies and randomized comparisons are required to establish its clinical utility. OST therefore represents a potential foundation for Dynamic Precision Oncology, but remains a conceptual framework rather than a validated clinical system.

title: On-Chip Biomimetic Intelligence: Integrating Adaptive Molecular Sensing With Longitudinal Proteomic Profiling for Advanced Disease Diagnostics.
text: Biological, molecular, and functional states evolve across multiple timescales, limiting the utility of conventional diagnostics based on isolated measurements. This Perspective introduces on-chip biomimetic intelligence as an integrated approach combining biomimetic molecular recognition and signal transduction with dynamic sensing, adaptive local computation, and longitudinal interpretation of molecular changes. It focuses on multiplexed molecular-affinity measurements of selected disease-associated protein panels, coupled with event-driven signal processing to reduce redundant data generation. Where appropriate, sensing outputs may inform patient-specific digital twin models and dynamically update PBPK or PK-PD models. Rather than treating intelligent biosensors, neuromorphic biosensing, edge AI, and digital twins as isolated technologies, it integrates their functions and describes architectural and functional requirements for chip-level biomimetic intelligence. Implementation requires regenerable molecular-recognition interfaces, reliable molecular-to-signal transduction, and computational methods capable of estimating protein states and temporal trajectories. Causal validation and constrained closed-loop control may support clinically relevant decision-making when sufficient evidence is available. However, complete architecture has not yet been demonstrated as a single clinically validated system. Its realization requires advances in sensing stability, biocompatibility, antifouling performance, calibration, drift control, and clinical validation. Thus, biosensing shifts from static biomarker detection to longitudinal, adaptive, and clinically interpretable monitoring of changes in biological state.

title: Model systems and integration strategies to capture human biology.
text: Modelling human biology is difficult precisely because many of the responses that matter most emerge not within a single tissue or cell type, but at the boundaries where matrix, immune and systemic signals converge in ways that are hard to recreate in isolation. Conventional in vitro systems and animal studies have advanced our understanding of many physiological processes, but they still consistently fall short at these interfaces. In this Review, we discuss how engineered materials, organoids, microphysiological systems and computational models can be used together to build more informative human model systems. We first consider engineered materials as tools for controlling the local environment around cells, including matrix composition, stiffness, geometry, transport and time-dependent cues. We then examine organoids, assembloids and microphysiological system platforms, with emphasis on functional benchmarking, vascularization, immune integration, maturation, reproducibility and biological variation across donors and conditions. Finally, we discuss computational models, including spatial atlases, generative models and digital twins, as tools for organizing measurements, testing mechanisms and improving prediction. A key insight is that no current platform fully closes the loop between sensing, tissue modelling, computational calibration and feedback-guided intervention. The central challenge now is to build models whose complexity is justified by the human question they are designed to answer.

title: Computational Models of the Foreign Body Response: A Focus on Biomaterial Properties.
text: The foreign body response (FBR) is the main biological process governing the long-term performance and safety of implantable biomaterials. As the FBR is complex, multifactorial, and unfolds over extended time scales, making in vitro replication challenging, standard biological evaluation frameworks continue to rely primarily on in vivo testing In this context, computational modeling offers a promising strategy to improve the fundamental understanding of FBR mechanisms, support biomaterial design, and reduce dependency on animal experimentation. Existing approaches, including ordinary differential equation (ODE), partial differential equation (PDE), and agent-based (AB) models, have provided important insights into inflammatory signaling, macrophage dynamics, fibrosis progression, and capsule formation. However, most computational models still treat the FBR in a simplified way and rarely integrate material-dependent effects in a quantitative manner, despite the well-established role of surface chemistry, topography, stiffness, and other properties in shaping host responses. This review summarizes the current state of the art in computational models of the FBR, including both mechanistic and data-driven methods, with a particular focus on how material properties are represented. We discuss the main limitations of current modeling approaches as well as the scarcity of standardized experimental data suitable for calibration and validation, and highlight the need for closer interplay between hybrid predictive models and experimental data, with a digital twin (DT) of the FBR representing the ultimate objective of these efforts.

title: Patient-Informed Biomechanical Modeling Reveals Mechanical Mechanism of Brain Damage in Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus.
text: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is a globally growing neurological disorder in older adults that is radiologically characterized by enlargement of ventricles. However, it remains unknown whether ventricular enlargement can produce biomechanical loading large enough to drive brain morphological changes and tissue damage. Here, we develop an anatomically detailed biomechanical model of aging human brain and apply ventricular enlargement using a three-dimensional displacement field derived from MRI of iNPH patients and age-matched controls. The model accurately reproduces radiological markers of iNPH, including Evans index, callosal angle, and high-convexity sulcal narrowing. It further predicts large mechanical strains in the periventricular white matter, particularly within the corona radiata, corpus callosum, and anterior thalamic radiations, tracts consistently implicated in iNPH imaging abnormalities. These findings provide strong evidence that ventricular enlargement induces mechanical strain that contributes to iNPH brain abnormalities, which can potentially be reversed by reducing strain following shunting surgery. The biomechanical brain model forms the foundation of a predictive digital platform and future "digital twin" technology to support diagnosis, patient stratification, and treatment planning in iNPH.

title: A roadmap for quantifying metabolism in patients with cancer.
text: Advancements in in vivo stable isotope tracing have revolutionized our understanding of cancer metabolism, transitioning the field from static metabolomic snapshots to dynamic metabolic pathway activities. However, interpreting raw fractional enrichment data presents significant biological and analytical challenges. This review systematically examines the methodological landscape of in vivo tracing, addressing the interpretive gap created by clinical constraints, such as single-timepoint surgical sampling. We dissect how secondary circulating tracers and the inherent heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment can confound metabolic signals. We highlight the critical transition to metabolic flux analysis as the requisite computational step to overcome these challenges and to identify targetable metabolic vulnerabilities in precision oncology.

title: Theranostic Imaging Agents: Integrating Molecular Diagnostics, Precision Therapeutics, and Artificial Intelligence.
text: Theranostic imaging agents combine molecular diagnosis, targeted therapy and monitoring of treatment response into a single paradigm of precision medicine. This review summarizes the current development and translational landscape of theranostic imaging agents, covering molecular targets, imaging platforms, principles of agent design, nanotheranostics, radiotheranostics, and disease-specific applications. Particular emphasis is given to clinically validated and emerging targeting strategies using prostate-specific membrane antigen, somatostatin receptors, fibroblast activation protein, C-X-C Chemokine Receptor 4 (CXCR4), Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 (HER2) and other disease-associated biomarkers. Moreover, the review addresses Positron Emission Tomography (PET), Single-Photon Emission Computed Tomography (SPECT), Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), optical, photoacoustic, Raman and multimodal imaging approaches, therapeutic payloads, stimulus-responsive systems, and pharmacokinetic optimization. Moreover, emerging applications of artificial intelligence, radiomics, radiogenomics, spatial and single-cell multiomics, liquid biopsy, digital pathology, personalized dosimetry, and digital twins are evaluated for their potential to improve patient stratification, treatment selection, response assessment and adaptive therapy. Despite tremendous progress, clinical translation is hampered by target heterogeneity, off-target accumulation, radionuclide availability, manufacturing complexity, dosimetric uncertainty, regulatory requirements, limited clinical validation, data interoperability, cost and unequal access. This review, overall, emphasizes the convergence of molecular imaging, targeted therapeutics, nanotechnology, and artificial intelligence in the development of next-generation theranostic platforms, and outlines critical priorities for their clinical translation.

title: From Mechanistic Models to AI Synergy: A Roadmap for Predictive and Personalized Biology.
text: Two paradigms now drive the life sciences. One is the explanatory depth of mathematical modeling, the other the predictive power of artificial intelligence. For decades, mechanistic models have offered a rigorous, hypothesis-driven framework for dissecting biological processes, while AI has proven itself at finding patterns in the large, high-dimensional datasets of modern biology. Each has delivered major advances on its own. Together they promise a synthesis that could redefine the boundaries of biological inquiry. In this review we propose a three-part taxonomy of integration strategies, namely AI-accelerated mechanistic modeling, mechanism-informed AI, and hybrid models spanning one-directional sequential coupling and bidirectional iterative systems, and we survey their applications in systems and synthetic biology, pharmacology and drug discovery, epidemiology, and neuroscience. We then examine seven challenges that stand in the way: interpretability, data sparsity, causality, identifiability, computational scale, multimodal integration, and validation and generalization, and we close with a view of biological digital twins, causal discovery engines, and automated science. Our argument is that combining these approaches is the principal task for a new generation of interdisciplinary scientists who aim to build a predictive and mechanistic science of life.

title: Streamline CNV - A Handy Nextflow Pipeline for Chromosomal Copy Number Variation Analysis.
text: Aneuploidy, characterized by imbalanced chromosomal copy number variation (CNV), occurs in both normal somatic tissues and a wide range of diseases. Low pass whole genome sequencing (LP-WGS) to detect CNVs in cells and tissues has been widely used in all biological research. Existing informatics tools for detecting CNV often require computational expertise, often posing challenges for wet-lab biologists. To address this need, we developed Streamline CNV (SLCNV) - a user-friendly and flexible copy number analysis pipeline that allows researchers to perform many copy number-related analyses steps with a single, straightforward command. Streamline CNV is based on Nextflow and is packaged in a Docker image that can be executed using Singularity, making it portable and reproducible across different user environments. The pipeline automatically processes input data, performs sequencing quality control to filter problematic samples, outputs mapping statistics, CNV calling, and generates outputs including intuitive CNV plots, segmentation files (with statistics), annotation of genes on altered chromosomes, evaluation of proportion of chromosomal regions that are non-euploid. Based on user preferences, it can cluster samples solely based on CNV patterns, map the genomic location and density of genes of interest along chromosomes, and visually highlight regions with evident CNVs. In addition, it allows users to select and order chromosomes for display in plots, define sample label color palettes, and choose whether to include sample labels in the clustering visualizations. It also allows users to specify the amount of computing resources to allocate to the pipeline, such as CPU, memory, and runtime. Streamline CNV can be customizable and upgradable. It works with any species and genome assembly and efficiently supports both single-cell and bulk sequencing data with improved performance coding. Jobs can be distributed across cores of a basic Unix workstation, multiple nodes in a high-performance computing cluster using the Slurm scheduler, or cloud environments, as needed. We demonstrated the tool using an in-house sequencing dataset of human and mouse cell lines. Our results showed that the Streamline CNV pipeline effectively detected copy number patterns and generated informative summaries. It annotated the findings by identifying affected genes within the copy-number segments and at the break-end regions. It also reported the proportions of altered chromosomal regions impacted by copy number changes for each sample. The clustering plot demonstrated the relationships between samples based on their copy number profiles. Gene density plots aid in interpreting how genes from distinct pathways are associated with CNV pattern alterations. This tool enables researchers, regardless of bioinformatics expertise, to perform comprehensive CNV analyses across a wide range of scenarios. It also facilitates the interpretation of the copy number results and makes it possible for transforming raw CNV data into further exploration of meaningful biological insights.

title: Artificial intelligence apps for medical image analysis using pyCERR and cancer genomics cloud.
text: To provide a software resource that enables medical researchers and practitioners to develop and apply reproducible, out-of-the-box, AI-based analysis workflows for radiological and radiotherapy data. The framework comprises two main components: the Python-native computational environment for radiological research (pyCERR) for radiological image processing, and the cancer genomics cloud (CGC), a National Cancer Institute-funded resource that supports cloud-hosted collaborative projects, with tools for managing collaborators and compute-hardware from providers such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud Platform. pyCERR is open-source (GNU GPL) and distributed at https://github.com/cerr/pycerr; it provides user-friendly data structures, simplified access to metadata across radiological imaging modalities, and tools for data transformation, AI-based image segmentation, radiomics, dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI analysis, radiotherapy dose-volume histogram (DVH) feature extraction, and normal-tissue complication and tumor-control models. Radiomics features comply with the Image biomarker standardization initiative (IBSI) standards and are validated against published reference values. Unit tests covering data input/output, radiomics, DVH features, and visualization run on every code update. Workflows are containerized for reproducible, identical execution on the CGC and on local hardware. The CGC enables AI inference from radiological images to be combined with other data types such as genomics and proteomics. Our public CGC project (https://cgc.sbgenomics.com/u/sevenbridges/pycerr-radiological-radiotherapy-imageanalysis), accessible with free registration, currently includes apps for organ-at-risk (OAR) and lung-nodule segmentation based on published models trained in-house and clinically validated. These apps can be run interactively from a web browser or programmatically via a REST API with client support for multiple programming languages. Notebooks demonstrating the CGC API and pyCERR capabilities are provided at https://github.com/cerr/pycerr-notebooks. The framework facilitates end-to-end radiological image analysis and reproducible research, including data access from public and private repositories, training and inference with AI models, and utilities for data management, visualization, and simplified access to image metadata.

title: The LiCO platform: A novel benzimidazole-based lipid conjugate for versatile and sustained siRNA delivery beyond the liver.
text: Extending oligonucleotide therapeutics beyond the liver remains a central challenge for RNA medicine. Here, we describe a lipid-conjugated oligonucleotide (LiCO), a benzimidazole-enabled lipid-duplex RNA conjugate platform synthesized as a single chemical entity by standard solid-phase chemistry. Structure-activity screening identified a 5'-passenger-strand hexadecyl (C16) conjugate whose benzimidazole (SDL) linker markedly improved delivery activity relative to a linker-free analog, and studies in CD36-knockout mice established CD36-dependent uptake as the principal driver of extrahepatic tropism. A single systemic dose in mice produced >90% target knockdown in skeletal muscle, heart, aorta, and adipose tissue, with ≥50% silencing persisting for 6 months and measurable activity at 9 months, whereas hepatic silencing was transient. In cynomolgus macaques, two intravenous doses of LiCO-siMSTN achieved ∼90% myostatin mRNA knockdown, 60%-70% suppression of circulating myostatin protein through day 98, and progressive muscle hypertrophy without adverse clinical, hematological, or biochemical findings. In situ hybridization confirmed deep penetration of myofibers, myocardium, and aortic smooth muscle. LiCO also enabled potent local delivery to the synovium, retina, and bladder with minimal systemic exposure. LiCO offers a scalable, versatile platform for neuromuscular, metabolic, and localized disorders.

title: Messenger RNA vaccines and beyond: Molecular design, delivery platforms, and emerging therapeutic applications.
text: Messenger RNA (mRNA) medicine has progressed from a conceptual nucleic acid modality to a clinically validated platform for transient protein expression, with SARS-CoV-2 vaccines providing population-scale proof of maturity. This review synthesizes the molecular and translational principles underlying this transition, emphasizing two determinants of mRNA performance: transcript engineering and delivery formulation. Transcript engineering integrates cap structure, untranslated regions, coding-sequence optimization, nucleoside chemistry, and poly(A) design, whereas formulation controls encapsulation, tissue tropism, cytosolic release, stability, and route-dependent biodistribution. We examine how this platform logic extends beyond vaccination to protein replacement, lung-directed gene complementation, regenerative signaling, in vivo antibody production, local tumor immunomodulation, genome editing, and transient ex vivo cell engineering. We also compare conventional mRNA, self-amplifying RNA, and circular RNA as complementary architectures with distinct dose requirements, expression durability, immunogenicity, and manufacturability. Across preventive and therapeutic settings, translation is constrained by extrahepatic delivery specificity, productive endosomal escape, innate and carrier-driven immune responses during repeat dosing, and scalable manufacturing with robust analytical quality control. The future of mRNA medicine will depend on platform matching: aligning RNA architecture, formulation, administration route, and disease context with clinical settings in which transient expression offers a genuine therapeutic advantage.

title: Programmable RNA therapeutics: converging vaccination and on-demand disease treatment via self-adaptive RNA platforms.
text: RNA technology, most prominently messenger RNA (mRNA), has transformed vaccine development by enabling rapid, sequence-specific antigen design, scalable manufacturing, and transient protein expression. Its long-term significance, however, extends beyond prophylactic vaccination. This Perspective argues that mRNA should be conceptualised as a programmable therapeutic platform capable of integrating vaccination, immune modulation, and on-demand disease treatment. Current mRNA vaccines deliver predefined antigenic instructions, whereas emerging RNA systems, including self-amplifying RNA (saRNA), circular RNA, sequence-engineered mRNA, and targeted lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), may support more adaptable therapeutic functions. Such platforms could prime immunity, replace deficient proteins, encode antibodies, reprogramme immune cells, or induce antigen-specific tolerance. The concept of self-adaptive RNA-based therapeutics remains at an early stage and should not be overstated; most existing systems are programmable at the design stage rather than biologically autonomous after administration. Nonetheless, this conceptual position is no longer purely speculative: the first regulatory approval of a self-amplifying RNA vaccine and controlled-trial evidence of clinical benefit from a personalised neoantigen mRNA therapeutic in resected melanoma indicate that programmable RNA platforms are beginning to move from concept to clinical validation across both the prophylactic and therapeutic ends of the spectrum. Key challenges include tissue-specific delivery, expression control, innate immune activation, repeat dosing, safety assessment, regulatory classification, and equitable access. A self-adaptive RNA-based framework does not replace existing vaccines or biologics but extends them towards responsive, personalised, and temporally controlled therapy.

title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Pentacyclic Triterpene Derivatives as Intestinal FXR Antagonists for Type 2 Diabetes.
text: Intestinal farnesoid X receptor (FXR) antagonism has emerged as a strategy to enhance endogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) secretion and improve metabolic control in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Dihydrooleanolic acid methyl ester (DKS26) served as the scaffold for the synthesis of 64 pentacyclic triterpene derivatives modified at the terminal carboxyl group and C-3/C-12 positions. Esterification of the terminal carboxylate emerged as a determinant of FXR antagonism, identifying 4l bearing a tetrazole-containing side chain and C-12 hydroxyl motif. Compound 4l antagonized FXR in a TR-FRET assay (IC50 = 11.79 μM), a fivefold improvement over DKS26. In NCI-H716 cells, 4l reduced NR0B2 (SHP) mRNA expression and markedly stimulated GLP-1 secretion. In HFD/STZ-induced diabetic mice, oral 4l improved glycemia, increased circulating GLP-1 and insulin, and alleviated dyslipidemia and organ injury markers. These findings establish the pentacyclic triterpene scaffold as a platform for FXR antagonism and identify 4l as a lead for further optimization.

title: Allogeneic CAR-T, CAR-NK, and in vivo CAR-T for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases: comparative evidence, platform trade-offs, and translational challenges.
text: Immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) remain treatment-dependent in many patients with severe, refractory, or organ-threatening disease. Deep B-cell depletion using chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-based therapies may induce clinical improvement and measurable immune reconstitution, but conventional autologous CAR-T manufacturing limits speed, standardization, and access. This structured narrative review compares allogeneic CAR-T, allogeneic CAR-natural killer (CAR-NK), and in vivo CAR-T. Bibliographic databases, trial registries, conference repositories, reference lists, and traceable sponsor, media, and regulatory sources were searched through 3 September 2026. Allogeneic CAR-T has the broadest clinical evidence base, although cohorts are small and mostly early-phase. All CAR-NK products with reported IMID clinical data are allogeneic; available studies suggest transient kinetics, repeat-infusion feasibility, and encouraging short-term tolerability, but durability is uncertain. Peer-reviewed in vivo evidence now includes a five-patient non-integrating LNP/linear mRNA report and a 16-patient integrating lentiviral report. Both are early, uncontrolled studies and neither supports class-wide inference. Disease-specific outcomes, background treatment, follow-up, and assays differ markedly. Complete treatment-free remission was distinguished from glucocorticoid withdrawal, immunosuppressant reduction, and remission on permitted therapy. CAR-cell, transgene DNA, and RNA detection were not pooled, and peripheral blood B-cell depletion was not treated as proof of tissue depletion. Naive-dominant B-cell recovery and declining autoantibodies indicate immune remodeling, not restored tolerance. No indirect efficacy ranking is justified. Prospective studies need standardized disease endpoints, treatment-free remission definitions, analyte-specific pharmacokinetics, paired blood-tissue pharmacodynamics, and long-term genomic, immune, and safety surveillance.

title: Fusion-independent virus-like particles enable rapid detection of antibody-mediated inhibition of ligand-receptor interactions.
text: Studying antibody-mediated inhibition of ligand-receptor interactions is critical for understanding fundamental biological processes and developing therapeutic interventions. However, for high-consequence viruses with entry machinery involving multiple viral proteins, it is often difficult to develop pseudotyped viruses that can infect susceptible host cells. Here, we report a rapid platform for detecting antibody-mediated inhibition of ligand-receptor interactions by decoupling viral attachment from post-entry membrane fusion and gene expression. Our platform leverages HIV Gag-based self-assembling virus-like particles (VLPs) where Gag is fused with GFP and further pseudotyped with selected ligands for easy readout of VLP binding to susceptible cells. We first validated the platform's stringent cell-type specificity using broadly tropic VSV-G and CD19-specific single chain fragment variable (scFv) pseudotypes. Next, we applied this technology to African swine fever virus (ASFV) - a high-consequence agricultural pathogen lacking surrogate neutralization assays due to its multi-protein entry machinery. By screening VLPs pseudotyped with different viral proteins against diverse mammalian cell lines, we found that VLP pseudotyped with ASFV CD2v binds specifically to Vero cells. Leveraging this interaction, we developed a rapid test for detecting antibodies that inhibit CD2v-pseudotyped VLP binding to Vero cells. Longitudinal analysis of sera from mRNA-LNP vaccinated pigs showed that the degrees of VLP-based binding-inhibition strongly correlated with the levels of anti-CD2v IgG, validating the assay's utility. Overall, the pseudotyped VLP platform provides an enabling tool for ligand-receptor discovery, vaccine evaluation, and disease surveillance for select agents.

title: A field-deployable colorimetric reverse transcription-LAMP assay for the detection of a prostate cancer biomarker.
text: Prostate cancer (PCa) is becoming increasingly common in males worldwide, and early identification is crucial for improved patient prognosis and therapeutic results. Messenger ribonucleic acids (mRNAs) are promising noninvasive biomarkers for PCa diagnosis because they can be extracted from various body fluids. Yes-Associated Protein 1 (YAP1) mRNA is a biomarker for PCa diagnosis and is highly expressed in human PCa cells. Herein, the ability of RT-LAMP and a visual platform to detect YAP1 mRNA for PCa diagnosis was explored. For the first time, the color behavior of a charge-transfer complex (oxTMB) was investigated to detect a PCa biomarker. Due to the electrostatic interactions between the positively-charged oxTMB and the negatively-charged LAMP amplicons, oxTMB was not reduced even when the potential reductant, dopamine (DA), was added. Consequently, the green color of oxTMB was retained under electrostatic interactions, whereas oxTMB in the negative sample was reduced, and the green color disappeared. The introduced oxTMB/DA-based LAMP approach showed high selectivity and a visual limit of detection of the PCa biomarker at 3.64 × 104 copies/μL in a cultured DU-145 cell line-derived RNA sample. Owing to its simplicity, rapidity, and practical viability, this oxTMB/DA-based colorimetric approach could be employed to detect PCa biomarkers in resource-limited areas.

title: Effects of COVID-19 vaccination type and vaccination-infection interval on viral clearance dynamics in Omicron BA.5 patients at Guangzhou Fangcang shelter hospitals: A propensity score matched multicenter retrospective cohort study.
text: The Omicron BA.5 subvariant exhibited pronounced immune evasion and was associated with widespread breakthrough infections. Unlike settings where mRNA vaccines predominated, China mainly used inactivated vaccines, with the adenovirus type 5-vectored vaccine Ad5-nCoV also administered at scale. Real-world evidence on post-infection viral clearance associated with these platforms remains limited. This multicenter retrospective cohort study enrolled 16,533 mild or asymptomatic Omicron BA.5 cases from two Fangcang shelter hospitals in Guangzhou, China, from Novernber 5 to December 8, 2022. The primary objective was to compare viral-clearance time between unvaccinated and vaccinated participants. The secondary objective was to compare inactivated-vaccine recipients, or and Ad5-nCoV recipients, containing regimens in a propensity score-matched cohort; the last-dose-to-infection interval analysis was exploratory. Propensity score matching was performed using age, sex, marital status, occupation, and province as covariates to improve between-group comparability. All patients underwent standardized daily RT-PCR testing containing both N and ORF1ab genes, with Ct values > 35 defined as negative. The outcome was time to viral clearance, defined as two consecutive negative nasopharyngeal swabs ≥ 24 hours apart. In the overall cohort, vaccinated patients had significantly shorter shedding duration (9.05 vs… 10.42d; P < .001) compared with unvaccinated patients. The matched cohort included 228 unvaccinated, 228 inactivated vaccine recipients, and 114 Ad5-nCoV recipients. Median time to viral clearance differed across groups with 9.42, 8.56, and 8.48d, respectively. Prior vaccination was associated with shorter viral clearance but with no significant difference observed between inactivated vaccine and Ad5-nCoV recipients among the matched regimens.

title: Therapeutic and Prophylactic Agents for Viral Diseases: Current Status, Challenges, and Future Prospects.
text: Viral diseases remain a major global health challenge despite substantial advances in vaccination, antiviral therapeutics, and public-health interventions. However, current antiviral strategies are still constrained by important gaps, including rapid viral evolution, limited broad-spectrum efficacy, immune escape, antiviral resistance, incomplete durability of protection, and inequitable global access to prevention and treatment. This review provides a comprehensive and integrated overview of contemporary antiviral prevention and therapeutic strategies, spanning vaccines, monoclonal antibodies, direct-acting antivirals, host-targeted therapies, immunomodulators, RNA-based therapeutics, gene-editing technologies, and cellular immunotherapies. We discuss the mechanistic foundations, clinical applications, pharmacologic considerations, and translational challenges associated with each modality across major human viral pathogens, including HIV, HBV, HCV, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, RSV, Ebola virus, arboviruses, and herpesviruses. Particular emphasis is placed on emerging innovations such as long-acting prophylaxis, Fc-engineered monoclonal antibodies, nanoparticle and mucosal vaccine platforms, CRISPR-based antiviral systems, and broadly protective host-directed approaches designed to overcome resistance and enhance pandemic preparedness. In addition, we highlight the growing importance of real-time genomic surveillance and equitable global deployment strategies in shaping future antiviral responses, collectively underscoring that the next generation of antiviral medicine will depend on the convergence of universal immunization strategies, durable therapeutics, precision immune modulation, and rapidly deployable platform technologies capable of addressing both endemic and emerging viral threats.

title: Nanocarrier-Mediated Immunotherapy for Gynecological Malignancies: Mechanisms, Clinical Translation, and Emerging Nucleic Acid-Based Strategies.
text: Gynecological cancers, including ovarian, cervical, and endometrial cancers, remain major contributors to female morbidity and mortality worldwide. Conventional treatments-surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy-have improved outcomes, but advanced or recurrent disease is still associated with poor prognosis, chemoresistance, and tumor heterogeneity. Immunotherapy has emerged as a transformative strategy because of its specificity and potential for durable responses. However, the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and inefficient delivery of immunotherapeutic agents limit clinical benefit. Nanocarriers, including organic, inorganic, and biomimetic platforms, can improve targeted delivery, sustained release, biocompatibility, and tumor microenvironment remodeling, thereby enhancing immunotherapy. This review summarizes major immunotherapeutic modalities for gynecological cancers-immune checkpoint blockade, CAR-T cell therapy, tumor vaccines, and oncolytic viruses-and the classification and characteristics of commonly used nanocarriers. We focus on nanocarrier-mediated immunotherapeutic mechanisms in ovarian, cervical, and endometrial cancers, and further highlight emerging lipid nanoparticle/mRNA and programmable RNA delivery strategies. Finally, we analyze challenges in clinical translation and provide perspectives for future development, aiming to support fundamental research and clinical application of nano-immunotherapy in gynecological malignancies. Gynecological cancers are difficult to treat when they are advanced or come back after treatment. Immunotherapy can help the immune system find and attack cancer cells, but current immunotherapies often do not reach tumors well, and the tumor environment can suppress immune responses. Nanocarriers are tiny delivery systems that can carry immunotherapy drugs to tumors more precisely, protect the drugs from being cleared too quickly, and release them in a controlled way. This review explains how different nanocarriers—such as liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, inorganic nanoparticles, cell membrane-coated nanoparticles, virus-like particles, and exosomes—can support immunotherapy for ovarian, cervical, and endometrial cancers. We also discuss new approaches such as lipid nanoparticles and mRNA vaccines. These strategies may make immunotherapy safer, more effective, and more personalized. However, more work is needed to improve targeting, reduce long-term toxicity, scale up production, and meet regulatory requirements before these treatments can reach patients.

title: Mechanism-driven nano-therapeutic platform integrating plant-derived compounds and membrane-active peptides reprograms inflammatory, cell cycle arrest, cGAS-STING, and apoptotic gene expression to quench colorectal cancer.
text: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and its first-line chemotherapeutic, 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), is constrained by poor tumor selectivity, dose-limiting systemic toxicity, and the frequent emergence of drug resistance. Nanocarrier-based co-delivery of naturally derived, multi-targeted agents offers a promising strategy to enhance efficacy while limiting off-target harm. This study evaluated the antitumor effects of nanoformulated liposomal melittin peptides (LIP-MLT) and niosomal chrysin (NsCR), administered as monotherapy or as combined therapy (LIP-MLT/NsCR), against DMH-induced CRC in a rat model. CRC was induced by subcutaneous injection of DMH (1,2-dimethylhydrazine, 40 mg/kg, twice weekly) for 8 weeks. Sprague-Dawley rats (n = 120) were randomly divided into six groups: healthy control (CON); untreated colorectal tumour (CR-TUM); and DMH-induced rats treated with 5-fluorouracil (CR-TUM + FU5), liposomal melittin (CR-TUM + LIP-MLT), niosomal chrysin (CR-TUM + NsCR), or the combination (CR-TUM + LIP-MLT/NsCR). Oxidant/antioxidant status, inflammatory cytokines, and the transcriptional profiles of inflammatory, cell-cycle-arrest, apoptotic/antiapoptotic, cGAS-STING innate-sensing, mTOR, and angiogenesis/metastasis genes were assessed, together with histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation. The untreated CR-TUM group showed pronounced tumor-markers elevation, anemia, oxidative damage, and a strong pro-inflammatory, immunosuppressive shift. Relative to CR-TUM, LIP-MLT/NsCR lowered the tumor markers CEA (3.1-fold), CA19-9 (3.5-fold), and CCSA (2.1-fold), and reduced the oxidative markers ROS (2.2-fold), MDA (1.8-fold), and NO (2.2-fold) while raising the antioxidants. It also decreased the pro-inflammatory mediators NF-κB (2.3-fold), IL-1β (2.4-fold), and TNF-α (1.7-fold) versus CR-TUM, reversing approximately 71% of the DMH-induced inflammatory signature. At the transcriptional level, the combination produced the strongest upregulation of the pro-apoptotic genes (Caspase-3, Caspase-8, BAX, and p53) with concurrent downregulation of the antiapoptotic mediators (Bcl-2, c-FLIP, and Survivin), and marked proliferative and metastatic drivers suppression, including CDK4, CDK6, cyclin D1, β-catenin, mTOR, MMP-9, and VEGF, alongside restoration of the CDK inhibitors p21, p27, and KLF4 and normalization of cGAS, STING, and IRF3 mRNA levels. LIP-MLT/NsCR further best-preserved body weight and colon length, lowered diarrhea and rectal-bleeding scores, restored colonic histopathological architecture, and most strongly diminished the immunoexpression of MMP-9 and VEGF relative to untreated cancer tissues. Taken together, the combined LIP-MLT/NsCR nanoformulation attenuated DMH-induced CRC progression to a greater extent than either monotherapy or conventional 5-FU, supporting the combined melittin-chrysin nanoformulation as a promising, multi-targeted strategy against colorectal cancer.

title: BIOREDIS: an integrated platform for end-to-end design of nucleic acid therapeutics.
text: Developing state-of-the-art RNA- and DNA-based therapeutics requires advanced computational frameworks that support the entire workflow - from biological rationale to the final drug construct - enabling tissue- and cell-specific targeting with high precision. Existing bioinformatics tools provide only partial solutions and rarely generate designs directly suitable for synthesis or preclinical evaluation. To address these limitations, we present BIOREDIS, a web-based platform for comprehensive nucleic acid therapeutic design. BIOREDIS integrates curated data from nine major biological resources and incorporates modules for coding sequence optimization, RNA interference (shRNA/siRNA) design, promoter/UTR selection, and automated construction of viral (AAV, lentiviral), non-viral, and mRNA vaccine vectors. The platform supports designs for human, mouse, and rat, with tissue-specific promoter recommendations available for human and mouse, and advanced cell-expression profiling natively restricted to human. BIOREDIS demonstrates competitive performance in coding sequence optimization and RNAi prediction, while uniquely providing an end-to-end workflow from target selection to fully specified next-generation DNA or RNA therapeutic constructs ready for synthesis and experimental validation. BIOREDIS is freely available at https://rnadrug.ichb.pl/bioredis, with a mirror site at https://bioredis.cs.put.poznan.pl. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: Selective ORgan-targeting lipid nanoparticles deliver SMAD7 mRNA to fibrotic lungs and attenuate pulmonary fibrosis.
text: Fibroblast activation and differentiation into myofibroblasts drive excessive extracellular matrix deposition and irreversible scarring in pulmonary fibrosis, such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), underscoring the need for therapies that directly target fibroblast activation. Here, we apply engineered lung-targeting Selective ORgan-Targeting (SORT) lipid nanoparticles for intravenous RNA delivery to fibrotic lungs. In a preclinical model of pulmonary fibrosis, engineered SORT LNPs achieved functional mRNA delivery in approximately 20% of CD45-CD31-EpCAM-Thy1.2+ mesenchymal cells in fibrotic lungs. Mechanistic studies further supported a contributory role of the vitronectin (Vtn)/vitronectin receptor (VtnR) axis in 1A7B13 Lung SORT LNP uptake. Therapeutic delivery of SMAD7 mRNA inhibited fibroblast activation in human lung fibroblast cultures and attenuated pulmonary fibrosis in vivo, resulting in an approximately 40% reduction in histological collagen deposition and a significant reduction in lung hydroxyproline content. Together, these findings establish engineered lung-enriched SORT LNPs as a platform for systemic RNA delivery to fibrotic lungs, including disease-relevant mesenchymal populations, and demonstrate their potential for RNA-based anti-fibrotic therapy.

title: Skin barrier and beyond: From structural blueprint to rational skin-targeted therapeutics.
text: The cutaneous interface represents a sophisticated biophysical barrier, governed by the complex lamellar organization of stratum corneum (SC) lipids. Traditionally viewed through the lens of static Brick and Mortar analogies, modern insights derived from molecular dynamics and cryo-electron microscopy have redefined the SC as a dynamic, tunable system. This review explores the evolutionary trajectory of barrier modeling from the Domain Mosaic to the Sandwich Model and highlights the critical role of ceramide stoichiometry and acyl-chain distribution in maintaining homeostatic integrity. We examine how these biophysical blueprints have catalyzed the development of next-generation transdermal delivery platforms, including ultra-flexible ethosomes, invasomes, and functionalized nanocarriers designed for targeted nucleic acid (mRNA/siRNA) delivery. By integrating surface modifications, such as mannosylated chitosan, with physical enhancement strategies like microneedle arrays, researchers are overcoming historical permeability constraints. Furthermore, the clinical paradigm is shifting toward barrier-targeted interventions that not only bypass but actively repair the SC matrix in chronic inflammatory conditions like atopic dermatitis. Ultimately, this synthesis underscores the transition of skin-targeted therapeutics from empirical formulation toward rational, biophysically-driven design, offering transformative potential for both localized dermatological therapy and non-invasive systemic immunization.

title: Spray-Dried mRNA-LNP Powder Enabling Multi-Route Delivery With 3-Year Refrigerated Stability.
text: The clinical translation of mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) therapeutics is constrained by limited stability of liquid formulations, necessitating ultra-cold storage and restricting global accessibility. Here, we report a spray-dried dry powder platform for mRNA-LNPs that overcomes these limitations while enabling flexible routes of administration. Systematic evaluation of pharmaceutically relevant sugars identifies trehalose as an optimal matrix former, yielding high-recovery mRNA-LNP dry powder product (DPP) with controlled particle size, low residual moisture, and preserved LNP physicochemical properties upon reconstitution. Mechanistic studies combining solid-state characterization, fluorescence tracking, and solvent extraction demonstrate that mRNA-LNPs are entrapped within an amorphous trehalose matrix core, providing protection against dehydration and rehydration stress. Reconstituted DPP (RDPP) maintains in vivo protein expression comparable to liquid control (LC) following intravenous and intramuscular administration, while supporting effective mucosal delivery via pulmonary and sublingual routes. Direct administration of DPP without reconstitution enables lung-targeted protein expression, highlighting potential for cold-chain-independent therapies. Critically, DPP preserves colloidal stability, mRNA integrity, ionizable lipid stability, and biological activity for over 3 years under refrigerated conditions, whereas liquid formulation exhibits substantial degradation within 6-9 months. These findings establish spray-dried mRNA-LNP DPPs as a robust platform integrating long-term stability with multi-route delivery for improved accessibility of mRNA therapeutics.

title: Cellulase catalysis on cell surfaces using Caulobacter S-layer display.
text: Sustainable bioprocesses for energy and materials production and waste resource recovery are needed to support circular economic development. Enzyme surface display on cells or functionalized materials has emerged as a promising paradigm for sustainable bioprocess innovation. Surface (S)-layers are geometric, often monomolecular, highly stable crystalline protein lattices encasing the outside of many bacteria and archaea. Several S-layer genes have been shown to tolerate heterologous insertions, thereby enabling high-density display of peptides of interest on cell surfaces without additional costly immobilization or conjugation steps. Here, we employ an S-layer display platform in Caulobacter vibrioides CB2A JS4038 to express functional cellulases up to 445 amino acids in length. We explore critical design considerations needed for successful catalytic display and demonstrate synergistic activities between differentially expressed cellulases relevant to combinatorial lignocellulosic biomass conversion. Functionalized S-layers could have useful applications in engineering whole-cell biocatalysts and synthetic microbial consortia tuned for different bioprocess applications.
