title: CDH1 loss remodels gene expression and lineage identity in human mammary epithelial cells
text: Invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) is a common subtype of breast cancer, molecularly defined by genetic loss of CDH1, and subsequent loss of cell adhesion protein E-cadherin, in ~95% of ILC. Though CDH1 loss occurs early in ILC oncogenesis, it is unclear how this facilitates transformation. We modeled early CDH1 loss using "normal" human mammary epithelial cells (HMEC), i.e., finite lifespan cells reflecting early hyperplasia, and targeted E-cadherin signaling using antibodies versus causing genetic CDH1 loss using siRNA or CRISPR/Cas9-knockout. Transcriptome analysis across four HMEC models showed that the mode of E-cadherin targeting is critical for the subsequent phenotype. Antibody-mediated inhibition of cell-cell contacts induced gene signatures of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), consistent with the role of E-cadherin suppression during the EMT process. Conversely, genetic CDH1 loss - as in ILC oncogenesis - repressed EMT signatures, and instead remodeled gene expression toward a luminal epithelial phenotype. RNA-seq, single cell transcriptomics, flow cytometry, microscopy, and ATAC-seq analyses support that CDH1 loss induces lineage remodeling to a luminal state, which is mirrored in transcriptomic analysis of clinical ILC precursor lesions. By isolating luminal versus basal cells prior to CDH1 knockout, we found that CDH1 loss led to remodeling of lineage identity in both populations, converging on a new lineage homeostasis with a luminal progenitor-like phenotype. Consistent with the shift to a luminal progenitor phenotype, CDH1 loss enhanced proliferative capacity over the finite lifespan of the HMECs, highlighting a feature of early CDH1 loss that may contribute to clonal advantage during tumor initiation. Moreover, CDH1 loss enhanced anoikis resistance, a defining feature of ILC cells. Our findings support that genetic loss of CDH1 in mammary epithelial cells induces transcriptional and phenotypic changes consistent with lineage identity remodeling toward a luminal progenitor-like state, which may underpin the mechanism by which early CDH1 loss mediates ILC oncogenesis.

title: Programmable and selective silencing of oncogenic fusion transcripts by CRISPR-Cas13b via breakpoint sequence recognition
text: Oncogenic gene fusions are key drivers of cancer, yet most remain undruggable by current therapies. Here, we establish CRISPR- Psp Cas13b as a personalizable platform for systematic silencing of various fusion transcripts. We reveal that recognition and cleavage of the breakpoint sequence by Psp Cas13b disrupt the fusion transcript, resulting in efficient protein depletion. Psp Cas13b cleavage produces aberrant, translation-incompetent target RNA species, a subset of which harbors internal deletions proximal to the cleavage site. We demonstrate that targeting the BCR::ABL1 breakpoint sequence efficiently degrades both wild-type and drug-resistant BCR::ABL1 mutants, which are the primary drivers of tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance and relapse in chronic myeloid leukemia. Molecular profiling revealed that Psp Cas13b impairs BCR::ABL1 tyrosine phosphokinase activity and triggers extensive transcriptomic and proteomic remodeling, leading to erythroid differentiation and apoptosis in drug-resistant cells. Beyond BCR::ABL1, personalized design of Psp Cas13b effectively silences other undruggable oncogenic fusions. Collectively, this study establishes a molecular framework for precise targeting of undruggable or drug-resistant oncogenic transcripts.

title: Elucidating cancer cachexia–mediated aberrant cardiac wasting signaling in human iPSC-derived cardiac muscle
text: Cancer cachexia is a debilitating syndrome of involuntary body mass loss featuring profound skeletal muscle wasting and high mortality. Cardiac muscle wasting is prominent in cancer patients and cancer survivors. We developed a human induced pluripotent stem cell–derived cardiac myocyte (hiPSC-CM) platform modeling cancer cachexia using conditioned media and Transwell coculture with C26 or HCT116 tumor cells. Cachectic hiPSC-CMs exhibited atrophy, reduced contraction amplitude, prolonged relaxation time, and elevated oxygen consumption rate, reflecting wasting, contractile dysfunction, and metabolic dysregulation. Mechanistically, suppression of the AKT/mTORC1/S6 signaling axis notably reduced total and p-AKT, decreased the p-S6/S6 ratio, and downregulated RPTOR , which coincided with FOXO1/3 activation and FOXO1 nuclear translocation, promoting downstream atrophic remodeling. Concurrently, Atrogin-1 upregulation reduced calcineurin A, impairing NFAT nuclear translocation, thereby suppressing downstream growth signaling. Increased autophagic flux with an elevated LC3BII/LC3BI ratio accompanied these changes. Following withdrawal of cachexia-inducing stimuli, Atrogin-1 and autophagy markers normalized within 1 week; however, contractile and metabolic impairments persisted, indicating delayed functional recovery. These findings establish the FOXO/Atrogin-1/calcineurin A/NFAT axis, operating within the broader context of AKT/mTORC1 suppression, as a central regulatory mechanism of cachexia-induced cardiac wasting, unveiling a tractable therapeutic target.

title: An aging-sensitive secreted phospholipase confers neuroprotection and cognitive resilience
text: Cognitive reserve theory posits that compensatory mechanisms during aging stave off cognitive decline and lower risk for Alzheimer's disease. Here, in a screen for hippocampal dentate granule cell (DGC) synapse loss-induced factors in mice, we identified a secreted phospholipase, Pla2g2f, whose expression increases in DGCs during aging and is associated with cognitive resilience in humans. Pla2g2f deletion in DGCs exacerbates aging-associated pathophysiological changes, including synapse loss, inflammatory microglia, reactive astrogliosis, impaired neurogenesis, lipid dysregulation, lipid droplet accumulation and hippocampal-dependent memory loss. Conversely, boosting Pla2g2f in DGCs during aging is sufficient to prevent these pathophysiological alterations in hippocampal-cortical circuits, protect memory and prophylactically modify trajectory of cognitive decline. Mutagenesis of the catalytic site of PLA2G2F prevented lipid droplet mobilization and reduction of reactive gliosis and inflammatory microglia. Neuronal PLA2G2F mediates intercellular signaling to decrease lipid droplet and cholesterol ester load in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia. Our findings implicate PLA2G2F as a compensatory neuroprotective broadcast signal that maintains lipid homeostasis to counteract aging-associated cognitive decline.

title: Continuous directed evolution using engineered human B cell lines
text: Abstract The B cells of the human immune system have evolved somatic hypermutation (SHM) mechanisms that introduce mutations at the immunoglobulin genomic loci at a significantly higher frequency than the rest of the genome thereby allowing them to evolve antibody sequences without compromising fitness due to genome-wide mutations. Inspired by these observations, here we develop a continuous directed evolution platform in human B cell lines (CODE-HB) that repurposes the SHM mechanisms to a stable, non-immunoglobulin genomic locus of the human B cell lines to continuously evolve cytosolic and surface displayed proteins with a broad mutational spectrum comprising of substitutions, deletions and insertions. Using our human B cell surface display platform and CODE-HB, we evolve neutralizing antibodies targeting avian influenza and escape variants of influenza. Given the modularity and simplicity of CODE-HB, we anticipate that this platform can be used for rapidly evolving biotechnologically relevant biomolecules directly in human cells.

title: Deletion of the Envelope gene attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection by altered spike localization and increased cell-to-cell transmission
text: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) causes COVID-19, a highly transmissible acute respiratory infection that can result in severe pneumonia and death. Many details of SARS-CoV-2 infection are not fully understood, including the cell biology and host-virus interactions involved in coronavirus assembly and release, in which the Envelope (E) structural protein is instrumental. Deletion of E in other coronaviruses has been shown previously to either attenuate or abrogate infection. To determine the role of E in SARS-CoV-2 virus production and infectivity, we produced a reporter SARS-CoV-2 with or without the E gene deleted using a bacterial artificial chromosome. Replication of ΔE SARS-CoV-2 was attenuated in Vero E6 cells expressing human ACE2 and TMPRSS2 and in human epithelial cell lines. Electron and immunofluorescence microscopy and virology assays showed that ΔE SARS-CoV-2 increased cell surface expression of Spike (S) glycoprotein, leading to reduced S incorporation into ΔE SARS-CoV-2 particles and promotion of increased cell-to-cell transmission that evades neutralizing antibody inhibition. Trans-complementation of E partially rescued ΔE SARS-CoV-2 S incorporation and restored cell-free transmission. In addition to validating the role of E in retention of S in the ER-Golgi intermediate complex (ERGIC), our results showed that a lack of E led to reorganization of the ERGIC and Golgi during SARS-CoV-2 infection. Improved understanding of E in SARS-CoV-2 replication and host pathogenesis may help the development of novel therapeutics.IMPORTANCENon-Spike coronavirus structural proteins, including Envelope, are conserved, making them potential pan-coronavirus therapeutic targets. Many details about these proteins and their roles in viral replication and host pathogenesis are unknown. In this study, we showed that severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) replicates without Envelope but is attenuated and impaired in virus particle formation, with less Spike incorporated into virions and more Spike expressed on the cell surface compared to wild-type virus. SARS-CoV-2 lacking Envelope transmitted primarily via cell fusion and evaded neutralizing antibodies. In addition, the absence of Envelope resulted in the reorganization of the cell secretory compartment during SARS-CoV-2 infection. A better understanding of how Envelope influences SARS-CoV-2 replication could guide directed design of novel therapeutics for treatment of COVID-19 patients, as well as the potential for pan-coronavirus protection against future coronavirus outbreaks.

title: A sex-specific platelet switch controls anti-tumor immunity in glioblastoma
text: Sex differences in glioblastoma (GBM) outcomes are shaped by biological, hormonal, and immune factors, but the mechanisms driving these disparities remain unclear. We identify platelet protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) signaling as a regulator of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity. GBM patients exhibit increased platelet reactivity driven by PAR4. In murine models, pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of PAR4 prolongs survival in females, but not males, and is estrogen dependent, persisting in hormonal females regardless of chromosomal sex. The survival advantage is mediated within the tumor microenvironment through enhanced CD8 + T cell infiltration and function. PAR4-activated platelets suppress CD8 + T cell activity, whereas CD8 + T cell depletion abolishes both tumor-induced platelet reactivity and the PAR4-dependent survival advantage. Mechanistically, PAR4 inhibition enhances CD8 + T cell signaling through interaction with estrogen receptor β (ERβ). These findings demonstrate that platelets are critical regulators of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity and identify PAR4 as a promising therapeutic target in cancer.

title: The FMR1 isoform landscape reveals new spliced variants in women’s blood and ovarian tissues
text: Abstract FMR1 encodes fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMRP), an RNA-binding protein involved in post-transcriptional regulation and highly expressed in ovarian tissue. Although extensive alternative splicing of FMR1 has been described, the full-set transcript landscape in ovarian cells remains incompletely characterized. Here, we used Oxford Nanopore Technologies long-read amplicon sequencing to characterize full-length FMR1 transcripts spanning exons 1–17 in human blood and ovarian granulosa cells. We identified 30 high-confidence isoforms accounting for 95% of amplicon-captured FMR1 expression. The predominant transcripts lacked exon 12 and retained exon 14, consistent with previous reports. Long-read sequencing also resolved previously uncharacterized splicing events, including infrequent splice-site usage in exons 15 and 17, exon 11 skipping, and partial retention of introns 2 and 7. Several transcripts preserve the open reading frame, whereas others introduce premature termination codons and may undergo nonsense-mediated decay or produce truncated FMRP isoforms. Notably, the FMR1 expression profile was conserved between blood and granulosa cells, indicating that blood may serve as an accessible proxy tissue for studying FMR1 isoform expression. These findings expand the known FMR1 transcript repertoire and demonstrate the value of long-read sequencing for resolving complex splicing, providing a basis for investigating these isoforms’ role in ovarian function.

title: Benchmarking and Experimental Validation of Machine Learning Strategies for Enzyme Engineering
text: Abstract Enzyme-directed evolution increasingly relies on computational tools to prioritize mutations, yet their practical value is difficult to assess because kinetic data are often aggregated across heterogeneous assay conditions, inflating apparent generalization. Here we introduce EnzyArena, a curated benchmark in which kinetic parameters (kcat, Km, or kcat/Km) are grouped by experimental campaign and measured under matched conditions, thereby minimizing confounders such as pH, temperature, reaction, and batch. Using EnzyArena, we systematically evaluate 20 models spanning four widely used strategies for guiding enzyme evolution: protein–ligand binding affinity prediction, protein stability prediction, zero-shot fitness prediction and enzyme kinetic parameters prediction. Across subsets derived from public databases and 25 literature-derived mutagenesis data sets, most models exhibit weak, fragile, or inconsistent correlation with measured functional outcomes. Kinetic-parameter predictors perform strongly on database-derived subsets but lose their advantage on literature-derived mutagenesis data sets, whereas zero-shot predictors show more consistent generalization. A simple consensus of multiple zero-shot models further improves the precision of identifying beneficial mutants in retrospective analyses. We prospectively validated these findings in a wet-lab campaign (150 mutants) comparing random mutants, UniKP-prioritized mutants, and ESM-1v-prioritized mutants (representing supervised kinetic parameters prediction and zero-shot fitness prediction, respectively), where ESM-1v achieved the highest utility and UniKP underperformed the random baseline. Together, this study establishes realistic baselines for computational mutant prioritization and indicates that zero-shot strategies provide the most consistent, although still modest, performance among the approaches evaluated.

title: Microbial CO2 bioconversion: integrating carbon fixation pathways and sustainable biomanufacturing
text: The continued rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) concentrations has intensified the need for sustainable technologies capable of mitigating greenhouse gas emissions while generating value-added products. In this context, microbial CO 2 bioconversion has emerged as a promising biological strategy within broader carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) frameworks, particularly through biological carbon capture and utilization (bio-CCU). These approaches enable the conversion of inorganic carbon into fuels, chemicals, biomaterials, proteins, and other value-added products. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of recent advances in microbial CO 2 bioconversion by bridging biological, technological, and industrial perspectives. Unlike previous reviews focusing on individual topics, such as carbon fixation pathways, gas fermentation, or metabolic engineering, this work presents an integrated framework connecting natural and synthetic carbon fixation pathways, microbial production platforms, metabolic engineering strategies, product diversification, and techno-economic considerations. To support this analysis, we conducted a systematic bibliometric assessment of 913 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, revealing sustained growth in scientific output, increasing interdisciplinarity, structured collaboration networks, and strong thematic interconnections across microbial ecology, carbon fixation, metabolism, and carbon utilization. Recent advances in synthetic biology, systems-level metabolic engineering, microbial electrosynthesis, bioelectrochemical systems, synthetic microbial consortia, and artificial intelligence-assisted strain engineering are discussed as important drivers of microbial carbon utilization. The review also critically examines major barriers to industrial implementation, including CO 2 mass transfer, carbon fixation efficiency, energy constraints, process scale-up, downstream processing, and economic feasibility. By integrating systematic bibliometric evidence with a critical assessment of microbial CO 2 biomanufacturing, this review identifies the convergence of microbial physiology, metabolic engineering, bioprocess development, renewable energy, and data-driven approaches as central to advancing biological CO 2 conversion toward scalable, sustainable biomanufacturing.

title: Multiparameter Optimization Extends the Lifetime of Cell-Free Protein Synthesis in a High-Throughput Format
text: Abstract Cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) is a powerful platform for synthetic biology, yet the factors governing reaction longevity remain poorly understood despite their importance for high-throughput applications. Here, the three principal determinants of CFPS performanceDNA template design, reaction composition, and lysate genotypewere systematically optimized to extend reaction lifetime in a 384-well plate format. Different energy regeneration systems were evaluated through real-time pH monitoring and metabolomic analyses to identify the metabolic constraints limiting prolonged protein synthesis. Lysates prepared from engineered Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) strains were further examined to assess the contributions of DNA, RNA, and amino acid stabilization. Systematic optimization of amino acid, nucleoside triphosphate, polyethylene glycol, and lysate concentrations identified DNA template stability and amino acid preservation as the primary factors sustaining CFPS activity. Combining these improvements yielded reactions that remained productive for >14 h and produced 567 ± 64 μg mL−1 active deGFP. These findings establish practical strategies for extending CFPS lifetime and improving high-throughput cell-free platforms.

title: Transformative Technologies and Anticipated Radical Technologies: Implications for Sustainable Value Production Networks
text: Transformative Technologies (TTs) and Anticipated Radical Technologies (ARTs) are frequently discussed as drivers of sustainability transitions, but their conceptual boundaries and the evidence supporting their systemic effects remain inconsistent. This review examines how engineering and foresight literature characterizes these technologies and relates them to sustainable value production networks. TTs refer to the capacity for substantial socio-technical change, whereas ARTs emphasize the anticipation of radical developments whose trajectories and consequences remain uncertain. Maturity is treated as a separate analytical dimension. Drawing on the Finnish and Peruvian foresight frameworks, the study organizes the literature through seven attributes and a three-level ontology linking technological enablers, application domains, and sustainability outcomes. The initial Scopus search returned 211 records. Descriptive attribute frequencies are reported against that initial set, separately from the selection of studies for qualitative synthesis. A reference-linked catalogue presents 114 entries from the reference-linked classification, without treating those references as an independently verified inventory of 145 distinct technologies. The synthesis identifies three recurring themes: smart digitalization, advanced manufacturing, and energy sustainability. Technical performance and enabling conditions receive more attention in the reported coding than genericity and socio-regulatory impacts. An interpretive matrix relates selected applications to the 20 value production networks while identifying limits in their evidential coverage. The findings support a framework for examining potential network reconfiguration; they do not establish causal sustainability effects or rank technologies by societal value. Policy recommendations therefore emphasize context-sensitive appraisal, transparent evidence, and governance that combines anticipation with learning during deployment.

title: Unlocking genetic accessibility in Halomonas bluephagenesis: A high-efficiency transformation chassis enables linear DNA-mediated genome editing
text: Halomonas bluephagenesis has emerged as a promising chassis for industrial biotechnology distinguished by its halophilic robustness and capacity for open and continuous fermentation. However, its poor transformability has substantially limited rapid, iterative, and automatable strain engineering. Here, we develop a “restriction release” strategy that increases transformation efficiency from approximately 10 2 to 10 7 cfu/μg DNA, rivaling the efficiency of standard laboratory Escherichia coli . A spontaneous IS30 insertion disrupting the type II restriction endonuclease gene notI increased plasmid transformation efficiency by about 2000-fold. Targeted deletion of notI reproduced this phenotype, confirming its role as a major barrier. Further deletion of the DNA phosphorothioation restriction locus dptFGH yielded an additional 10 to 37-fold improvement, generating the highly transformable ΔEPSΔFlgΔNotIΔPTRes chassis. Notably, the enhanced chassis further facilitated two linear-DNA-based editing strategies: direct RecET-mediated pyrF deletion using a linear donor coupled with phenotypic selection, achieving a recombination efficiency of 16.7%, and CRISPR/Cas9-assisted ribDHBA promoter replacement via co-delivery of a gRNA plasmid and a linear donor, achieving an efficiency of 11.1%. Together, these results identify endogenous restriction systems as primary barriers to genetic manipulation in H. bluephagenesis . Stepwise restriction release markedly improves plasmid transformation and enables linear DNA-mediated genome editing, providing an improved genetic platform for the iterative engineering of this industrial halophile. More broadly, this study suggests a practical strategy for overcoming the genetic inaccessibility of other non-model microorganisms and accelerating iterative strain engineering.

title: EnzymeRSI: A dual-loop recursive self-improvement system for enzyme design
text: Enzyme engineering usually optimises which candidates to assay within a fixed model and workflow; when the bottleneck is a mismatched method or a failing workflow, that route is hard to escape. We present EnzymeRSI, a dual-loop system for recursive self-improvement (RSI). The outer loop evolves harness assets without changing model weights; the inner loop develops prediction and selection algorithms under controlled conditions; a cloud laboratory system is specified for closing the physical loop with quality-controlled feedback. The outer loop raised the mean development-set Spearman correlation on ProteinGym by 0.044 across five assays, reaching 0.335 on CD19 and 0.683 on OPSD (rhodopsin); of the two first places, only CD19 was produced by the outer loop itself. In ThermoMPNN self-improvement the inner loop reached a PCC of 0.849, and on TadA-Bench a Spearman correlation of 0.307 in 1.13 h. We examined the system's experimental decision-making in three enzyme systems. For the luciferase RLuc, 10 of the 32 nominated substitutions not pre-specified reached at least twice wild-type activity in a single round. For the cytidine deaminase A3A, a variant selected by a rule that caps loss of unmodified C raised 5mC conversion in the weaker CT context from 11.4% to 46.5% and reversed the substrate preference in both contexts. For the DNA polymerase KOD-E, 189 single-substitution variants defined a landscape on which different objective functions selected divergent next steps from the same parent; one assayed combination reached 31.1 times the parent on a modified substrate. By treating the organisation of research and the development of algorithms as separately scored objects of evolution, and linking a frozen decision record to a physical measurement, this work offers an evolutionary paradigm for moving beyond the blind spots of a fixed method and for autonomous enzyme engineering.

title: AI-driven structural informatics reveals diverse glycosylation machinery across double-stranded DNA viruses
text: Abstract Glycosylation is widespread in biology and shapes molecular recognition, yet the diversity and biosynthetic organization of viral glycosyltransferases (GTs) remain poorly understood. Here we integrate structural-alphabet-guided searches and structure similarity networks with genomic-neighbourhood and biosynthetic gene cluster embedding analyses to examine viral GT-A proteins. This approach reveals extensive structural diversity overlooked by sequence-based annotation, including previously uncharacterized viral GT lineages. Most strikingly, we identified a jumbo-phage locus encoding five tandem glycosyltransferases alongside hydroxymethyl-pyrimidine biosynthetic and sulfation-associated enzymes, suggesting a previously unrecognized form of viral DNA modification involving a sulfated pentasaccharide. Beyond these examples, predicted saccharide-associated loci span divergent double-stranded DNA viruses, from giant viruses to tailed phages, and occupy multiple regions of the reference biosynthetic landscape. Together, our findings uncover an underappreciated repertoire of virus-encoded glycosylation machinery and suggest that viral glycan biosynthesis encompasses diverse molecular contexts and potential biological functions.

title: From conventional monitoring to agentic AI: integration of data streams and computational tools for real-time microalgal surveillance
text: Microalgal cultivation generates continuous and diverse data streams, including physicochemical sensor measurements, optical and spectroscopic signals, and episodic molecular tests. Together, these data characterize cultivation conditions at different biological scales. Existing AI/ML frameworks can interpret these streams independently; however, human intervention is required to translate predictions into cultivation decisions, adding delays and limiting adaptability across strains, reactors, and environmental conditions. This mini-review describes the transition from conventional monitoring to agentic AI as the progressive integration of sensing, interpretation, and action. The real-time sensing modalities that constitute an agent’s perceptual field include AI/ML models and genome-scale metabolic models, which serve as callable tools in the proposed agentic architecture for coordinated data-model integration in algal systems biology. Emerging evidence from agentic systems in microbiome research and precision oncology supports the conceptual and technical plausibility of a multi-agent, tool-enabled framework for autonomous microalgal cultivation and management. However, the proposed integrated architecture holds significant potential for microalgal cultivation systems, it has not yet been implemented and requires experimental validation.

title: Iterative computational and rational design generates diverse PET hydrolases for plastic depolymerization
text: Evolutionary relationships among homologous enzymes can be leveraged to introduce large numbers of amino acid substitutions for improved functional properties. Here, we combine evolution-informed design (EVdesign) with rational design to engineer improved poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) hydrolases (PETases). Designs derived from multiple PETases reveal strong parent-dependent differences in success and performance, with Thermobifida fusca TfCut2 emerging as the most design-amenable scaffold. Increasing sequence diversification reduces the number of active enzymes but broadens performance variance, enabling discovery of high-performing outliers. Four rational mutations overcome a thermostability bottleneck in TfCut2 and this variant provides a robust scaffold for iterative EVdesign, which further improves activity. Overall, we experimentally test 603 designs from eight parent PETases. More than 400 variants containing 12-68 substitutions were able to depolymerize PET, nearly all outperforming their parent enzymes, and many approach benchmark LCC-ICCG performance in partial conversion assays. These results establish EVdesign as a robust strategy for generating diverse, high-activity enzymes.

title: NPlasmid-seq: Cas9-encoded terminal signatures enable molecule-level nanopore quality control of vector and IVT-template plasmids
text: Abstract Consensus-based plasmid quality control can overlook structural heterogeneity within a preparation. We developed NPlasmid-seq, a Cas9-guided nanopore workflow that encodes sample identity through paired terminal signatures generated at predefined backbone positions, without sample-specific oligonucleotide barcodes. We cleavage-validated 24 sgRNAs. In five representative assigned read bins, each bin showed its strongest sequence agreement with its cognate reference. Contaminant detection was evaluated with a single class-specific classifier applied both to computational read mixtures and to physical DNA mixtures, placing the two designs on a common scale. In computational read mixtures of 5,000 reads, a contaminant was detected in all 20 independent subsamples at each of 0.2%, 0.5%, 1% and 5% abundance and in 13 of 20 subsamples at 0.1%; precision was 1.000 in all 100 subsamples, with no false-positive calls among 493,200 reads from the declared target plasmid. In physical DNA mixtures carried through cleavage, pooled library preparation and sequencing, a contaminant was detected in all six samples prepared at 0.5 mol% input and all six at 1 mol%. Observed read fractions did not distinguish the 0.5 and 1 mol% input levels. Instead, they differed systematically by 4.0-fold between preparation pools, a larger effect than the difference between the two input levels. We therefore interpret the workflow as a detector, not a quantifier, of sub-percent contamination. Read-level analysis identified a recurrent 93-bp deletion in 61.7% of reads from a preparation that had passed consensus-based quality control. Sanger genotyping of 24 colonies identified deletion-type profiles in 10 colonies and intact-type profiles in three. The remaining 11 colonies showed double peaks at the diagnostic locus, consistent with coexistence of both sequence forms within individual clones. In in vitro transcription template plasmids, longer poly(A) tracts were associated with higher multimeric-read fractions. Across ten matched A90 culture pairs, propagation at 30 °C reduced these fractions relative to 37 °C (paired t-test, P = 0.0098). These measurements describe recovered read populations, not absolute molecular abundances. NPlasmid-seq therefore complements consensus validation by revealing sequence and structural heterogeneity within a preparation and by identifying a culture condition associated with a lower multimeric-read fraction.

title: ExPert infers causal perturbations from cell states across biological and clinical contexts
text: ABSTRACT Pooled single-cell CRISPR screens have driven substantial effort toward models predicting the response to a perturbation. We posed the inverse question: which perturbation produced an observed cell state? Here we developed ExPert (Extracting Perturbations), which learns one prototype per perturbation in a latent space shared by 12 cellular contexts, trained on 8,964 perturbations and 19.5 million cells, and ranks 19,895 candidate genes per query, over half absent from training. ExPert more than doubled held-out-context recall over the best existing method with 1,000-fold less compute, and transferred without retraining to drugs, protein degradation and combinations. In alcohol-associated liver disease it implicated mRNA export, unchanged in expression, and we experimentally confirmed nuclear poly(A) retention and isoform switching. In primary mitochondrial disease it recovered the affected complex from blood, localized the signal to monocytes, and flagged a misdiagnosed control. Perturbation atlases can thus be queried in reverse, from state to likely driver.

title: Multi-dataset INST 13C metabolic flux analysis reveals robust fluxes but variable metabolite pools
text: Isotopically non-stationary metabolic flux analysis (INST 13 C-MFA) provides unique insights into cellular physiology but remains limited by low throughput and high experimental costs. This is particularly relevant for emerging C1/C2 bioprocesses, where isotopically stationary 13 C-MFA is generally uninformative due to limited labeling diversity. We developed a miniaturized and automated workflow that combines parallelized transient isotope labeling experiments with high-performance computational analysis to enable INST 13 C-MFA at microliter scale. Applied to an evolved Corynebacterium glutamicum strain growing on ethanol, robotic micro-cultivations with complementary tracers, hot isopropanol quenching, and LC-QToF-MS analytics yielded highly informative datasets. Joint analysis produced the first quantitative flux map of ethanol metabolism in evolved C. glutamicum , revealing strong glyoxylate shunt activity. Multi-dataset INST 13 C-MFA further showed that integrating complementary ILEs increased net flux resolution and preserved flux estimates across tracers and independent experimental runs, while pool size estimates remained dataset-specific. Together, this work establishes a cost-efficient, scalable framework for quantitative fluxomics and its integration into biofoundry pipelines, enabling systematic physiological characterization of microorganisms growing on sustainable C1/C2 feedstocks.

title: Genetic Engineering Efforts to Generate Chlamydomonas Strains for Large‐Scale Biomolecule Production
text: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii is an established model microalga. Its easy manipulation, metabolic flexibility and tractable genomes allowed researchers to investigate fundamental processes such as photosynthesis using genetic studies for decades. Chlamydomonas is not naturally rich in lipids or pigments compared to industrially relevant microalgae. However, we highlight how its biotechnological potential relies on advanced genetic and metabolic engineering strategies, now possible due to the availability of extensive toolbox and synthetic biology platforms, which can improve industrial traits and allow to produce a variety of biomolecules of biotechnological interest. We provide examples of biomolecule production (terpenoids and recombinant proteins), and show that productivities (mg/L) are in the same range or could even be higher than those reached in other photosynthetic chassis (e.g., cyanobacteria or mosses). We point out that despite these achievements, the industrial implementation of C. reinhardtii is still lacking. Further technological advancements as well as clear international regulations and social acceptance are fundamental to reach the full potential of this microalga.

title: Yeast-Based Platforms for Next-Generation Human Health Applications
text: Yeast platforms are rapidly transitioning from traditional eukaryotic model organisms to versatile, programmable chassis for next-generation human health applications. This review systematically examines the translational evolution of conventional and non-conventional yeasts including Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Komagataella phaffii, Saccharomyces boulardii, and Yarrowia lipolytica and redefines them as scalable biomanufacturing factories and advanced living therapeutics. We highlight milestone advancements in synthetic biology toolkits that lower technical barriers, such as CRISPR-mediated multiplex editing, modular cloning frameworks, and high-throughput secretion screening. We focus on sophisticated glycoengineering strategies for humanized N-glycosylation, alongside data-driven paradigms that leverage artificial intelligence to predict gene expression and streamline strain design. In clinical domains, we detail the established success of yeast in producing subunit or virus-like particle vaccines (e.g. HBV and HPV) and therapeutic enzymes (e.g. ecallantide), alongside its emerging role as gut-adapted live biotherapeutic products (LBPs) engineered for in situ delivery and biosensing. Finally, we explore specialized non-conventional platforms, focusing on lipid- and acetyl-CoA-rich hosts for lipophilic drug discovery, and stress-tolerant systems optimized for economical, feedstock-flexible bioprocesses. In summary, this review underscores the integrated value of yeast systems across disease modeling, industrial manufacturing, and clinical intervention, charting future directions to address global health challenges.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Tool Descriptions Are Smelly! Towards Improving AI Agent Efficiency with Augmented MCP Tool Descriptions,
text: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) introduces a standard specification that defines how Foundation Model (FM)-based agents should interact with external systems by invoking tools. However, to understand a tool’s purpose and features, FMs rely on natural-language tool descriptions, making these descriptions a critical component in guiding FMs to select the optimal tool for a given (sub)task and to pass the right arguments to the tool. While defects or smells in these descriptions can misguide FM-based agents, their prevalence and consequences in the MCP ecosystem remain unclear. Hence, we examine 856 tools spread across 103 MCP servers empirically, assess their description quality, and their impact on agent performance. We identify six components of tool descriptions from the literature, develop a scoring rubric utilizing these components, and then formalize tool description smells based on this rubric. By operationalizing this rubric through an FM-based scanner, we find that 97.1% of the analyzed tool descriptions contain at least one smell, with 56% failing to state their purpose clearly. While augmenting these descriptions for all components improves task success rates by a median of 5.85 percentage points and improves partial goal completion by 15.12%, it also increases the number of execution steps by 67.46% and regresses performance in 16.67% of cases. These results indicate that achieving performance gains is not straightforward; while execution cost can act as a trade-off, execution context can also impact. Furthermore, component ablations show that compact variants of different component combinations often preserve behavioral reliability while reducing unnecessary token overhead, enabling more efficient use of the FM context window and lower execution costs.

title: Blockchain and Biometrics: Survey, GDPR Analysis, and Future Directions
text: Biometric recognition, as an efficient and hard-to-forge method of identification and verification, has become an indispensable part of the current digital world. Meanwhile, blockchain has been widely received by both research and industry. Researchers have started to speculate on the pros and cons when these two technologies cross paths. This paper provides a survey of the literature on the combination of blockchain and biometrics and includes a first legal analysis of this integration based on GDPR. Although the integration of blockchain technology into the biometric sector is still in its infancy, this paper aims to provide a holistic understanding of blockchain applicability in biometrics. This article examines several patterns, including biometric-bound public-key credentials, distributed identity management, and auditable biometric services. The survey distinguishes applications where blockchain provides a genuine technical advantage from those where it is not fundamentally required, and identifies its role as an integrity and audit layer around off-chain biometric storage and processing. Challenges and limitations when combining blockchain and biometrics are also discussed; e.g., blockchain networks may not be efficient or economical for some real-time biometric applications. Finally, we discuss key legal aspects of the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) related to this combination of technologies.

title: Shadow banks on the rise: Evidence across market segments
text: This paper examines the comparative advantages of shadow banks across market segments. Combining credit bureau data on retail loans in India with weather shocks as a proxy for credit demand, we show that Fintechs respond more in uncollateralized markets. In contrast, non-Fintech shadow banks exhibit stronger responsiveness in collateralized markets. Exploiting geographic heterogeneity in the adoption of digital payments, we identify technology as the key advantage for Fintechs. Leveraging four natural experiments, we document the significance of lower regulation for non-Fintech shadow banks. Our results suggest that the comparative advantage of shadow banks differs across market segments.

title: A comprehensive survey on green blockchain: Developing the next generation of energy efficient and sustainable blockchain systems
text: Although Blockchain has been successfully used in many different fields and applications, it has been traditionally regarded as an energy-intensive technology, essentially due to the past use of inefficient consensus algorithms that prioritized security over sustainability. However, in the last years, thanks to the significant progress made on key blockchain components, their energy consumption can be decreased noticeably. To achieve this objective, this article analyzes the main components of blockchains and explores strategies to reduce their energy consumption. In this way, this article delves into each component of a blockchain system, including consensus mechanisms, network architecture, data storage and validation, smart contract execution, mining and block creation, and outlines specific strategies to decrease their energy consumption. For such a purpose, consensus mechanisms are compared, recommendations for reducing network communications energy consumption are provided, techniques for data storage and validation are suggested, and diverse optimizations are proposed both for software and hardware components. Moreover, the main challenges and limitations for reducing power consumption in blockchain systems are analyzed. As a consequence, this article provides a guideline for the future researchers and developers who aim to develop the next generation of Green Blockchain solutions. • A detailed analysis of the essential components of a blockchain in order to determine the main software and hardware contributors to energy consumption. • The most relevant energy-saving strategies for each component of a blockchain system, including consensus mechanisms, network architecture, data storage and validation, smart contract execution and mining/block creation. • The main challenges and limitations for implementing energy-efficient blockchains are discussed, considering the trade-offs between energy efficiency and security, the problem of estimating energy consumption in blockchain, the regulatory and governance aspects that impact energy efficiency and sustainability, or the scalability/performance implications of energy consumption reductions.

title: Cognitive digital twins: A state-of-the-art review
text: Digital twins are a key enabling technology for Industry 4.0/5.0 that provide digital representations of physical systems for monitoring and decision-making support. However, the increasing complexity, autonomy, and connectivity of modern industrial systems challenge traditional digital twin approaches focused on simple replication. Therefore, advanced capabilities that go beyond mirroring physical assets are required to enable simulation, optimization, prediction, and adaptive behavior. Cognitive digital twins extend the capabilities of traditional digital twins by integrating cognitive functions such as perception, attention, memory, reasoning, problem-solving, and learning through artificial intelligence techniques, including machine learning. This review considers the differences between cognitive and traditional digital twins, and investigates the operationalization of cognitive functions. It examines how algorithms, software, tools, and frameworks are implemented for cognitive digital twins through a systematic literature review conducted using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) methodology. Moreover, it identifies current advancements; maps cognitive functions to applications; highlights underrepresented functions and implementation gaps in interoperability, validation, and learning infrastructure; and establishes opportunities for standardized evaluation and modular cross-sector designs.

title: OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
text: Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

title: Generation of synthetic clinical text: a systematic review
text: Generating medical synthetic text represents an effective solution for clinical NLP issues like sparsity and privacy. This paper conducts a systematic review on synthetic clinical text generation by formulating quantitative analysis to three research questions concerning the generation’s purpose, generation techniques, and the evaluation methods. We searched four databases including PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect and Web of Science for publications associated with the topic and identified 87 relevant articles out of 1148. Results showed that the generation purposes were dedicated to Trustworthy, Medical Assistance, and Language Resource themes. Prompting LLMs was the main source of synthetic text (40 articles). GPTs were the main predominant technique used to generate the text (63 articles), especially ChatGPT (47 articles). Additionally, there were four main aspects of evaluation, including similarity, privacy, structure, and utility, where utility was the prevailing method for assessment (52 articles). The synthetic medical text empowered data augmentation and clinical documentation. Using text alteration, controlling real text portions, and federated learning, generative models can produce privacy-preserving medical text. This accelerates the development of new digital health applications.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Telemedicine: Transforming Diagnosis and Personalized Care in Virtual Health Systems
text: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) within telemedicine has revolutionized virtual healthcare delivery by enabling high-precision diagnostics and tailored treatment strategies remotely. This paper evaluates state-of-the-art AI models applied to medical imaging and clinical text data within telehealth platforms, highlighting significant improvements in diagnostic accuracy and clinical decision support. Using deep learning architectures like ResNet-50 for imaging and BERT for natural language processing of electronic health records, the framework demonstrates enhanced patient care personalization and operational efficiency. Survey feedback from clinicians and patients underscores AI's practical benefits in improving healthcare accessibility and quality in remote settings. Challenges, including algorithmic biases and data privacy risks, are discussed, along with future research directions aimed at sustaining AI-driven telemedicine enhancements to health systems worldwide.

title: A comprehensive review of digital twin driven pavement health monitoring and maintenance optimization using graph neural networks
Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data
text: The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic, and (meta)proteomic data analysis within a FAIR-aligned environment. It also supports research in the health and infectious disease sectors, as well as in environmental microbiology. The platform's utility is exemplified through various use cases, including antimicrobial resistance tracking, biomarker prediction, microbiome classification, and functional annotation of key microbes. Built on reproducibility and community engagement, it supports the creation, sharing, and updating of best-practice workflows. Over 35 tutorials and learning paths empower scientists, fostering an ecosystem that keeps resources at the forefront of microbiological data analysis. The MGL enables collective analysis, democratising research, thereby accelerating discovery across the global microbiology community ( microbiology.usegalaxy.org , .eu , .org.au , . fr ).

title: HuBMAP Data Portal: a resource for multimodal spatial and single-cell data of healthy human tissues
text: The NIH Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP) Data Portal ( https://portal.hubmapconsortium.org/ ) serves as a comprehensive repository for multimodal, multi-scale spatial and single-cell data from healthy human tissues. As of August 2026, the portal hosts 9,316 public datasets from 26 data types spanning 29 organ classes across 501 donors. Portal infrastructure and user interfaces support data search and discovery, visualization, and analysis directly in web browsers. These capabilities include metadata- and data-driven search, collaborative Workspaces with access to high-performance compute, and interactive Vitessce visualizations across non-spatial, 2D, and 3D spatial datasets. Data-type-specific uniform processing pipelines and rigorous quality control processes ensure comparability of results across laboratories, organs, and donors, while externally processed community-contributed datasets provide complementary perspectives. Here we describe portal functionality, infrastructure, and design, and highlight its role as a platform for large-scale spatial single-cell research across diverse data types, organs, and scales.

title: AI in HRM: a unified model of AI capabilities and process efficiency for enhanced HRM effectiveness
text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming human resource management (HRM) by supporting recruitment, training, performance management, workforce planning, talent analytics, and employee engagement. Nevertheless, limited evidence explains how different AI-enabled HRM practices contribute to process efficiency, decision-making, workforce agility, and overall HRM effectiveness. This study examined six AI-enabled HRM capabilities through an integrated Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory framework. The proposed model included AI in Recruitment and Selection, Training and Development, Performance Management, Strategic HR Planning, Talent Analytics and Retention, and Employee Engagement and Wellbeing. HR Process Efficiency, Decision-Making Accuracy, and Workforce Agility and Innovation were examined as organizational mechanisms contributing to Enhanced HRM Effectiveness. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of 256 h professionals from public-sector, private-sector, and higher-education settings in Saudi Arabia and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. The findings showed that recruitment and performance-management AI were positively associated with HR process efficiency, while strategic-planning and talent-analytics AI were positively associated with decision-making accuracy. Employee engagement and wellbeing AI was positively associated with workforce agility and innovation. However, training and development AI was not significantly associated with process efficiency, and decision-making accuracy was not significantly associated with enhanced HRM effectiveness. The study demonstrates that the contribution of AI to HRM effectiveness depends on the HR function and the organizational mechanism involved. The findings provide theoretical and practical guidance for integrating AI with HR expertise, organizational routines, workforce capabilities, and responsible governance.

title: Population-scale ancestral recombination graphs with tskit 1.0
