Our data shows remodeling of fibroblasts, vascular and basal cells that encircle the DCIS regions and immunosuppressive ducts that support the growth of the preinvasive cancer cells. This study delineates early alterations in the DCIS TME, including many changes that persist during invasive progression.

title: Lipid nanoparticle-mediated co-delivery of human RB1 mRNA and triptolide for localized genetic therapy of retinoblastoma.
text: Retinoblastoma is a rare pediatric intraocular malignancy for which intravitreal administration offers a clinically attractive route for localized therapy owing to its minimally invasive nature and direct access to intraocular tumors. However, efficient intravitreal delivery of nucleic acids remains challenging because the protein-poor vitreous microenvironment restricts nanoparticle transport and subsequent intracellular delivery. Conventional lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), which have been primarily developed for systemic administration, are therefore not necessarily suited to this unique biological environment. Here, we developed a C12-200-containing lipid nanoparticle (CLNP) engineered for efficient intravitreal gene delivery through systematic optimization of lipid composition. The optimized CLNP exhibited favorable diffusion within the vitreous, efficient intracellular mRNA delivery, and reduced dependence on extracellular protein-assisted uptake under vitreous-mimetic conditions. To demonstrate the therapeutic versatility of the platform, human RB transcriptional corepressor 1 mRNA and triptolide were co-delivered as representative gene and small-molecule therapeutics. CLNP-mediated co-delivery of hRB1 mRNA and triptolide produced greater antiproliferative activity than either monotherapy in vitro and markedly suppressed tumor progression in an orthotopic retinoblastoma model following a single intravitreal administration, with no detectable abnormalities in retinal function, structure, or apoptosis during the evaluation period. Collectively, this study establishes a vitreous-oriented lipid engineering strategy that simultaneously improves extracellular transport through the vitreous and intracellular nucleic acid delivery, providing a broadly applicable platform for localized gene delivery and combination gene-drug therapy for ocular diseases.

title: Dual-glycolipid engineered vaccine platform empowers delivery route customization to intercept tumor lung metastasis.
text: Pulmonary metastasis remains a lethal challenge, necessitating potent mRNA vaccines to establish proactive immune surveillance. Although lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the gold standard for delivery mRNA, the "PEG dilemma"-comprising immunogenicity and poor cellular engagement-critically limits their efficacy. Here, we developed a biocompatibility, PEG-free mRNA platform (SG-LNP) co-modified with sialic acid-dimyristoyl-glycerol (SA-DMG) and monosialotetrahexosylganglioside (GM1), enabling a customizable tissue-targeting delivery pathway. This platform leverages the SA-Siglec axis to target antigen-presenting cells (APCs), markedly enhancing APCs uptake and facilitating endosomal escape. Upon pulmonary inhalation, the vaccine directly targets pulmonary APCs, shortening immunological pathways and enabling in situ priming of multiple immune effector cells (dendritic cells, macrophages, natural killer cells, and T cells). Following intravenous administration, it selectively targets splenic APCs to orchestrate a systemic immune surveillance network. Furthermore, leveraging this vaccine platform with tunable delivery routes, we investigated the contributions of local and systemic immune toward the prevention of tumor lung metastasis. We found that inhaled SG-LNP elicit robust local immune activation, leading to markedly reduced melanoma infiltration in the lungs relative to conventional PEG-modified LNPs. Notably, systemic administration of SG-LNP drives more extensive expansion of circulating antigen-specific T cells and natural killer cells (NKs). This systemic mobilization effectively intercepts circulating tumor cells before pulmonary colonization, achieving complete prevention of pulmonary metastasis with 100% protective efficacy. Our findings demonstrate that systemic coordination outperforms localized activation in prophylactic of organ-specific metastasis, providing a strategic blueprint for the design and administration of next-generation PEG-free mRNA vaccines.

title: A systemic-absorption-blocked (SEAL) nanoplatform for mRNA-based local immunotherapy.
text: Rapid transport of locally delivered mRNA lipid nanoparticles (mRNA-LNPs) into systemic circulation induces off-target protein expression and undesired side effects. Here we describe a systemic-absorption-blocked (SEAL) nanoplatform that achieves efficient mRNA delivery to disseminated peritoneal tumors using LNPs with minimized systemic exposure. Intraperitoneal administration of SEAL LNPs significantly reduces unintended mRNA expression in the liver and spleen, while maintaining robust protein expression in peritoneal tumors. Incorporation of cationic helper lipid is demonstrated essential for SEAL LNPs to minimize their systemic exposure. Using an in vitro transwell model to simulate the mesothelial barrier, we further elucidate that SEAL LNPs favor clathrin-mediated endocytosis and Golgi apparatus less involved intracellular trafficking in mesothelial cells, leading to reduced capability to penetrate the mesothelium for lymphatic transport. Intraperitoneal delivery of IL-12 mRNA (mIL-12) using the SEAL platform generates localized IL-12 expression with reduced systemic toxicity, leading to potent antitumor effects in mice bearing colorectal cancer (CRC) peritoneal dissemination. Delivery of mRNA-encoded therapeutic proteins using this platform presents a promising strategy to address peritoneal carcinomatosis.

title: Tailoring lipid nanoparticles for application-specific mRNA delivery.
text: Expanding the therapeutic landscape of mRNA medicines to diverse applications necessitates delivery systems tailored to distinct biological requirements. However, beyond vaccine applications, current FDA-approved lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are often directly used as their original vaccine formulations, substantially limiting their therapeutic potential. Rather than pursuing new ionizable lipids with uncertain safety profiles, we propose an application-oriented re-engineering strategy that leverages the clinically validated SM-102 platform, enabling rational LNP optimization for diverse mRNA delivery and therapeutic scenarios. Through systematic modulation of phospholipid component (e.g., 1,2-distearoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DSPC) and 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine (DOPE)) and lipid molar ratios, we tailor LNPs for transfection across representative cell types in vitro, systemic administration in vivo, and intramuscular delivery in vivo. Consequently, SM-102/DSPC and SM-102/DOPE LNPs emerge as preferred formulations for RAW 264.7 macrophages and IGROV1 ovarian cancer cells, respectively, achieving up to a 25.6-fold enhanced mRNA delivery over original SM-102 LNPs in vitro. For intravenous administration, optimal SM-102/DSPC LNPs enable 2.3-fold enhanced hepatic mRNA delivery compared to original SM-102 LNPs. In contrast, intramuscular injection preferentially benefits from SM-102/DOPE LNPs, achieving 17.7-fold higher muscular expression and 22.0-fold enhanced lymph node delivery than SM-102 LNPs. All optimized formulations show comparable tolerability to the clinically validated SM-102 LNPs. This study supports an application-specific tailoring platform that enables the rational selection of appropriate mRNA delivery systems for diverse therapeutic scenarios.

title: Beyond efficiency: the AI-driven shift toward safer lipid nanoparticles for gene delivery.
text: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have reshaped gene delivery, most notably through their pivotal role in mRNA vaccines. However, as LNPs move beyond vaccination toward broader therapeutic applications, maximizing delivery efficiency alone is no longer sufficient. The inherent immunogenicity of both lipid and nucleic acid components initially observed in vaccines is posing new safety challenges. Herein, we advocate a shift from efficiency-driven optimization to a principled balance between safety and efficiency. We summarize recently uncovered mechanistic insights into LNP-associated immunogenicity and review strategies to mitigate these effects through rational lipid optimization. Advances in targeting, endosomal escape, and subcellular delivery are also examined, contributing to enhance overall delivery performance. The rapid iteration and the need to integrate multidimensional design parameters call for the assistance of artificial intelligence (AI)-guided approaches, that are enabling data-driven optimization of the safety-efficiency balance. This review concludes with a discussion of current progress, limitations, and future directions of the integrated wet-dry research paradigm, outlining a roadmap for next-generation LNP platforms across diverse therapeutic applications.

title: mRNA vaccines for glioblastoma: integrating multiomics and nanomedicine to overcome spatiotemporal heterogeneity.
text: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains among the most lethal central nervous system (CNS) malignancies, characterized by inevitable recurrence and dismal prognosis. GBM exhibits profound spatiotemporal heterogeneity, continuously evading the immune system and developing drug resistance, which results in limited efficacy of traditional therapies. In this context, mRNA vaccines have emerged as a programmable immunotherapeutic platform well-suited to address this dynamic challenge. Recent advances in multiomics technologies enable systematic identification and real-time tracking of tumor-specific antigens, providing a dynamic roadmap of the evolving tumor ecosystem. Concurrently, engineered nanoparticle delivery systems demonstrate the capacity to navigate the sequential spatial barriers constraining GBM therapy. The integration of multiomics-guided mRNA vaccine design with precision nanocarriers represents a transformative strategy for achieving spatiotemporally matched immunotherapy. This review examines how multiomics approaches enable dynamic antigen discovery, analyzes the mechanisms by which mRNA vaccines activate CNS immunity, evaluates nanoparticle platforms designed to overcome biological barriers, and discusses emerging strategies for spatiotemporally coordinated combination therapies and clinical translation. Ultimately, we propose a paradigm of spatiotemporally matched therapy that integrates multiomics sensing, mRNA programmability, and nanomedicine precision to address the dynamic challenges in GBM.

title: Nitric oxide-assisted lipid nanoparticles amplify mRNA vaccine responses.
text: mRNA vaccines have made substantial clinical advances, yet their full clinical potential can be further expanded by enhancing cytosolic delivery. Here, we integrate a nitric oxide (NO) generator with lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) to boost mRNA delivery efficiency and mRNA-based vaccine efficacy. SM-102/DEA LNPs, the lead formulation, achieved significantly higher mRNA delivery compared with the FDA approved SM-102 LNPs in both cellular and animal models. The intramuscular administration of SM-102/DEA LNPs encapsulating mRNA encoding SARS-CoV-2 spike protein elicited substantially higher anti-spike IgG levels and robust CD8+ and CD4+ T cell responses compared to SM-102 LNPs. Mechanistic studies revealed that DEA incorporation promotes endosomal escape of mRNA cargos in SM-102/DEA LNPs. These findings establish NO-assisted LNPs as a unique platform for potent mRNA delivery, which provides a new paradigm for overcoming endosomal barriers and improving the efficacy of mRNA vaccines.

title: Process evaluation of the Integrated Cardiac Rehabilitation Program Employing Smartphone Technology (I-CREST) for coronary heart disease management.
text: To evaluate the Integrated-Cardiac Rehabilitation Employing Smartphone Technology (I-CREST) program's implementation fidelity, impact mechanisms, experiences, and contextual factors influencing its delivery from post-myocardial infarction participants and healthcare professionals. A mixed-methods approach following the Medical Research Council (MRC) guidelines for complex interventions, focusing on implementation, mechanisms of impact, and context. Three quantitative data sources were collected: (ⅰ) records of intervention delivery; (ⅱ) records of intervention delivery time; (ⅲ) content analysis on the frequency of contextual factors from the qualitative interview data. Qualitative data were collected through individual semi-structured interviews with 14 I-CREST participants and healthcare professionals (HCPs). The I-CREST program achieved a high level of intervention delivery fidelity, with an average delivery time of 3.02 h per participant over 6 weeks. Deductive content analysis of participants' experiences found key mechanisms of impact, including knowledge and belief, self-regulation skills and abilities, and social facilitation. Thematic analysis of participants' experiences found four main themes: benefits of the I-CREST intervention; a change in mindset; life beyond the 6-weeks intervention; and the potential of I-CREST. Inductive content analysis of both participants' and HCPs experiences identified implementation-level factors such as recruitment, interoperability and cost, and mechanism/experience-level factors like work commitments and motivation that influenced the I-CREST program's implementation, mechanisms of impact, participants' experiences and trial outcomes. The I-CREST program is a promising home-based cardiac telerehabilitation option that was well accepted. However, further revisions are needed if I-CREST is to achieve its full intended benefits and see successful implementation in real-world clinical settings.

title: Conformalized Semi-Supervised Learning for Medical Imaging.
text: To investigate whether conformal prediction (CP)-based uncertainty quantification (UQ) can improve semi-supervised learning (SSL) frameworks. Five machine learning (ML) frameworks were developed and evaluated: supervised learning (SL), standard SSL, iterative SSL, conformalized SSL (CSSL), and iterative CSSL. Logistic regression (LR) models were trained using radiomics features extracted from MRI and CT datasets across three classification tasks: isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation prediction in gliomas, O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter methylation prediction in gliomas, and histopathological classification in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) with 95% confidence intervals, and statistical comparisons were performed using DeLong's test. Across all three tasks, uncertainty-aware SSL frameworks outperformed conventional SL and standard SSL approaches. For IDH prediction, CSSL and iterative CSSL demonstrated statistically significant improvements compared with SL and SSL (p < 0.05). For MGMT prediction, iterative SSL, CSSL, and iterative CSSL significantly outperformed SL (p < 0.05). Similarly, in NSCLC histology classification, iterative SSL and CSSL-based methods significantly improved performance compared with SL (p < 0.05). Integrating CP into SSL frameworks improves pseudo-label reliability by filtering uncertain predictions and reducing error propagation during self-training. The proposed uncertainty-aware SSL approaches demonstrated improved performance across multiple radiomics-based classification tasks, highlighting their potential utility in medical imaging applications where labeled data are limited but unlabeled data are abundant.

title: Discovery and development of antimicrobial polymers.
text: Antimicrobial resistance is among the most pressing healthcare challenges of our time. Multidrug-resistant 'superbugs' continue to emerge at an alarming rate, while antibiotic development has stalled in recent decades. Antimicrobial peptides have attracted interest for their potent bactericidal activity and lower propensity to spur resistance; however, translation into clinical practice has been hampered by poor bioavailability, challenging syntheses and limited stability. By contrast, synthetic copolymers mimicking antimicrobial peptides have received attention for their efficacy and synthetic tractability. Here we highlight recent advances in antimicrobial polymer development and discuss future directions for their design and implementation. We also outline future research directions, including the use of machine learning to guide polymer design and the development of scalable production methods that ensure the worldwide accessibility of these materials.

title: A single-cell lung cancer atlas reveals cellular and molecular drivers of metastasis and clinical outcome.
text: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, characterized by extensive cellular and molecular heterogeneity. Here, to capture this complexity, we present LuCaS+, a multicenter single-cell RNA sequencing atlas comprising over 2.5 million nuclei from 454 clinically annotated patients with NSCLC with long-term follow-up. LuCaS+ consists of a discovery dataset (Berlin and Cologne, 364 patients) and an independent validation dataset (Munich, 90 patients). Leveraging this dataset, we identified tumor subpopulations with high metastatic potential associated with oncogenic signaling, immune evasion and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. In early-stage adenocarcinoma (lung adenocarcinoma), these cells showed strong prognostic value. Integrating tumor and microenvironmental cell profiles improved survival prediction across all stages, identifying distinct tumor-immune-stromal interaction patterns. These included monocyte- and fibroblast-driven inflammation (lung adenocarcinoma), VEGF-TGFβ-mediated angiogenic feedback loops (lung squamous cell carcinoma) and immune-permissive niches promoting antitumor immunity. LuCaS+ offers a clinically anchored single-cell resource to enable personalized, biology-driven therapies in NSCLC.

title: Molecular Biomarkers and Biosensing Innovations for the Early Diagnosis of Ankylosing Spondylitis: From Molecular Mechanisms to Precision Diagnostics.
text: Ankylosing spondylitis is a chronic immune-mediated, inflammatory spondyloarthropathy in which delayed diagnosis remains a major clinical challenge, particularly during the early stages when definitive structural radiographic changes may be absent. Although HLA-B27 represents the most potent genetic association with ankylosing spondylitis, its incomplete penetrance and variability limit its use as a single diagnostic biomarker. This review critically examines the molecular mechanisms underlying HLA-B27-associated disease, evaluates circulating and molecular biomarkers according to their demonstrated clinical roles and assesses the current development of biosensing technologies for their detection. Biomarkers including IL-17, IL-13, TNF-α, MMP-3, calprotectin, microRNAs, and anti-CD74 antibodies reflect complementary aspects of inflammation, immune dysregulation and tissue remodelling; however, their biological association with the disease should not be compared with validated early diagnostic performance. Emerging optical and electrochemical biosensing platforms demonstrate promising analytical sensitivity and potential for rapid and minimally invasive detection. However, much of the available biosensor research remains at the level of analytical feasibility or biomarker detection, with limited evidence demonstrating discrimination of ankylosing spondylitis from clinical controls and very limited independent clinical validation. Major translational barriers include biomarker heterogeneity, sensor standardisation, and clinical testing. Future development should focus on clinically validated multi-biomarker biosensor systems, nanomaterial-enhanced detection and machine learning-assisted analysis. Collectively, the combination of molecular biomarker research and next-generation biosensing technology can elevate diagnostic accuracy, providing early intervention and precision medicine strategies for disease assessment.

title: Applicability of Prediction Models: Aligning Models with Clinical Use.
text: Doctors increasingly rely on models that predict a patient's risk of future health problems. These models only work well when the patients they were built on resemble the patients being treated now, in illness type, care setting, and stage of disease. This is easy to see when the mismatch is obvious: a model built on hospital patients may not suit those seen in a family doctor's office. The same problem is harder to appreciate when it comes from where a patient sits on a chronic illness journey. Using severe chronic kidney disease as an example, this review shows that a model built from patients who have recently progressed to this more severe stage works better for patients at that same point, while a model built from patients who have lived with the disease for years works better for those further along. This review offers practical steps to keep predictions aligned with the patients they serve.

title: Prognostic Clinical Changes During the Last 3 Months of Life Among Nursing-home Residents: An Explainable Machine-Learning Study.
text: Timely recognition of the terminal phase among nursing-home residents is essential to align care goals. However, how dynamic changes during this period relate to mortality beyond baseline factors remains unclear. We aimed to examine baseline values and temporal changes in clinical and daily life conditions during the last 3 months of life. Retrospective cohort study using explainable machine learning with repeated stratified crossvalidation. Five nursing homes in the Kanto region of Japan. Included were 87 residents who died between August 2022 and June 2024 (cases) and 278 surviving controls (total n = 365). We analyzed longitudinal data on clinical status, vital signs, physical, cognitive, and oral function, nutritional status, and bowel movements from routine electronic care records of 365 matched decedents and surviving controls. Extreme gradient boosting and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values were used to describe how baseline indicators and temporal changes were associated with all-cause mortality. Models incorporating monthly change indicators from the last 3 months and weekly indicators from the last 4 weeks showed substantially better discrimination than the baseline-only model. With dynamic indicators included, short-term changes in vital signs, oral intake, and bowel movements had the largest SHAP contributions, whereas activities of daily living, body mass index, and background clinical characteristics contributed mainly through baseline levels measured 3 months before death. Time-specific SHAP analyses indicated a 2-phase structure: bowel-movement changes 2 to 3 months prior were more strongly related to mortality, whereas rapid deterioration in oral intake and vital signs became dominant from the final month to week. Mortality was associated with long-term frailty and short-term physiological decline. Characterizing these monthly and weekly patterns using routine assessment systems may support earlier recognition of end-of-life transition and inform care planning without increasing staff burden.

title: Plasma ATR-FTIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning for early classification of response to neoadjuvant endocrine therapy: exploratory results from the ANNE trial.
text: Neoadjuvant endocrine therapy (NET) is an effective treatment strategy for luminal breast cancer, but early identification of responders remains challenging. ATR-FTIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning may provide a low-cost, minimally invasive liquid biopsy approach for capturing biochemical information from plasma. This exploratory study was embedded within the ANNE trial, a prospective single-arm phase II study evaluating neoadjuvant anastrozole in stage II-III luminal breast cancer. Plasma ATR-FTIR spectra obtained at baseline and after 2-4 weeks of treatment were used to classify response defined by rebiopsy Ki67 and surgical PEPI, respectively. Eight classifier families, including PCA followed by linear discriminant analysis and ridge logistic regression, were evaluated in R. Hyperparameters and the use and configuration of synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) were selected jointly using stratified four-fold validation within an outer leave-one-out cross-validation procedure. The Ki67 analysis included 49 patients (41 responders; 8 non-responders), and the PEPI analysis included 36 patients (10 responders; 26 non-responders). The highest observed classifier-specific AUCs were 0.738 for baseline Ki67 classification using an RBF support vector machine and 0.869 for PEPI classification using k-nearest neighbors. The respective accuracies were 0.816 and 0.833, sensitivities were 0.854 and 0.800, specificities were 0.625 and 0.846, and Matthews correlation coefficients were 0.424 and 0.614. Complementary analyses showed that mandatory SMOTE did not improve every classifier. When classifier family was also selected within inner validation, AUCs were 0.616 for Ki67 and 0.854 for PEPI. Spectral features were tentatively associated with lipid-, protein-, nucleic acid- and carbohydrate-related vibrational modes. Plasma ATR-FTIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning showed exploratory potential for classifying endocrine response, with stronger observed discrimination for PEPI using on-treatment plasma than for Ki67 using baseline plasma. Joint tuning of hyperparameters and balance strategy allowed class-specific performance to be assessed without imposing oversampling on every model. The findings require external validation in larger cohorts before clinical application.

title: Digital journaling enables privacy-preserving behavioral phenotyping and real-time risk monitoring at scale
text: BackgroundDigital journaling may serve both as a low-intensity mental health intervention and as a source of longitudinal behavioral data. Its clinical effects and its potential for privacy-preserving behavioral phenotyping and risk-signal characterization require separate evaluation. ObjectiveThis study evaluated the clinical effects of guided and unguided digital journaling and explored whether longitudinal journaling data could characterize reproducible patterns in mood and classifier-derived distress and risk signals. MethodsPart I was an 8-week randomized controlled trial with a 1-month follow-up among 665 assigned young adults with mild-to-moderate symptoms of anxiety or depression recruited via Prolific Academic. Participants were randomized to guided journaling plus mood check, unguided journaling plus mood check, mood check only, or passive control. Available follow-up PROMIS outcomes from 423 participants contributed to the intention-to-treat models. Part II comprised exploratory, non-preregistered analyses of more than 12,000 self-initiated mood observations and classifier-derived distress and risk signals. Selected behavioral dynamics were examined in an independent general-population dataset of 16,630 users. ResultsOf 665 assigned participants, 158 (23.8%) were not invited to follow-up because of incomplete onboarding/linkage or administrative issues; 84 (12.6%) were invited but provided no follow-up outcomes. Overall, 423 (63.6%) provided at least one follow-up outcome, with similar availability across conditions (61.5%-65.1%). Primary contamination-corrected analyses excluded nine passive-control participants who used the study app and yielded small anxiety estimates favoring journaling, with the largest arm-level estimate observed for guided journaling at week 12 (Cohen d=0.25). Secondary pooled estimates were approximately d=0.16 at week 8 and d=0.19 at week 12. Neither the arm-level nor pooled comparisons survived correction for multiple comparisons. Complementary Bayesian estimates were directionally consistent with lower anxiety but indicated substantial uncertainty regarding effect magnitude. We found no evidence of benefit for depression or functional impairment. In Part II, classifier-derived high-risk signals were more common among younger users (odds ratio 0.81 per year of age; P=.013). Classifier-derived distress and self-reported energy varied by time of day, and mood and risk states exhibited short-term persistence and escalation patterns. Selected behavioral dynamics were reproduced in the independent general-population dataset, although absolute rates differed between samples. ConclusionsThe randomized trial yielded small, uncertain anxiety estimates favoring journaling, but these did not establish clinical benefit as no comparison survived statistical correction for multiple comparisons. No benefit was demonstrated for depression or functional impairment. Separately, the exploratory behavioral analyses showed that privacy-preserving longitudinal journaling data could be used to characterize reproducible temporal patterns in mood and classifier-derived distress and risk signals. These findings support further evaluation of digital journaling as a behavioral measurement and risk-signal characterization platform and motivate future trials of more targeted guided-journaling approaches matched to specific symptoms or therapeutic mechanisms. The study also highlights opportunities and procedural challenges in online panel-based digital trials. Trial RegistrationClinicalTrials.gov NCT07126275.

title: Quantifying Academic Risk Factors for Student Depression Using WHO Frameworks: Odds Ratios, SHAP Explainability, and Tipping Point Analysis
text: Depression has become a serious concern for students worldwide. Aligned with the WHO Helping Adolescents Thrive (HAT) Guidelines and the Social Determinants of Health (SDoH) model, this study isolates five academically relevant factors--academic pressure, work/study hours, study satisfaction, sleep duration, and financial stress--from a dataset of 27,880 university students in India and quantifies their associations with depression. Unlike prior work that maximises classification accuracy, this study prioritises interpretability: logistic regression provides odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals, Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost rank predictors by feature importance, and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values extend the analysis to individual-level risk explanation. Sleep Duration is encoded as an ordinal integer (0-3) preserving its natural order, and Spearman correlations are computed on the original 27,880-row dataset prior to any resampling. SMOTE oversampling was applied exclusively to the training set, and performance was evaluated on the original imbalanced test set (n = 5,576). Both ensemble models achieve approximately 77-78% accuracy and an AUC of 0.845, confirmed by 5-fold pipeline cross-validation (CV AUC [~] 0.843). Academic pressure is the dominant risk factor (OR = 2.271; RF importance = 0.481; mean |SHAP| = 0.174), while study satisfaction (OR = 0.796) and sleep duration (OR = 0.835) are protective. Interaction analysis reveals how depression risk is amplified by low sleep, high financial stress, and extended study hours: under average conditions the 50% risk threshold is crossed at Academic Pressure {approx} 3.04, and under compounded adverse conditions this tipping point shifts to even lower pressure values. These findings provide data-driven thresholds aligned with WHO-endorsed modifiable determinants to support early detection and institutional counselling.

title: The development and psychometric evaluation of the Post Activity Symptom Scale (PASS) for Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/ Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
text: PurposeTo develop and psychometrically evaluate a new scale measuring post-exertional malaise in people with myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME)/ chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS). MethodsA draft scale was co-produced with patient and clinician advisory groups. After extensive pilot testing, adults with ME/CFS completed the Post Activity Symptom Scale online and repeated it two weeks later to assess test-retest reliability and sensitivity to change. Rasch analysis assessed each domain for unidimensionality, targeting, internal reliability, item fit and local dependency. Then Rasch-transformed interval data and parametric statistics were used to assess criterion-related and discriminant validity (by comparison with measures of physical health and ME/CFS severity), test-retest reliability and minimal detectable difference. ResultsThe item regarding delay in PEM onset was an under-discriminating misfit anomaly which was inconsistent with the remaining PASS items. When this was removed, the PASS was a unidimensional, psychometrically robust scale. Criterion-related validity (r=0.58, p<0.001) was moderate and highly significant, discriminant validity (p<0.001) and test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.81) were excellent. The minimal detectable difference was 1.93/100. Participants found the PASS easy to complete, comprehensive and relevant. ConclusionThe Post Activity Symptom Scale is a valid, reliable, sensitive measure of people of PEM in ME/CFS

title: Development of a deep learning model for glomerulus detection and segmentation in kidney histopathology images
text: BackgroundEstimation of nephron number, an indicator of renal reserve, requires quantitative assessment of glomerular number and size in kidney biopsy specimens. We aimed to develop an automated system for quantitative measurement of glomerular areas from clinical kidney biopsy images, across diverse kidney diseases. MethodsWe developed a two-stage deep learning system combining Faster R-CNN for glomerular detection in whole-slide images (WSIs) and DeepLabV3+ for segmentation. Of 114 kidney biopsies (228 WSIs), 104 were used for model development and 10 for independent final evaluation. Agreement was assessed using the F1-score for detection, the Dice coefficient for segmentation, and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for glomerular area measurement. Analysis was performed at 40x total magnification (2.331 m/pixel) and validated against 400x images. ResultsIn the independent evaluation set, the artificial intelligence (AI) model achieved a mean F1-score of 0.851 for detection, compared with 0.888 among experts. For segmentation, the Dice coefficient was 0.959 {+/-} 0.011 and the per-pair ICC (2,1) for area measurement was 0.989 {+/-} 0.009; both were comparable to inter-expert agreement. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of -344 m{superscript 2} (95% limits of agreement, -1904 to 1216 m{superscript 2}) between 40x and 400x measurements. ConclusionThe two-stage model achieved glomerular segmentation and area measurement comparable to expert agreement in independent clinical data, with detection performance approaching inter-expert agreement, and provided reliable measurements at low magnification. This automated approach may facilitate large-scale quantitative kidney pathology and nephron number estimation from clinical kidney biopsies.

title: Genetic effects on serum and urine metabolites across ancestries and their links to disease
text: Genome-wide association studies of the metabolome have predominantly examined European-ancestry populations using a single biofluid, constraining both the discovery of metabolite quantitative trait loci (mQTLs) and the resolution of causal variant finemapping. Here, we report a multi-ancestry genome-wide association study of 1,955 serum and urine metabolites in 4,431 European American and African American participants from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study. We identify 969 mQTLs for 553 metabolites, 30% unreported in studies of matched biofluid and ancestry, and replicate 91-99% of testable mQTLs in two independent cohorts. In the African American sample with balanced sample sizes, 36% of metabolites with mQTLs are serum-specific, 39% urine-specific, and 25% shared, demonstrating complementary genetic architecture. Only 23 of 632 candidate ancestry-specific mQTLs show heterogeneous effects beyond variant availability and power, yet allele frequency differences expose functional variants such as an SLC28A1 splice variant, virtually absent in Europeans, that increases urine uridine excretion, implicating impaired CNT1-mediated renal nucleoside reabsorption. Multi-ancestry finemapping improves credible set resolution, and colocalization with the Million Veteran Program phenome links the catalog to cardiometabolic, kidney and liver traits consistent with prioritized gene function. Integrating biofluids and ancestries enhances genetic discovery and mechanistic characterization of the human metabolome.

title: Room-Aware Transformer for Activities of Daily Living Recognition in Adults with Mild Neurocognitive Disorder Using Ambient Sensors: Development and Evaluation Study
text: AO_SCPLOWBSTRACTC_SCPLOWO_ST_ABSBackgroundC_ST_ABSUnobtrusive recognition of activities of daily living (ADLs) from ambient sensors may support longitudinal assessment of everyday functioning in adults with mild neurocognitive disorder (mild NCD). However, real-world activity recognition is complicated by heterogeneous home layouts, sensor configurations, routines, and class distributions. ObjectiveThis study evaluated whether a room-aware Transformer that preserves location-specific sensor structure improves participant-level ADL recognition relative to a global Transformer and a stacked unidirectional long short-term memory (LSTM) network. MethodsFollowing pilot feasibility testing with two adult volunteers, we analyzed five homes of adults with mild NCD, comprising 92,765 minute-level observations across 67 annotated home-days. Motion, temperature, illuminance, humidity, and door-contact data were aligned to participant activity logs. The original labels were harmonized into eight categories. Models were developed separately for each home using 10-, 30-, and 60-minute windows. Complete calendar days were assigned to mutually exclusive training, validation, and chronological test sets, and no sequence crossed a day or partition boundary. The same partitions and evaluation procedures were used for all three architectures. Performance was assessed on held-out test days using accuracy, per-class F1 score, and micro- and macro-averaged one-versus-rest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). ResultsThe room-aware Transformer achieved the highest or tied accuracy in 9 of 15 home-window comparisons. Its accuracy ranged from 0.27 to 0.57, micro-AUC from 0.57 to 0.82, and macro-AUC from 0.54 to 0.78. Across the 15 settings, mean accuracy was similar for the room-aware and global Transformers and higher than for the LSTM. Mean micro-AUC and macro-AUC were marginally higher for the global Transformer than for the room-aware Transformer. The room-aware model showed its clearest gains in selected contexts, including Homes C and E at 10 minutes and Home A at 60 minutes, but no architecture or temporal window was uniformly optimal. Sleep/Rest was the most consistently recognized activity, whereas low-support activities frequently had low F1 scores despite moderate or high AUC values. ConclusionsRoom-specific feature processing provided context-dependent gains in participant-level ADL classification, particularly for accuracy in several home-window settings. The marked variation across homes, activities, and temporal windows supports personalized model development, class-sensitive evaluation, and validation in larger and more diverse residential samples before clinical use.

title: Cardiovascular hospital demand projections for Suriname up to 2050 with implications for health system planning
text: This study developed a data-driven decision-support framework to project annual hospital admissions and in-hospital mortality for ischemic heart disease (IHD) and cerebrovascular disease in Suriname from 2023 through 2050. Using retrospective discharge data from 2013-2022 across three major public hospitals--accounting for approximately 71.8% of national admissions--historical trends were analyzed using log-linear regression across six age groups. Population projections relied on the UN World Population Prospects 2024 Revision. Future admissions and deaths were modelled across five policy pathways: status quo, current HEARTS, strengthened HEARTS, full HEARTS targets, and full HEARTS combined with improved hospital survival, with uncertainty assessed via 10,000 Monte Carlo simulations. Results showed that admission rates increased for most age groups between 2013 and 2022. Under the status quo pathway, combined cardiovascular admissions are projected to reach 15,592 in 2030, 30,772 in 2040, and 62,643 in 2050. Compared to the status quo in 2050, projected admissions would drop to 58,073 under current HEARTS, 41,690 under strengthened HEARTS, and 27,469 under full HEARTS--representing median reductions of 6.0%, 33.5%, and 56.1%, respectively. Additionally, projected 2050 deaths would decrease from 2,644 under the status quo to 1,155 under full HEARTS, and further to 924 with improved hospital survival. Cardiovascular hospital demand could rise substantially if historical trends continue, impacting health-system capacity. While not causal estimates or precise forecasts, these modelled pathways illustrate how routine health data can create a transparent framework to guide cardiovascular prevention, resource allocation, and health-system planning in Suriname.

title: Human-centered design can optimize operational details of an implementation strategy: Experiences from a peer-based hypertension medication delivery program in western Kenya
text: Background: Human-centered design (HCD) is a co-creation approach that is increasingly being utilized by implementation science researchers to engage key stakeholders in developing contextually appropriate health interventions and implementation strategies. The exact role of HCD in implementation research, however, remains uncertain. We describe the process, outcome, and experiences of using HCD to develop the operational details of an implementation strategy based on a pre-existing scaffolding that consisted of combining community-based peer medication delivery with health information technology (HIT) to improve medication adherence among hypertension patients in rural western Kenya. Methods: A design team of 22 members was formed representing key stakeholders: hypertension patients, healthcare workers, pharmacists, peers, HIT personnel, policy/program leaders, and implementation researchers. We conducted six meetings utilizing established HCD principles and processes (inspiration, brainstorming, conceptualization, creation, iteration, and finalization), aimed at developing a final implementation strategy with full operational details. Quantitative assessment of acceptability and appropriateness was conducted among healthcare workers, patients, and peers, using the Acceptability of Intervention Measure and Intervention Appropriateness Measure. Results: The design team developed key operational details across five domains: peer recruitment, training and monitoring; HIT; medication delivery; medication payment; and stakeholder identification. Acceptability and appropriateness scores (maximum of 20) were favorable among all participants, but mean scores were notably higher among patients with hypertension (19.3, 19.2) and peers (19.2, 19.2) compared to healthcare workers (17.7, 17.3). Specific recommendations were made to improve the acceptability and appropriateness of the strategy. These findings were subsequently used to develop a final iteration of the implementation strategy. Conclusion: HCD was feasible and useful in optimizing the operational details of our implementation strategy, aligning it with the healthcare goals and needs of the community. It allowed end-users to co-create with researchers, ultimately yielding high pre-implementation acceptability and appropriateness, which we anticipate will ultimately enhance implementation success.

title: Factors associated with the clinical outcomes of maternal Intensive Care Unit admission following obstetric surgeries at Muhimbili National Hospital, Tanzania: a cross-sectional study.
text: Maternal ICU admission provides advanced, lifesaving medical care for pregnant or postpartum women who are critically ill. The burden of obstetric critical illness requiring ICU admission is higher in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) than in high-income countries. Most critically ill obstetric patients admitted to the ICU have undergone major surgical interventions such as caesarean sections, hysterectomies and explorative laparotomies. Common indications for maternal ICU admission following surgery include postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and sepsis. Maternal ICU admission following obstetric surgery is associated with high maternal mortality, prolonged ICU stay, and poor neonatal outcomes. Identifying factors associated with poor maternal outcomes after ICU admission following obstetrics surgeries is essential for reducing preventable severe morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to assess the factors associated with the clinical outcomes of maternal ICU admissions following obstetric surgery at Muhimbili National Hospital (MNH), Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. This was a prospective cross-sectional study, conducted at the MNH, Obstetrics ICU, involving 115 women admitted following obstetric surgery. Data were collected using a modified WHO maternal near-miss checklist. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27. Categorical variables were summarized using frequencies and percentages, and continuous variables were summarized using median and interquartile range (IQR). The associations between variables were assessed using Pearsons chi-square and Fishers exact tests. Modified Poisson regression analysis was used to determine the strength of associations, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05 and 95% confidence interval. PPH was the most common indication for maternal ICU admission following surgery, accounting for 46.1% of admissions. The overall maternal ICU mortality was 16.5%, whereas 40.9% of patients experienced prolonged ICU stays. In bivariate analysis, mechanical ventilation (p = 0.04) and use of inotropes and/or vasopressors (p = 0.022) were significantly associated with maternal mortality, while mechanical ventilation (p = 0.025), PPH (p = 0.031), and blood and/or blood products transfusion (p = 0.003) were significantly associated with prolonged ICU stay. In the modified Poisson regression analysis, mechanical ventilation (adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR] = 2.3; 95% CI: 1.11-4.64; p = 0.025) and blood and/or blood product transfusion (aPR = 1.9; 95% CI: 1.23-2.80; p = 0.003) were independently and significantly associated with prolonged ICU stay. This study demonstrates that PPH was the most common indication for maternal ICU admission following obstetric surgery. The overall maternal mortality was 16.5% with 40.9% of patients experience prolonged ICU stay. The need for mechanical ventilation, vasoactive support and blood transfusion were significantly associated with poor maternal outcomes. Healthcare providers should strengthen antenatal identification and correction of risk factors for PPH, including anaemia, previous PPH, multiple pregnancy, and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy during antenatal care visits (ANC); ensure appropriate prophylactic uterotonics administration during delivery; and promote early detection and timely, multidisciplinary management of PPH to reduce severe maternal morbidity, ICU admission, and maternal mortality. In addition, hospital management should strengthen early recognition and timely management of critically ill obstetric patients to reduce maternal mortality and prolonged ICU stay.

title: Benchmarking Large Language AI Models Against Human Doctors Using an Emergency Medicine Simulation Approach
text: BackgroundProper adoption of AI in emergency medicine necessitate thorough and rigorous appraisal. Classic benchmarks, which rely heavily on basic question-and-answer formats, though dominating the benchmarking field of LLM usage in medicine, have proven inadequate in assessing the full spectrum of skills incumbent upon an agent in healthcare. MethodsWe propose an intricate benchmarking scheme in which the skill set required of an emergency physician is tested and quantified. Our benchmarking structure is 3-fold: skills such as history taking, diagnostic accuracy, treatment plan, and empathy are evaluated by an emergency medicine expert, while the same expertise is scored by an intern from the perspective of a patient, through what we call a simulated emergency room visit. A comprehensive written examination is also utilized to measure general emergency medicine knowledge. ResultsEight LLMs were benchmarked against each other and in contrast to nine emergency medical doctors. Our findings indicate that the AI models significantly outperformed human physicians across several key domains, including history taking, investigation, diagnostic accuracy, and treatment planning. Furthermore, the models demonstrated superior performance in comprehensibility, credibility, and empathy. When comparing AI models against each other, performance advantages were marginal during simulated emergency room visits and were mostly pronounced during the written examination. ConclusionAI models demonstrate a clear advantage over human physicians across a diverse range of emergency medicine competencies. The proposed benchmarking scheme provides a comprehensive metric for a thorough evaluation of medical skill set, furthering validation, adaptation, and utilization of AI in emergency medicine.

title: Data-driven estimation of the onset of heat-related mortality in five Indian cities
text: AO_SCPLOWBSTRACTC_SCPLOWO_ST_ABSBackgroundC_ST_ABSExtreme heat is an increasingly pressing public health threat, particularly in South Asia. Yet the temperatures at which mortality risk begins to increase in Indian cities remain poorly characterized. Operational heat wave definitions are based on meteorological criteria and may not reflect epidemiologically relevant temperature thresholds. Widely used distributed lag non-linear models are designed to flexibly estimate expected mortality as a function of temperature, but do not directly target the onset of excess risk from heat, a quantity central to early warning and planning. MethodsWe conducted a multi-city time-series study of daily mortality and temperature data in Ahmedabad (2001-2010), Chennai (2012-2017), Delhi (2011-2015), Kolkata (2011-2018), and Mumbai (2011-2015). We developed a data-driven structured modeling framework that permits likelihood-based inference for city-specific temperatures at which heat-related mortality first exceeds seasonal background levels, a parameter that is challenging to estimate and perform statistical inference from short and noisy series. Using these health-based thresholds, we also estimated heat-associated excess deaths. ResultsIn all five cities, the onset of excess mortality occurred at temperatures substantially lower than those implied by current operational heat wave definitions. The proposed framework yielded stable and interpretable threshold estimates and confidence intervals across heterogeneous climates and time-series lengths and identified a larger burden of heat-associated mortality than would be captured using standard meteorological criteria. ConclusionsData-driven estimation of mortality-based heat thresholds provides epidemiologically relevant targets for early warning systems and heat action plans. Reliance on meteorological definitions alone may delay intervention and underestimate population risk in rapidly warming regions. Key messagesO_LIWe estimated the temperature at which mortality risk begins to increase above seasonal background levels in warm-climate settings and compared these estimates with current operational heat wave definitions in five Indian cities. C_LIO_LIUsing a structured modeling approach motivated by observed patterns in the data, we found that mortality risk began to increase at temperatures below current operational heat wave thresholds, with higher-intensity heat events associated with a larger share of excess mortality. C_LIO_LIThese findings suggest that epidemiologically derived thresholds may complement existing meteorological definitions in characterizing heat-related risk and setting triggers for action plans and warning systems. C_LI

title: Pediatric lumbar puncture rates in urban tertiary hospitals in Africa participating in the SURE pediatric tuberculous meningitis treatment trial
text: Lumbar puncture (LP) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis are essential for the diagnosis and management of central nervous system (CNS) infections, but LP is underutilised in pediatric patients in high burden settings. As part of the pre-screening and screening procedures of the SURE+DP diagnostic sub-study of the SURE pediatric tuberculous meningitis randomised control trial we identified this as a key clinical issue and quantified how often pediatric lumbar puncture was performed at recruiting African hospitals and implemented a package of interventions to increase LP rates. MethodsWe evaluated the frequency of pediatric CSF sampling of children aged 28 days to 18 years at four urban tertiary hospitals in Kampala, Lusaka and Harare. We developed a family-facing educational video to support LP consent discussions. In Zambia and Zimbabwe, healthcare workers received training sessions including mannequin-based LP simulation, with knowledge, confidence, experience and perceived barriers assessed before and after training. We assessed the effect of healthcare worker LP training on confidence and LP performance and explored reported barriers to pediatric LP. ResultsMedian weekly pediatric CSF samples were 1 at both Sally Mugabe and Parirenyatwa hospitals in Harare, 6 at University Teaching Hospital in Lusaka, and 4 at Mulago Hospital in Kampala. Training significantly improved healthcare-worker self-reported confidence to assist (p-value <0.001) and perform pediatric LP (p-value <0.001). At the Zambian site, the proportion of children with coded diagnoses compatible with consideration of LP who had CSF samples increased by 7% in the six months after training compared with the preceding six months (p=0.002). In Zimbabwe, there was an increase in LP activity the week following training, which was not subsequently sustained. Healthcare workers identified parental refusal, limited procedural confidence, delays obtaining consent from male family decision makers, fear of complications, and consumables availability as barriers. DiscussionPediatric LP was performed infrequently across these tertiary hospitals, and improved healthcare worker confidence following training did not consistently translate into sustained increases in LP performance. Multifaceted sustained approaches combining healthcare worker training with caregiver engagement, system level support and improved resources are needed to improve diagnostic LP use for children with suspected CNS infections.

title: Proteomic profiling of postmortem prefrontal cortex identifies molecular signatures of borderline personality disorder
text: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is characterized by a severe pattern of symptoms including emotional instability, impulsivity, and unstable interpersonal relationships. A complex interplay between genetics and environmental factors has been hypothesized to be associated with the development of BPD. While neuroimaging studies have identified structural and functional changes in the brain, and genome-wide association studies described some first genetic risk loci, the neurobiological underpinnings of BPD remain poorly described. To better understand disease processes in BPD, we performed a molecular characterization of the prefrontal cortex (PFC), an important brain region for emotion and impulsivity regulation in BPD. Label-free brain proteomics was performed in postmortem human brain tissue in a sample of n=79, with a case group of n=36 individuals with BPD and a control group of n=43 individuals without BPD. Differential protein expression analysis suggested protein-level dysregulation of mitochondrial, immunological, and neuroplasticity pathways. Network analyses identified a BPD-associated co-expression module enriched for protein secretory and synaptic processes that is druggable with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. Additional druggability analyses on protein-protein interaction networks and drug-repositioning analysis suggested VEGF signaling as a potential pharmacologic target in BPD. When we integrated BPD proteomic signatures with genomic and proteomic datasets of common comorbidities such as posttraumatic stress disorder and major depressive disorder, we observed a strong convergent overlap across disorders, with STX7 and RTN4 identified as conserved, differentially expressed proteins. Our study provides first insights into proteomic signatures of BPD in the brain, suggests potential pharmacological targets, and provides evidence for convergent protein signatures across BPD and common comorbidites.

title: Adapting a Shared Digital Communication Intervention for Caregivers of Children with Physical Disabilities and Professionals through Co-design: A Workshop Study
text: IntroductionCaregivers of children with disabilities act as intermediaries between professionals due to fragmented communication and information sharing across sectors. The use of shared digital communication may support integrated care. Therefore, this study explored challenges and needs among caregivers and professionals and how an existing shared digital communication intervention could be adapted to support communication and coordination in this context. MethodsThree future workshops involved 26 co-designers: caregivers (n=8), professionals across sectors (n=14), and software developers (n=4). Caregiver and professional data were analysed thematically, followed by matrix analysis to identify convergences, tensions, and design principles. In workshop with software developers, design principles were translated into design specifications. ResultsBoth caregivers and professionals described how caregivers become de facto care coordinators. Clear responsibilities, continuity, and shared knowledge were identified as essential for improving communication and coordination. Shared digital communication was considered promising, but tensions emerged between accessibility and workload, and between transparency and confidentiality. The adapted intervention incorporated structured communication, shared responsibility, relational continuity, a shared overview, and a human digital coordination function. Discussion/conclusionThe adapted intervention provides a foundation for cross-sector communication between caregivers and professionals and adds to the evidence base of communication solutions that may strengthen integrated care.

title: Impact of transnational gentrification on the health of adults from the EPIPorto cohort: a quasi-experimental study
text: Gentrification is a global, accelerating urban process involving complex socio-spatial transformations. Although increasingly recognised as a determinant of urban health, quantitative evidence on its population health impacts remains scarce and inconsistent, limiting evidence-informed urban policymaking, especially in rapidly gentrifying contexts. Thus, we assessed the health impact of neighbourhood-level gentrification among adults in Porto (Northern Portugal), a hotspot of transnational gentrification. A quasi-experimental study was conducted using data from the EPIPorto population-based cohort (1999-2022), with 2,485 participants at baseline. A validated, context-sensitive 16-variable index of transnational gentrification, derived from 2011 and 2021 census and tourism-accommodation data through Principal Component Analysis, enabled neighbourhood classification as gentrifying or non-gentrifying. Difference-in-differences models estimated the effect of living in gentrifying neighbourhoods on ten cardiometabolic and behavioural outcomes. Inverse probability of censoring weighting was used to account for loss to follow-up and missing data. At baseline, 26.2% of participants resided in gentrifying neighbourhoods. Residence in a gentrifying neighbourhood was associated with a statistically significant reduction in nightly sleep duration (-0.346 h; 95% CI -0.650, -0.042), with statistically significant reductions in the lower-education and [≥]65-year subgroups. No significant effects were observed for body mass index, overweight/obesity, total/HDL/LDL cholesterol, blood pressure, and tobacco or alcohol use. Transnational gentrification in Porto showed limited effects on most cardiometabolic outcomes but was associated with reduced sleep duration, suggesting that the health impacts of gentrification may initially emerge through psychosocial pathways before translating into measurable cardiometabolic changes.

title: Intersectional Inequalities in Mental Health Need and Youth Justice Contact among Pupils enrolled in Alternative Provision
text: BackgroundUnmet mental health and education needs increase the risk of youth justice contact. Understanding inequalities in alternative provision (AP) and how these relate to school recorded mental health needs or police criminalisation may identify opportunities to intervene. MethodsWe analysed population-level linked school and police administrative data for 3.7m pupils (born 1997-2003) who attended state schools in England. We examined differences by racial-ethnic group and gender in rates and timing of AP enrolment and recording patterns of mental health-related provision and youth justice contacts among pupils with AP enrolment. ResultsOur findings indicate heightened mental health need and vulnerability to criminalisation among pupils recorded with AP enrolment. Enrolment was highest among Irish Traveller and Romani pupils, followed by Black Caribbean and Mixed White-Black Caribbean pupils. Boys were enrolled more than girls, but some girls had higher rates than boys from other groups. Over 50% boys from Black Caribbean and Mixed White-Black Caribbean backgrounds with AP enrolment had a youth justice contact, the majority of whom had recorded mental health needs. ConclusionHeightened need and intersectional inequalities among pupils enrolled in AP highlight the importance of a co-ordinated public health approach to understanding and responding to childrens needs.

title: Disease-Specific Trends and Ethnic Inequities in In-Hospital Cardiovascular Mortality in Suriname, 2013-2022
text: ObjectiveTo examine temporal trends in in-hospital mortality among patients hospitalized with heart failure, ischemic heart disease, and cerebrovascular disease in Suriname from 2013 to 2022, and to assess differences according to age, sex, and ethnicity. MethodsConducted a retrospective hospital-based observational study using routinely collected discharge data from three major public hospitals in Suriname. These hospitals accounted for approximately 71.8% of national hospital admissions. Admissions with a primary diagnosis of HF (ICD-10 I50), IHD (I20-I25), or Stroke (I60-I69) were included. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for each disease, adjusting for calendar year, age, sex, and ethnicity. ResultsAmong 84,691 admissions, 42,301 were IHD, 24,584 for Stroke, and 17,806 for HF. In-hospital mortality declined significantly across all three conditions, with adjusted odds decreasing by 14% annually for HF (aOR 0.858; 95% CI 0.841-0.875), 6% for IHD (aOR 0.941; 95% CI 0.914-0.969), and 5% for Stroke (aOR 0.947; 95% CI 0.931-0.963). Increasing age was associated with higher mortality in IHD and Stroke. Female sex was associated with lower mortality in HF (aOR 0.835; 95% CI 0.744-0.937). Ethnic disparities were most pronounced for Stroke, with higher mortality among Maroon, Creole, Javanese, and Other groups than Hindustani patients. ConclusionsIn-hospital mortality declined across cardiovascular conditions, but improvements were heterogeneous. Pronounced ethnic inequalities in Stroke mortality and age-related gradients highlight the need for equity-focused cardiovascular surveillance and provide a baseline for evaluating future health-system and prevention initiatives in Suriname.

title: Myeloid subpopulations correlate with responsiveness to therapy in a prospective, longitudinal study on RA patients
text: BackgroundRheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease associated with the destruction of cartilage and bone, increased risk of cardiovascular disease and a higher mortality rate. Despite the many therapies that exist for RA, there is little information to guide selection of the most effective treatment for an individual patient. Ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies have created an opportunity to investigate the target tissue. While a number of studies have characterized the stromal and immune cell populations using single-cell technology on synovial biopsy samples, here we performed a longitudinal study, where we collected comprehensive clinical data over a one-year period on each patient in the process of changing their therapy. MethodsSamples from minimally invasive, ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies were collected from RA patients at baseline prior to start of a new therapy and 4-6-week follow-up under IRB-approved protocols with informed consent. Comprehensive clinical data from each appointment were recorded into a shared REDCap database. Failure to respond to therapy was based on clinical disease activity index (CDAI) for RA after 12-18 weeks post therapy. Biopsied samples were dissociated, enriched for CD45 or CD45CD11b cells, and processed on the 10X Genomics Chromium platform to generate libraries for single-cell RNA sequencing with cell-surface protein detection (CITE-seq). Spatial transcriptomics were performed on formalin-fixed paraffin embedded sections analyzed with 10X Xenium and NanoString CosMx. ResultsWe performed CITE-seq analysis on [~]38,000 CD45+ synovial cells isolated from 17 patients who failed a conventional or biologic DMARD and planned to change therapy. We then subclustered on the myeloid population to reveal 12 myeloid subpopulations that consist of macrophages (n = 8), Osteoclast-like cells, DCs (n = 2) and proliferating cells. The proportion of cDCs was significantly higher in responders, while the proportion of macrophages was significantly lower in responders. The proportion of ISG15+and THBS1+macrophages were enriched in the non-responder patients. Spatial transcriptomics revealed that ISG15+ macrophages were preferentially localized to the synovial lining, while the THBS1+ macrophages are likely interacting with lymphoid cells within the sublining tissue. ConclusionsThese data are among the first to prospectively profile macrophage populations as predictors of response to therapy. Future studies are required to verify whether myeloid subpopulation associations hold across specific therapies.

title: SARS-CoV-2 susceptibility and vulnerability of human blastocysts during in vitro preimplantation development.
text: Human preimplantation embryos express the SARS-CoV-2 entry factors ACE2, TMPRSS2 and BSG (CD147) on trophectoderm (TE) cells, suggesting susceptibility to infection. Likewise, SARS-CoV-2-pseudotyped reporter viruses induced cytopathic effects in blastocysts, while the zona pellucida (ZP) appeared to confer partial protection. The impact of authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection on embryonic lineage specification and developmental competence has not been established. Here, we exposed cryopreserved human embryos, donated under ethics approval and informed consent, to authentic SARS-CoV-2 (B.1.617.2, Delta variant). While embryos with an intact ZP remained uninfected, laser-assisted hatching rendered 19/21 (90.5%) of embryos susceptible to infection, as confirmed by detection of viral dsRNA. Moreover, SARS-CoV-2 infection had a pronounced effect on blastocyst development with a possibly fatal outcome. Compared to mock-treated embryos (n = 47), infected blastocysts (n = 48) showed a significantly reduced surface area (p = 0.0003), reduced total cell number (p = 0.0139), and reduced NANOG+ epiblast cell numbers (p = 0.0054) 24 hours post-exposure, while the number of GATA4+ primitive endoderm cells remained unaffected (p = 0.5255). Intriguingly, despite viral replication being largely confined to the trophectoderm (TE), this selective epiblast reduction suggests a disruption of TE-derived paracrine signaling required for epiblast specification. Finally, prolonged viral replication resulted in embryonic lysis and death. Digital transcriptomic profiling (mock, n = 29 embryos; SARS-CoV-2, n = 28 embryos; each in n = 5 minipools) revealed upregulation of innate antiviral and inflammatory genes, including IFIH1, IRF7, NOD2, and TNFRSF1A, as well as the recently identified SARS-CoV-2 entry factor TMEM106B, alongside altered developmental signatures concerning genome activation, pluripotency, and lineage-specific programs. These findings show that ZP disruption makes human blastocysts susceptible to productive SARS-CoV-2 infection, with adverse consequences for lineage allocation and direct implications for biosafety and virological counselling in medically assisted reproduction practice.
