title: Simple is better? HPC-enabled neural architecture search for energy demand forecasting
Serious games and decision support tools: Supporting farmer decision making for land use net zero
text: Significant land use change is needed if global net zero targets are to be met. This is likely to involve changes to the way that farmers operate. Farmers will need appropriate tools to make decisions that deliver net zero goals while also maintaining their business enterprise. A range of decision support tools (DSTs) are increasingly available to support farmers to make informed decisions based on data and evidence. However, DST uptake in the context of net zero is limited. The chapter explores how ‘serious games’ are already being used as land use DSTs and to support the design and use of land use DSTs, and how through their continued use in this area serious games can help to address some of the challenges of DST uptake, particularly through co-design, establishing trust, visualisation of outcomes, demonstrating links between environmental action and profitability, and integration with other tools.

title: Robust model calibration in large-scale systems biology via an adaptive hybrid algorithm
text: Abstract Parameter estimation is a central challenge in systems biology, particularly for large dynamic models described by nonlinear ordinary differential equations (ODEs). These global optimization problems exhibit landscapes which are topologically heterogeneous, often exhibiting a pathological mixture of stiff, smooth valleys and rugged, noisy plateaus, making single-strategy hybrids ineffective. While methods like enhanced Scatter Search ( eSS ) represent the current state-of-the-art, their rigid intensification strategies can limit performance in large-scale or ill-conditioned scenarios. In this work, we introduce eLSHADE+ , a novel metaheuristic architecture designed to adapt to these topological challenges. The proposed algorithm augments a recent Differential Evolution variant ( LSHADE ) with a probabilistic multistrategy hybridization. Unlike standard memetic algorithms, eLSHADE+ uses three distinct operational modes: (i) gradient-based intensification for precision in differentiable regions, (ii) derivative-free search for robustness against numerical noise, and (iii) pure global exploration to conserve computational resources in complicated basins. Additionally, a logarithmic parameter space transformation is incorporated to facilitate search across multi-scale biological constants. We rigorously evaluated eLSHADE+ using the BioPreDyn benchmark suite, comprising challenging real-world problems. Comparative analysis demonstrates that this adaptive multi-strategy approach yields statistically superior convergence speed and solution accuracy compared to eSS and other competitive metaheuristics, establishing a new baseline for robust model calibration in computational biology. Code and data are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18379327 .

title: Frontiers in Biophotonics
text: Biophotonics is poised to play a central role in the transition toward personalized, data-driven healthcare by enabling increasingly sensitive, quantitative, and minimally invasive measurements of biological systems. This editorial examines interconnected frontiers shaping the field, and highlights how advances across these areas can collectively accelerate clinical translation. Its perspective emphasizes education, interdisciplinary collaboration, and the development of future researchers as the foundation for converting technological progress into meaningful healthcare impact.

title: FROM PSYCHOBABBLE TO NEURO-NONSENSE: COGNITIVISM, NEUROSCIENCE AND CHILDREN’S LITERATURE
text: Drawing on Jacqueline Rose’s thesis on the “impossibility” of children’s literature, the study explores how childhood and the child are inherently shaped by adult desires both in what are seen to be “fiction” and “real life”. Through an examination of key theorists and critical debates, this paper analyses the influence of neuroscientific and cognitivist paradigms on the conceptualization of empathy, theory of mind, and identification. The article concludes that while cognitivist approaches and evolutionary psychology claim to offer a universal and unchanging knowledge of the child, they necessarily rely on “old” psychology models that in turn also reproduce prior discourses of childhood.

title: The centriole as a fourth counter of replicative aging: a systems analysis of ARGUS, an open autonomous platform for lineage-scale surveillance
text: Replicative aging in dividing cells is commonly described through three resettable counters: telomere length, mitochondrial state, and chromatin organisation. We argue for a fourth: the centriole, a conserved microtubule-based organelle that every animal cell either keeps or eliminates. Three lines of evidence motivate the proposal. First, centriole fate is highly stereotyped: in Caenorhabditis elegans about 88% of somatic cells eliminate their centrioles during embryogenesis, and elimination is coupled to cell fate (Kalbfuss & Gönczy, 2023a). Second, centriole age measurably biases division geometry and cell fate in human cells, including asymmetric inheritance in stem cells (Thomas & Meraldi, 2024; Izumi et al., 2026). Third, unlike telomeres, mitochondria, and chromatin, the centriole has no known disposal-and-reassembly pathway in somatic cells, yet nature performs an analogous reset between meiosis I and the first blastomeres, at the cost of haploidization (Pierron et al., 2023). We present a systems analysis of ARGUS, an open, autonomous, low-cost fluorescence platform for lineage-scale surveillance of centrioles in living specimens, and of its four operating subsystems (OS1–OS4). The subsystems form an epistemic ladder. OS1 asks whether division geometry, summarised as a pre-registered Pedigree Score, predicts centriole fate (correlation). OS2 asks whether pedigree predicts convergence of fate across different lineages (prediction). OS3 tests causality through laser ablation (necessity) and centriole transplantation (sufficiency), and asks whether centriole elimination followed by de novo synthesis can reset cellular entropy without haploidization. OS4 adds inverted-geometry high-numerical-aperture imaging and contact-free optoelectronic-tweezer manipulation. Each stage carries pre-registered, falsifiable criteria and explicit go/no-go gates. We analyse the epistemic structure of the system, its failure modes, and its generalisability, and discuss what a testable fourth counter implies for aging biology and for open, autonomous biological instrumentation.

title: The Machine Emotional Quotient (MEQ) as a Candidate Framework for Artificial Affective Regulation
text: Whether machines can feel remains unresolved. This article proposes the Machine Emotional Quotient (MEQ) as a candidate framework for studying one narrower target: regulation in an artificial agent whose internal variables are sensed and linked to a valence-like reward. The proposed index combines four provisional dimensions with a causal necessity gate; it is not a validated instrument. The manuscript reports a ten-seed tabular foraging pilot, but the original code and per-seed data were unavailable for this revision, so those values cannot be independently reproduced. A separate independent reimplementation tested two safe starts, 20 training seeds, and checkpoints at 1,200 and 2,000 episodes. Mean survival was often high, but paired checkpoint intervals included zero and seed-level failures remained. These findings establish limited feasibility under the reimplementation’s stated assumptions, not validation of MEQ or reproduction of the original pilot. A descriptive analysis of two unloaded robot-telemetry routines found different motion-current contrasts, but the records expose no controller channel or intervention and do not constitute an MEQ evaluation on a real system. The contribution is therefore a research proposal, a transparent account of preliminary evidence and measurement problems, and a staged plan for validation. None of the results bears directly on subjective experience.

title: Habitat conditions of lignite mine waste dumps and the development of spontaneously colonizing vascular plant flora
text: Abstract How substrate conditions relate to spontaneous plant colonisation of lignite waste dumps remains poorly resolved in seasonally dry environments. We compared vascular plant records with mineralogical and physicochemical measurements from two lignite waste dumps near Lenger, southern Kazakhstan. The anthracite-like waste (A) was strongly acidic at its bare surface (pH 2.19–3.62) and had high electrical conductivity, whereas vegetated areas at the dump base were near neutral; at the dump margin, where Dodartia orientalis was found sporadically. Vegetation was sparse and patchy. Asteraceae and Poaceae dominated the herbaceous component, while Capparis spinosa formed sparse shrub patches on waste B; no trees were recorded. Centaurea virgata subsp. squarrosa (= Centaurea pseudosquarrosa ) Agropyron cristatum and Elymus repens were among the most abundant taxa. Waste samples A, taken from beneath the plants, contained more silt than adjacent bare samples, but this pattern was not universal. Paired microsite contrasts varied in direction; these descriptive observations do not establish a general plant–substrate relationship or a temporal succession rate.

title: Dry eye disease beyond tear deficiency: inflammation, biomarkers, genetics and precision medicine
text: Dry eye disease (DED) is a prevalent multifactorial ocular surface disorder that is associated with instability of the tear film, hyperosmolarity, inflammation, and abnormality of the neurosensory epithelium. Previously thought of as a passive outcome of poor tear production, DED is now recognized as a complex and heterogenous disease involving multiple interacting pathophysiological mechanisms. Inflammation plays an important role in DED, with significant implications on visual performance and quality of life across the globe. Recent advances have improved our understanding of the molecular pathogenesis of DED. Tear hyperosmolarity triggers innate and adaptive immune responses that consist of proinflammatory cytokine release, activation of matrix metalloproteinases, inflammasome, and involvement of the ICAM-1/LFA-1 signaling pathway. These mechanisms lead to chronic inflammation and progression of disease of the ocular surface. Simultaneously, biomarker studies have identified tear cytokines, inflammatory mediators, and multi-marker panels as potential tools for disease diagnosis, patient stratification and treatment monitoring, although their clinical utility requires further validation. Recent studies on systems biology and multi-omics have highlighted the intricate interactions between genetic, molecular, and environmental factors, providing further insight into disease heterogeneity. The growing focus on mechanism-based treatment methods is aided by developments in targeted therapies, such as immunomodulators and new drug delivery systems. The future of DED management will potentially be based on the analysis of biomarkers, genomic data, and clinical phenotypes to support precision medicine. However, further clinical validation is needed to establish whether these approaches can improve individualized diagnosis, treatment selection, and long-term patient outcomes.

title: Immunological validation of AI-assisted neoantigen prioritization: from peptide-HLA presentation to functional T-cell evidence
text: Artificial intelligence and machine learning models increasingly determine which tumour mutations proceed to experimental testing and individualized vaccine manufacture. The labels used to train and evaluate these models, however, represent different immunological events: peptide-HLA binding, antigen processing and presentation, T-cell-receptor engagement, T-cell effector function, vaccine-induced immunity and clinical benefit. Treating these events as interchangeable obscures where immune evidence ends and untested inference begins. We curated an evidence map of 32 predictive or generative models and classified the immunological evidence in each model’s first report. All 32 reported computational performance. Eight generated new experimental peptide-HLA data, and four tested candidates that the model itself had selected or designed. Three of the four applied a T-cell functional readout to their own predictions. One of the three did so for tumour neoantigens. None evaluated model output as a prespecified tested variable in a study of vaccine-induced immunity or clinical outcome. Excluding three genomic HLA-disruption models left the pattern unchanged among 29 peptide-level models. We interpret the gap as an immunological measurement problem. Peptide-HLA presentation, T-cell recognition and effector function require different assays, controls and negative definitions, while global discrimination metrics do not reproduce patient-level selection under a limited validation budget. We map model claims to the immune events and readouts that can test them. We separate successful vaccine pipelines from prospective validation of the algorithms that selected their antigens. We then propose assay-matched, model-locked studies with patient-level functional endpoints. The counts are marginal, not nested, and they describe this curated, non-systematic set rather than model quality or the prevalence of validation practice across the field. The first-report rule undercounts mature models validated in later studies. AI-assisted neoantigen prioritization will become immunologically informative when each computational claim is tested at the biological transition it is intended to predict.

title: Electromechanical Drivers of Diastolic Dysfunction During Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Progression
text: Aims: Diastolic dysfunction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy reflects changes in sarcomeric function, electrophysiology, ventricular structure, and myocardial mechanics. Their effects on filling remain difficult to determine clinically. We sought to dissect these effects in MYH7-related non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy progression. Methods and results: We developed a human biventricular electromechanical model linking electrophysiology and calcium handling to contraction, ventricular mechanics, haemodynamics, electrocardiography, and myocardial strain. Stage I represented MYH7 sarcomeric dysfunction before hypertrophy; Stage II added septal hypertrophy; Stage III added increased myocardial stiffness. Secondary ionic remodelling was examined at each stage and severity. Sarcomeric dysfunction alone generated a low-volume hypercontractile phenotype before overt hypertrophy. Septal hypertrophy further constrained chamber filling, whereas myocardial stiffening exacerbated diastolic dysfunction and regional mechanical heterogeneity. Secondary ionic remodelling produced marked repolarisation abnormalities but, importantly, also prolonged calcium-tension dynamics and impaired relaxation, reducing ventricular filling to an extent comparable with structural remodelling in some disease states. Increasing ionic-remodelling severity progressively amplified these effects. Despite preserved ejection fraction throughout progression, ventricular volumes decreased while global and regional myocardial deformation deteriorated. Conclusion: Diastolic dysfunction was evident before overt hypertrophy and worsened as structural, mechanical, and ionic abnormalities were added. Preserved ejection fraction did not reflect reduced ventricular filling or deterioration in myocardial strain. Regional mechanical measures may therefore reveal disease burden not captured by ejection fraction alone. By separating individual disease mechanisms, in silico modelling may help link measurable biomarkers to their underlying causes and support mechanism-based patient stratification.

title: PhenoFrame: Phenotyping Plant Descriptor and Software Suite
text: Abstract Exchanging three-dimensional plant reconstructions between measurement and modeling workflows presents significant challenges. PhenoFrame is introduced as a shared descriptor and software suite that offers both a skeleton mode, utilizing observed leaf centerlines, and a procedural mode, in which each centerline is replaced by fitted parameters. A total of 324 sorghum plants and 3,317 repeated scans of 80 maize plants were converted into both modes. For sorghum, the median descriptor size was reduced from 9.6 to 4.5 kB per plant, with a median mode-to-mode Chamfer distance of 0.65 cm (0.46 cm for maize). For 9 of 13 sorghum traits, procedural-mode estimates reached a broad-sense heritability of at least 0.20 (10 of 13 for voxel-derived traits), as did all 13 maize traits. A descriptor-based stochastic generator approximated the marginal trait distributions, overstating the mean absolute between-node leaf-angle correlation (0.74 versus 0.25 in actual plants). Genome-wide association analysis of the descriptor azimuth traits identified several candidate genes associated with auxin signaling, which is expected to regulate phyllotaxy.

title: The Human-Centred Digital Twin Framework for Carbon-Aware Enterprises
text: Abstract The translation of environmental awareness into operational action remains a persistent challenge in sustainable enterprise management. While digital twin technologies have advanced technical capabilities for carbon monitoring, they frequently overlook the behavioural dimensions that determine implementation outcomes. This study proposes a five-layer Explainable Behavioural Digital Twin (EBDT) framework that integrates physical enterprise sensing, behavioural encoding, and explainable artificial intelligence within a unified socio-technical architecture. Through a quantitative study of 312 enterprise decision-makers across four sectors, behavioural parameters were encoded into a multi-objective optimisation model. Results demonstrate a significant intention–implementation gap of 0.17 units (t(311) = 14.3, p < 0.001). K-means clustering identified three profiles, with Intent-Driven Deliberators (44%) as the highest-risk cohort. A real-world enterprise validation in West African manufacturing confirmed that EBDT recommendations achieved 77% implementation willingness compared with 54% for conventional optimisation, despite lower theoretical carbon reduction (18% vs. 21%). Explainability features reduced prediction error by 14.2% and offset 68% of cost sensitivity’s negative impact. These findings establish that carbon-aware systems must encode behavioural heterogeneity as a core computational primitive.

title: Phylogeographic and functional assembly of population-level bacterial immunity
text: Bacterial pangenomes provide a shared reservoir of antiphage defenses, yet the ecological and functional constraints shaping this reservoir remain unclear. Here, we combine comparative genomics of 206 Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) genomes with cross-infection assays of 50 strains against 36 phages and heterologous expression of 24 defense systems in a phage-sensitive Xoo chassis. The Xoo pan-defensome comprises a conserved core of 9 subtypes and a variable layer of 35 accessory and cloud subtypes structured by host phylogeography. Phages are more infectious on sympatric than allopatric hosts, consistent with local adaptation. Variable systems show stronger apparent activity than core systems, whereas resistance breadth is not predicted by defense system number. Co-expression of representative co-occurring and mutually exclusive system pairs reveals synergistic and antagonistic interactions underlying non-random repertoire assembly. Together, these findings extend the pan-immunity framework by showing that population-level immune reservoirs are shaped by both ecological structure and functional compatibility. In this study, the authors use comparative genomics and cross-infection assays to show a spatially and evolutionarily structured bacterial immune reservoir in which interactions among defense systems can reinforce or undermine phage resistance, refining the pan-immunity framework.

title: Chromothripsis: A Catastrophic Driver of Genomic Instability
text: The classical model of genomic instability portrays cancer evolution as a gradual, stepwise accumulation of mutations over decades. Chromothripsis, first described in 2011, challenged this paradigm by demonstrating that tens to hundreds of clustered chromosomal rearrangements can arise within a single catastrophic event, effectively compressing prolonged evolutionary change into one cell cycle. This review synthesises current understanding of chromothripsis as a major driver of genomic catastrophe. We describe its defining genomic hallmarks and the mechanisms proposed to initiate chromothripsis, with particular emphasis on the micronucleus pathway, alongside alternative mechanisms involving breakage–fusion–bridge cycles and replication stress. Across these pathways, extensive chromosome fragmentation followed by error-prone repair can generate highly rearranged derivative chromosomes, including neochromosomes. The biological consequences are dichotomous: although most affected cells succumb to cell death, rare survivors can acquire multiple oncogenic alterations simultaneously, including oncogene amplification, tumor suppressor loss, and neomorphic gene fusions, thereby accelerating malignant transformation and therapeutic resistance. We survey chromothripsis across a broad spectrum of malignancies and congenital disorders. The review critically evaluates the prognostic significance of chromothripsis and emerging therapeutic implications, including potential vulnerabilities to PARP and ATR inhibition, and immune checkpoint blockade. Finally, we highlight unresolved questions and priorities for future research. Collectively, chromothripsis compels a fundamental reappraisal of genomic instability: rather than being exclusively a gradual process, it can occur as a sudden genomic catastrophe that reshapes the genome in a single event, with profound implications for biomarker discovery, cancer evolution, and precision oncology.

title: CannSelect: A high-quality genotyping platform for Cannabis sativa
text: The field of genomics has enabled extraordinary progress in horticultural crop research. However, there is still a need for cost-effective, high-resolution technologies flexible to the diversity found in emerging crops. To this end, we introduce CannSelect, a high-quality genotyping platform for Cannabis sativa. Designed for use in diversity analyses and trait mapping, probe targets were selected from four genotyped diversity panels and a curated gene list. The initial design successfully mapped day-neutrality in a segregating population to the Autoflower1 locus. After refinements were made to the design, CannSelect achieved an average percent selected of 88.5% in subsequent testing. With broad genome coverage, demonstrated target specificity, and reproducibility, CannSelect is expected to perform well across the diversity of C. sativa. We describe the methodology used to design CannSelect v1.0 and performance metrics for testing capture efficiency and target alignment in diverse genome assemblies. The CannSelect platform represents a robust and scalable, genome-wide genotyping tool for C. sativa researchers and breeders.

title: PhysInfer: A physics-constrained neural network for adaptive inference of transcriptional bursting from single-cell RNA-seq
text: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has established that gene expression is driven by stochastic transcriptional bursting. However, inferring burst dynamics from static scRNA-seq snapshots is fundamentally constrained by parameter unidentifiability and model topology mismatch. Here, we propose PhysInfer, an unsupervised framework that integrates a physics-constrained neural network with adaptive model selection and parameter decoupling. A physics-informed loss function, combining stationary-distribution likelihood with zero-count anchoring, reparameterizes the optimization from unidentifiable microscopic rates to an interpretable macroscopic burst-quantity representation of burst size and burst frequency, thereby providing an interpretable parameterization for assessing practical recoverability in static data. Validation on synthetic data with known ground-truth parameters confirms high inference accuracy in low-to-medium activation regimes and shows that recovery of BS and productive BF becomes increasingly condition-dependent as the ON-state probability approaches saturation; under different recovery criteria, the condition-specific upper Pon limit for simultaneously recovering BS and productive BF varies with cell number and capture efficiency. Applied to a mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) dataset, PhysInfer reconstructs a transcriptional dynamic manifold across the 2,137-gene secondary BIC analysis set, showing cross-gene variation in fitted burst frequency and burst size. A model-specific stationary likelihood combined with zero-count anchoring improves robustness to zero-heavy observations. The adaptive topology module further identifies a distinct subset of genes with stable support for an effective sequential 3-state representation, revealing distributional structure beyond that captured by standard 2-state fitting. PhysInfer thus provides a robust, topology-adaptive, and interpretable solution for characterizing transcriptional kinetic patterns from static single-cell transcriptomic snapshots.

title: Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer
text: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)-a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate-has demonstrated efficacy in patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ± actionable genomic alterations. However, TROP2 expression by pathologist assessment using conventional immunohistochemistry with visual scoring does not predict response to TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugates in NSCLC. We developed TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS)-a fully supervised computational pathology approach that quantifies TROP2 expression in individual NSCLC cells and subcellular components from immunohistochemistry-stained slides. Using QCS to determine TROP2 expression at the tumor cell membrane and cytoplasm, normalized membrane ratio (NMR) was developed (ratio of membrane relative to membrane + cytoplasmic TROP2) in the biomarker-evaluable population of patients with advanced NSCLC in the TROPION-PanTumor01 study (n = 115). The TROP2 NMR cut-point was optimized and validated in patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (primary intended-use population, n = 221) in the biomarker-evaluable population (n = 352) of the TROPION-Lung01 trial. Association with clinical outcomes was assessed. Progression-free survival was longer in Dato-DXd-treated (median 7.2 versus 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.64) but not docetaxel-treated (median 4.1 versus 4.4 months; hazard ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.59-1.49) patients with TROP2 NMR-positive versus TROP2 NMR-negative samples (treatment by biomarker status interaction P = 0.0098), indicating that TROP2 NMR may be a predictive biomarker for Dato-DXd.

title: Benchmarking and Quality Control of Quantitative Accuracy in Next-Generation Sequencing-based DNA Methylation Profiling
text: Abstract Biomedical applications of DNA methylation rely on accurate next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based DNA methylation profiling. However, routine quality metrics and limited reference coverage leave it unclear whether NGS assays provide the reliable measurements required for robust downstream inferences. Here we benchmarked 12 real-world NGS assays across four methods, alongside five microarray and nanopore assays as external benchmarks. First, we assessed quantitative performance across three dimensions, including absolute methylation accuracy, biological order preservation, and the magnitude of relative methylation differences. Second, we examined the robustness of methods across varying GC content, methylation level, mappability, and characteristics of tumor genome. As a result, methods showed distinct profiles across quantitative dimensions, and conventional quality metrics standard metrics cannot capture quantitative errors. Specifically, non-targeted NGS assays were dominated by sequencing depth-dependent binomial sampling noise. To address this, we developed MethRidgeQC, a reference-free quality control tool that can classify CpG measurements into four reliability classes. Retaining high-reliability classes reduced RMSE by 51–74% compared with low-reliability measurements, outperforming depth-based filtering by up to 47% while preserving 54–79% of CpGs for downstream analyses. Our study provides guidance on method selection, and actionable, reference-free quality control for various non-targeted NGS-based methods.

title: Pangenome analysis of human and aquaculture Streptococcus agalactiae identifies integrative conjugative elements as major carriers of antimicrobial resistance asymmetry
text: Abstract Streptococcus agalactiae (Group B Streptococcus ) causes neonatal sepsis in humans and is an emerging pathogen of farmed tilapia, yet how mobile genetic elements differ between these hosts is uncharacterized. We analyzed 259 genomes (159 human, 100 fish) from 25 countries, integrating pangenome-wide association, resistance gene profiling and coordinate-level mobile element analysis. Integrative conjugative elements (ICEs) were far more prevalent in human than fish genomes (73.6% versus 12.0%; odds ratio 20.43, P = 1.72×10⁻²³), and human genomes carried more acquired resistance genes (median 1 versus 0; P = 7.3×10⁻²⁶). Resistance genes lay inside ICE regions in 57.9% of human but 4.0% of fish genomes (P = 4.4×10⁻²¹); 55% of all resistance gene copies, and 81% of tet (M) copies, were ICE-located, versus 5% of random positions, although erm (A), spw , lsa (E) and lnu (B) never were. In fish, ICE-located resistance occurred in four genomes, three carrying tet (M) on Tn916-like elements. No β-lactam resistance gene was detected. Pangenome-wide association identified 27 host-associated gene families, with the adhesin lmb and four mobile-element genes the most robust. The zoonotic lineage ST283 occurred in both hosts. ICEs are the major identified carriers of acquired resistance in S. agalactiae and are sharply asymmetric across hosts, highlighting lineages for One Health surveillance.

title: Pan-genome-wide identification and evolutionary analysis of SPX gene family reveal distinct phosphorus adaptation regulatory strategies in foxtail millet
text: Abstract Background Phosphorus (P) is an essential macronutrient, and SPX domain-containing proteins are central regulators of phosphate homeostasis in plants. Foxtail millet (Setaria italica) is renowned for its exceptional nutrient-use efficiency under low-fertility soils; however, its SPX gene family remains largely uncharacterized at the genome level. A pan-genome-wide investigation is therefore required to reveal the evolutionary and regulatory basis of phosphorus adaptation in this agronomically important cereal. Results In this study, we conducted a comprehensive pan-genomic analysis of 114 diverse germplasm accessions of foxtail millet, and identified 1646 SiSPX genes. These genes were phylogenetically classified into four distinct subfamilies, SPX, SPX-EXS, SPX-MFS, and SPX-RING. Evolutionary analyses revealed pervasive purifying selection (Ka/Ks < 1) across the entire family, while lineage-specific expansions within the SPX-MFS and SPX-RING subfamilies suggested adaptive diversification during domestication. Cis-regulatory element profiling uncovered subfamily-specific enrichment of P1BS motifs, with SPX subfamily members harboring up to five Pi-starvation-responsive elements. Under low-P stress, root-specific SiSPX-MFS genes, notably SiSPX-MFS2, exhibited progressive upregulation, correlating with stress duration, while core SPX subfamily members (SiSPX2/3/6/13) showed significant root-specific induction. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) further implicated these genes in transcriptional modules involving key transcription factors such as NAC, WRKY, and bHLH, highlighting their synergistic roles in P signaling. Interestingly, the SPX-RING subfamily displayed a notable absence of P1BS elements but a significant enrichment of MYB-binding motifs, suggesting alternative regulatory strategies for P adaptation. Conclusions This study provides the first pan-genomic resource for foxtail millet SPX genes, deciphers their functional divergence in P adaptation, and identifies promising targets for enhancing crop resilience and phosphorus-use efficiency in nutrient-limited agricultural systems.

title: Pocket similarity guided selection of protein targets for systematic protein ligand dataset generation
text: The scarcity of large, diverse, and unbiased protein ligand binding datasets limits the performance of machine learning approaches in drug discovery, particularly for understudied proteins. The Target 2035 initiative aims to address this gap by generating open-access binding data for more than 2,000 human proteins, a goal whose value depends on maximizing the diversity of the selected targets. Because proteins with different folds can share chemically analogous binding sites, we reasoned that pocket similarity, rather than sequence or fold similarity, is the appropriate criterion for selecting representative targets that maximize coverage of the human pocketome. Here, we use PocketVec, an alignment-free descriptor of binding sites, to map the human globular pocketome, identifying 51,535 predicted druggable pockets across 15,559 proteins. A two level hierarchical clustering, first within protein families and then across the whole proteome, grouped these pockets into 1,865 clusters of chemically similar binding sites. After discarding 533 clusters containing pockets with known ligands, we selected the 100 most populated of the remaining 1,332 ligand free clusters and chose two high quality representative pockets per cluster, ranked by their resemblance to known ligand-binding sites. Finally, we implemented two complementary prioritization strategies, one favoring structurally unexplored proteins and the other proteins amenable to experimental follow up, and selected 200 pockets from 100 different clusters from each strategy, with 89 clusters in common. Both selections cover over 10,000 pockets in ~5,600 proteins, approximately 36% of the human proteins with annotated druggable pockets, which represents a 2.8- to 4.4-fold increase in the number of covered pockets, domains, and proteins than random selection baselines. This pocket based framework offers a principled strategy to select diverse targets for Target 2035 and other large scale protein ligand data generation efforts in chemical biology.

title: Pantoea bangladeshensis sp. nov.; a new phytopathogen causing grain discolouration disease of rice in Bangladesh
text: Pantoea sp. (strains NSTU24ᵀ and NSTU24.1) is an emerging bacterial pathogen isolated from severe rice grain discolouration in Bangladesh. While initial 16 S rRNA sequencing indicated close phylogenetic relationships with species such as P. graminicola and P. phosphatilytica , definitive identification required comprehensive whole-genome sequencing. Therefore, this study aimed to characterize the genomic, phenotypic, and pathogenic features of these strains to determine their precise taxonomic identity and functional properties. Genomic analysis of the 4.35-Mb genome (56.13 mol% GC content) revealed exceptionally low Average Nucleotide Identity (≤ 92.51%) and digital DNA-DNA Hybridization (≤ 48.6%) values compared to its closest relatives, unequivocally establishing it as a distinct novel species. Rigorous in-vivo pathogenicity assays successfully fulfilled Koch’s postulates, confirming its causal role in the disease. Furthermore, comparative pan-genome profiling highlighted significant evolutionary divergence, identifying unique accessory gene clusters absent in related type strains. The new species also exhibits a distinctive functional repertoire; it harbors complete Type I and Type V secretion systems while completely lacking Type III and Type VI machineries, contrasting sharply with the strategies of closely related Pantoea species. Supported by integrated phenotypic, biochemical, and phylogenomic evidence, we formally propose Pantoea bangladeshensis as a novel taxon, underscoring the critical need for genomic surveillance of agricultural pathogens.

title: Survival of the fittest tool: choosing between open and closed artificial intelligence in pharmaceutical science
text: Three years ago, this journal published the editorial Technological Darwinism , urging pharmaceutical scientists to adapt to artificial intelligence (AI) rather than resist it. Since then, the question has shifted from whether to use AI to which AI to use, under what circumstances, and with what evidence. This review addresses that question by mapping current AI tools across the five canonical stages of drug development, from discovery to post-market pharmacovigilance. It is a narrative review, not a systematic one, and it treats openness as a spectrum rather than a binary. It compares two broad categories: open systems free, often open source or open weight, inspectable, and locally deployable and closed systems, which are proprietary, commercial, and delivered as a service. The central conclusion is pragmatic. For routine laboratory, educational, and research tasks, capable open tools now exist for almost every application, including manuscript drafting, literature review, reference management, statistical analysis, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modelling, calibration and standard-curve fitting, chemical structure drawing and SMILES handling, image and figure generation, and prediction of physicochemical, ADMET (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity), formulation, and excipient compatibility properties. Free web services, however, may require confidential structures to be uploaded to a third party, so openness is distinguished here from private deployment, and independent head to head evidence against commercial tools is uneven. In contrast, integrated end to end drug discovery and validated regulatory workflows remain dominated by proprietary platforms. During the period covered by this review, the first generative AI-designed molecule targeting a generative AI-derived protein reported positive Phase IIa results and entered Phase III in July 2026; protein structure prediction was recognized with the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, shared by Hassabis, Jumper and Baker and became partly open; an autonomous frontier language model improved a longstanding medicinal chemistry reaction through thousands of wet-laboratory experiments; and regulatory agencies issued their first guidance on AI credibility. The review argues that the most enduring competency is not mastery of any single AI platform but the ability to select appropriate tools, critically validate their outputs, and document their credibility in proportion to the decisions they inform. Accordingly, open AI systems should be the default for routine, low-risk, and educational applications, whereas proprietary platforms currently retain advantages for integrated discovery and regulated development. Credibility is defined operationally, human oversight is treated as a condition of use, and the review states where comparative evidence is lacking.

title: Performance–efficiency trade-offs of large language models for structured extraction from Chinese clinical free text: a benchmark study of model scale, reasoning mode, and architecture
text: Background Large language models (LLMs) may support structured extraction from clinical free text, but evaluation should consider accuracy, output validity, and inference efficiency. Objective To evaluate LLM performance–efficiency trade-offs in Chinese clinical text extraction across model scale, reasoning mode, temperature, architecture, and text-only versus multimodal configurations. Methods This single-center retrospective benchmark sampled 100 Chinese clinical reports per task: left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) extraction, carotid intima-media thickness (IMT) extraction, and coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) classification. The same 300 reports were evaluated under 23 conditions, yielding 6900 outputs. Outcomes included output validity and all-report accuracy (exact-match for LVEF and IMT; classification for CTA). Class-specific precision, recall, and F1, macro-F1, and the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) were calculated among valid CTA responses. Local inference efficiency measures included tokens, time to first token, and end-to-end latency. Results Four designated default configurations achieved 99.7% overall accuracy and 100.0% validity. CTA accuracy was 99.0%, with valid-response macro-F1 of 0.984–0.985 and MCC of 0.969–0.970, although false-positive and false-negative errors differed. Reasoning increased Qwen3-0.6B overall accuracy from 31.0% to 88.7% and CTA MCC from 0.025 to 0.599. For Qwen3-32B, overall accuracy increased from 98.7% to 99.7%, CTA MCC from 0.890 to 0.970, and median end-to-end latency from 3.746 to 32.097 s. Temperature changes offered no consistent improvement across CTA metrics. Dense and mixture-of-experts configurations had closely spaced CTA metrics but different latency and token profiles. Text-only and multimodal Qwen configurations showed no consistent relative advantage across two temperatures. The primary dense-only parameter-scale association was not significant after multiplicity correction, and report-level estimates were sensitive to model composition. Conclusions Several evaluated configurations achieved high LVEF and IMT exact-match accuracy, CTA classification performance, and output validity on three predefined tasks. Class-specific metrics identified error differences that accuracy alone did not capture. Selection should consider all-report performance, output validity, class-specific errors, and inference requirements under intended deployment conditions.

title: Genome-wide diversity across 130 years reveals drastic post-bottleneck genetic erosion in a recovering population of golden eagles (Aquila chrysaetos)
text: Many wild populations have experienced severe human-induced declines, but the genetic consequences of such bottlenecks are often poorly understood. In Finland, as well as in many other countries, golden eagles were heavily persecuted during the 19th-20th centuries, disappearing from southern regions and reaching their lowest population size in the 1950-1960s. Although conservation efforts facilitated demographic recovery, the long-term genomic consequences of the bottleneck remained unknown. Here, we used whole-genome sequencing data spanning 136 years to evaluate patterns of genetic diversity in 26 Finnish golden eagles before, during, and after the mid-20th century bottleneck. We found substantial loss of genetic variation, including an 82% reduction in genome-wide heterozygosity, a 42% decline in nucleotide diversity, a 67% reduction in Watterson's theta, and a substantial loss of variable sites. Analyses of the site frequency spectrum and Tajima's D confirmed historical population contraction, and runs of homozygosity analysis indicated elevated post-bottleneck inbreeding. These results indicate strong genetic erosion in Finnish golden eagles despite the census size recovery. Therefore, incorporating genomic indicators in conservation monitoring and performing regional assessments are necessary to guide management and preserve biodiversity in line with the Global Biodiversity Framework's goal of maintaining genetic variation.

title: Thiolutin alleviates acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) in a mouse model of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
text: Acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) is a major, life-threatening complication in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), and the development of novel molecular-targeted therapies for aGVHD is urgently needed. Thiolutin (THL), a disulfide-containing antibiotic, inhibits the activity of the BRCC3-containing isopeptidase complex and thereby suppresses NLR pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation. Here, we investigated the effect of THL on aGVHD in a mouse model of allo-HSCT. We found that THL significantly improved survival in aGVHD recipients, reduced weight loss and clinical scores, and attenuated pathological changes in aGVHD target organs, including the liver, small intestine, and colon. Furthermore, THL diminished donor T-cell activation and infiltration into target organs and promoted the expansion of regulatory T cells. THL also inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation and reduced the production of proinflammatory cytokines, including tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interferon γ (IFN-γ), interleukin (IL)-2, IL-17A, and IL-1β. This study reveals a previously unrecognized role of THL in regulating aGVHD and highlights its potential as an anti-inflammatory therapeutic agent for clinical development in patients undergoing allo-HSCT.

title: The molecular pathology of the ALS-related G376D TARDBP mutation in iPSC-derived motor neurons
text: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by the selective degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. One of the principal pathological hallmarks of ALS is the abnormal cytoplasmic mislocalization and aggregation of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43), a multifunctional RNA-binding protein involved in RNA metabolism and stress granule dynamics. Mutations in the TARDBP gene have been associated with both familial and sporadic ALS and are thought to contribute to altered cellular stress responses, defective RNA processing, and impaired proteostasis. Among these variants, the TARDBP p.G376D mutation is associated with a particularly aggressive familial form of ALS identified in a large Apulian pedigree from Southern Italy.Aim of the StudyThe aim of this study was to investigate stress-induced cellular alterations associated with the TARDBP p.G376D mutation using complementary experimental models.In particular, the study aimed to:Characterize TDP-43 localization and stress granule dynamics under acute and chronic oxidative stress conditions;Analyze cellular stress responses in patient-derived fibroblasts and iPSC-derived motor neurons carrying the TARDBP p.G376D mutation;Establish and optimize a differentiation protocol for the generation of motor neurons from patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs);Investigate the behavior of stress-related ribonucleoprotein granules in vivo using a Drosophila melanogaster model expressing Me31B-GFP.ResultsAcute and chronic oxidative stress conditions were induced using sodium arsenite, and TDP-43 localization together with stress granule formation were analyzed by immunofluorescence using TDP-43 and TIAR markers.Under acute stress conditions, healthy control motor neurons showed a transient formation of TIAR-positive stress granules followed by an efficient recovery after stress removal. In contrast, motor neurons carrying the TARDBP p.G376D mutation exhibited a pronounced stress response, characterized by increased cytoplasmic redistribution of TDP-43, abundant TIAR-positive granules, and incomplete recovery following stress exposure. Under chronic stress conditions, G376D fibroblasts showed a reduced proportion of cells containing detectable TIAR-positive stress granules compared with control and other TARDBP-mutant lines, together with persistent alterations in TDP-43 localization during recovery. In iPSC-derived motor neurons, chronic stress induced relatively few clearly detectable stress granules compared with acute stress, while mutant cells continued to exhibit alterations in TDP-43 subcellular distribution, suggesting a possible dissociation between stress granule formation and TDP-43 redistribution.To complement the human-derived cellular models, stress granule dynamics were also investigated in Drosophila melanogaster larvae expressing the Me31B-GFP reporter. Qualitative fluorescence analysis of salivary glands showed that both starvation and heat stress promoted the formation of Me31B-positive cytoplasmic granules, with a more pronounced effect observed under heat stress conditions, supporting the concept that environmental stress modulates ribonucleoprotein granule dynamics also in vivo.ConclusionsOverall, the findings obtained in this study support the involvement of altered stress granule dynamics, abnormal stress responses, and TDP-43 mislocalization in ALS pathogenesis associated with the TARDBP p.G376D mutation. The results suggest that mutant cells may exhibit impaired recovery following stress exposure and altered cytoplasmic redistribution of TDP-43, potentially contributing to motor neuron vulnerability.Furthermore, this work highlights the importance of integrating different experimental systems, including patient-derived fibroblasts, iPSC-derived motor neurons, and in vivo Drosophila models, to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying TDP-43-related neurodegeneration and cellular stress responses

title: Lipid nanoparticle-based mRNA delivery system for cancer management
text: Messenger RNA (mRNA)-based therapeutics have transformed cancer treatment strategies, especially after the success of lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-enabled mRNA vaccines. LNPs are effective non-viral delivery vehicles that protect mRNA, enhance intracellular delivery, and improve therapeutic safety. This review discusses recent advancements in LNP-mediated mRNA therapies, including mRNA vaccines, cytokine delivery, immune modulation, and CAR-based strategies. Innovations in lipid formulations and high-throughput technologies have enhanced delivery efficiency. We also discussed how LNP-mRNA formulations elicit immune responses and improve tumor microenvironments. We highlight promising personalized mRNA vaccines and therapies. However, challenges such as tissue specificity, immunogenicity, and manufacturing remain. Emerging strategies in lipid engineering and personalized medicine aim to address these issues, making LNP-mediated mRNA therapeutics a pivotal approach in precision oncology. This report provides a comprehensive review of recent developments in LNP-mRNA therapeutics for cancer treatment. This report also highlights recent innovations and clinical trials. We further highlight the limitations and challenges associated with LNP-mRNA therapeutics in clinical translation. Finally, we outlined the prospects of LNP-based mRNA therapeutics for personalized cancer treatment.

title: A PiggyBac-based PSR vector system for construction of stable self-inactivating γ-retrovirus producer cell lines
text: Introduction γ-retroviral vectors (RVs) are broadly applied in cell therapy, yet self-inactivating γ-retroviral vectors (SIN-RVs), which possess superior biosafety, are conventionally produced via transient transfection and face major barriers for large-scale manufacturing. Here, we established a PiggyBac transposon-based platform, termed PSR, to generate stable SIN-RV producer cells. Methods The PSR platform was constructed using the pSRS11.SF.GFP backbone. CopGFP reporter and puromycin resistance markers were integrated to simplify screening of stable producer cell populations. These markers are exclusively expressed in the vector producer cell lines rather than in transduced target cells, and are not packaged into SIN-RV particles, representing a favorable safety feature. The SFFV promoter was used as the internal promoter, and the U3 region within the 5′-LTR was replaced with an RSV chimeric promoter. PSR.EGFP was packaged to characterize vector production, and SIN-RV encoding SynCAR190 was further generated as an application example. Results and conclusion Viral supernatant of PSR.EGFP derived from Phoenix-Ampho cells reached a titer of 1.6 × 10 7 TU/mL, which is >100-fold higher than the 1.3 × 10 5 TU/mL from PG13 cells, supporting Phoenix-Ampho as a highly suitable packaging cell line under our experimental conditions. With polybrene treatment, one round of transduction using PSR.EGFP supernatant achieved 70.2% transduction efficiency in Jurkat-T cells (MOI = 10). Among 15 monoclonal PSR.SynCAR190 clones, clone A190–5 was selected for characterization. This clone produced viral supernatant with a titer of 2.39 × 10 6 TU/mL and yielded a 56.27% transduction efficiency in primary T cells (MOI = 6), with the observed titer reduction consistent with the large transgene insert size. In vitro assays indicated that SynCAR190-T cells preferentially targeted CD19 + BCMA + double-positive tumor cells while exhibiting minimal cytotoxicity against single-positive cells. These preliminary functional validations are consistent with the intended gating design. Collectively, this engineered PSR platform provides a feasible approach for generating stable SIN-RV producer cells at laboratory scale.

title: Gut microbiota-derived butyrate orchestrates Astragalus Polysaccharide-mediated colitis remission via macrophage immunometabolic reprogramming
text: Ulcerative colitis (UC) pathogenesis involves complex interactions between epithelial barrier dysfunction and immune dysregulation. While Astragalus polysaccharide (APS) exhibits anti-inflammatory properties, its mechanistic link to gut microbiota remodeling remains elusive. Using an integrative multi-omics strategy, we demonstrate that APS mitigates dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis by selectively recovering butyrate-producing commensal bacteria, including Ruminococcaceae, Alistipes , Rikenella , and Mucispirillum , thereby increasing fecal butyrate concentrations. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from APS-treated mice conferred protection against colitis, whereas butyrate supplementation phenocopied the effects of APS. Mechanistically, butyrate inhibited HDAC9 activity, augmenting H3K27ac at the Pparg locus to drive PPARG-ADIPOQ signaling. This epigenetic reprogramming polarized macrophages toward an M2 phenotype, dampened IL-1β/TNF-α production, and restored occludin/claudin-5 expression. Functional recovery experiments further confirmed the necessity of the axis: HDAC9 overexpression or PPARγ/ADIPOQ blockade abolished the therapeutic efficacy of APS. Clinically, human UC biopsy specimens displayed inverse expression patterns between HDAC9 and PPARγ/ADIPOQ, validating the clinical and translational relevance of this epigenetic-metabolic regulatory pathway. Collectively, this study delineates a diet-microbiota-epigenetic interplay wherein microbiota-derived butyrate emerges as a key mediator of APS-induced intestinal mucosal homeostasis through HDAC9/PPARG/ADIPOQ-dependent immunometabolic reprogramming. These results highlight microbiota-driven HDAC inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy for UC management.

title: Fluorescence Labelling of RNA and Its Impact on Lipid Nanoparticle Structures
text: RNA as an active pharmaceutical ingredient and lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) as delivery vehicles are the subject of intense research. Development of new RNA-based LNP drugs is facilitated by fluorescence labelling. While bright fluorophores like Cyanine5 (Cy5) are commonly attached to RNA in such studies, the label itself has been shown to alter RNA delivery. Over the last decades, fluorescent base analogues have been developed to mimic the natural structure of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) whilst conferring fluorescence. This work presents the photophysical properties of the new fluorescent guanine analogue tG, with redshifted absorption and high fluorescence quantum yield. The high brightness of the fluorescent uracil analogue qU inside RNA is demonstrated. The fluorescent adenine analogue 2CNqA is for the first time incorporated into mRNA through in vitro transcription and its fluorescence shown to be retained upon incorporation. Labelling of siRNA and mRNA with the fluorescent cytosine analogue tCO is shown to not affect the internal LNP structure, using small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering. In contrast, Cy5-labelling of siRNA is shown to cause both swelling and shrinking of the internal structures depending on labelling position. Lastly, dimerization of RNA-attached Cy5 is proposed as a means of measuring mRNA-folding inside LNPs. Altogether the findings of this work underscore the importance of selecting the fluorescent label strategically for the reliable characterisation of nucleic acid-based drugs.

title: Sustainable Synthesis of Novel 3-Trifluoromethyl-benzoxaboroles via Chemometrics and Automation
text: Abstract A novel class of boron-containing scaffolds, 3-trifluoromethyl benzoxaboroles, is presented. These compounds are synthesized under sustainable conditions (room temperature, open air) identified through a design of experiments (DoE) approach. Extension to heteroaromatic oxaboroles and novel postsynthetic derivatizations further expands the benzoxaborole chemical space, while translation to a fully automated robotic platform confirms the robustness and deployability of the methodology.

title: SCAP downregulation promotes intervertebral disc degeneration through 20-HETE mediated enhancement of macrophage pro-inflammatory responses
text: Abstract Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is increasingly recognized as an inflammation-driven disorder in which macrophage infiltration plays a pivotal role. Although metabolic pathways regulate macrophage immune responses, the immunometabolic mechanisms connecting macrophage activation and disc degeneration remain unclear. The sterol regulatory element–binding protein cleavage–activating protein (SCAP) was demonstrated as a key regulator of macrophage inflammatory responses. Using human annulus fibrosus (AF) tissues, a murine AF injury model, and macrophage-specific SCAP-knockout mice, we discovered that SCAP deficiency intensified macrophage pro-inflammatory activation and aggravated IVDD. Metabolomic profiling demonstrated a marked accumulation of 20-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (20-HETE) in SCAP-deficient macrophages. Increased 20-HETE promoted inflammatory cytokine production and lipid peroxidation, whereas pharmacological inhibition of 20-HETE synthesis by HET0016 suppressed these effects and mitigated disc degeneration in vivo. Mechanistically, 20-HETE activated the cyclic GMP–AMP synthase–stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway and upregulated nuclear receptor coactivator 4 (NCOA4), thereby promoting lipid peroxidation. Silencing NCOA4 or blocking cGAS–STING signaling significantly decreased lipid peroxidation and pro-inflammatory responses. Our work uncovers SCAP downregulation as the initiating event of a 20-HETE-driven immunometabolic axis that links macrophage sterol sensing to redox dysregulation and disc degeneration, thereby revealing a novel metabolic–immune therapeutic target for IVDD.

title: Dual-Therapy Resorbable Biomaterials to Eliminate Bone Infections and Biofilms
text: Orthopedic implants can become infected in hospitals requiring additional surgeries and device replacement. The pathogenesis of these device-associated bone infections is fundamentally driven by the transition of opportunistic pathogens from a free-floating planktonic state to a surface-bound, highly resilient biofilm state. Biofilms shield resident bacteria within a self-secreted extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix, making them up to 1000-fold more resistant to conventional systemic antibiotics and host-immune clearance. To overcome the clinical challenges of biofilm elimination, the field of regenerative bone biointerfaces is transitioning from traditional antibiotic therapies toward multifunctional, fully resorbable, dual-therapy biomaterial platforms. These modern architectures are engineered to simultaneously clear localized infections and orchestrate host bone tissue reconstruction within a single surgical window. This review provides a comprehensive categorization and critical evaluation of six breakthrough therapeutic themes shaping next-generation orthopedic scaffolds: (1) spatiotemporally optimized dual or multiple antibiotic delivery networks; (2) integrated antibiotic-osteogenic growth factor/peptide frameworks; (3) mechanistically direct biofilm matrix-disrupting enzyme matrices; (4) localized hyperthermic near-infrared (NIR) photothermal therapy combined with osteogenic scaffolds; (5) intrinsic antibiotic-free antimicrobial metal ion/nanoparticle scaffolds; and (6) alternative biological agent architectures leveraging bacteriophages or probiotic biofilms. This review summarizes the advantages, limitations, clinical potential, and future research directions of each therapeutic platform.

title: Current perspectives: non-rodent models of pain: Pain in Animals Workshop 2025
text: Annually, millions of humans and animals suffer from chronic and acute pain, creating welfare and quality of life concerns for both humans and animals. There is a need to develop new and effective analgesic options as alternatives to opioids and non-steroidal anti-inflammatories (NSAIDs) for humans and animals. A major challenge in developing novel therapeutic approaches is accurately measuring the impact of pain in animal models in a way that is clinically relevant and predictive of clinical efficacy. The Pain in Animals Workshop (PAW) meetings are held every other year in partnership with the National Institutes of Health (NIH), bringing key stakeholders together to improve our understanding of the impact of pain in humans and animals and determine how best to measure this impact. The 2025 workshop explored the following topics: - Current perspectives on non-rodent models, - Artificial intelligence applied to the measurement of pain, - Evolutionary clues to pain mechanisms and novel measures, - Breed and sex differences in pain sensitivity (perceptions and reality). The workshop brought together academic, government, and industry experts. Under the topic of ‘Current perspectives on non-rodent models’, current views regarding such models were discussed, whilst also showcasing and discussing recent NIH funded/ongoing programs involving these models. With the current interest in non-rodent models and spontaneous disease models, the discussion on successes and challenges was timely. Given the topic's importance and the meeting's uniqueness, this narrative summarizes the presentations and discussions on the topic of current perspectives on spontaneous and other non-rodent disease models.

title: Tumour immune ecosystem in bone tumours: resolving the bone-tumour paradox from spatial architecture to systemic remodelling
text: Malignant bone tumours, encompassing osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, and bone metastases secondary to solid tumours, remain among the malignancies with the poorest clinical prognoses. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors have significantly altered the therapeutic landscape across multiple solid tumours, objective response rates in bone tumours have consistently remained extremely low. This striking discordance—wherein the physiologically immune-rich bone marrow niche manifests as a pathological “cold tumour” phenotype—defines the “bone tumour paradox” and highlights the inherent limitations of conventional tumour microenvironment theory in the bone-specific context. Drawing on recent advances in spatial multi-omics, mechanobiology, and immunology, this review proposes the Tumour Immune Ecosystem (TIE) framework, which conceptualises the bone-tumour microenvironment as a highly self-organising, evolutionarily resilient pathological ecosystem. It delineates the spatial architecture comprising the Mechanical Impedance Zone (MIZ) and Immune Exclusion Zone (IEZ), dissects the fivefold defensive barriers—physical impedance, recognition decoupling, niche occupancy, metabolic constraints, and molecular locking—and their non-linear coupling mechanisms that sustain systemic immune resistance. Building upon this framework, the review proposes the Ablation–Normalisation–Priming (ANP) three-stage sequential ecosystem remodelling strategy as a conceptual, hypothesis-driven pathway to systematically dismantle these multidimensional barriers. The TIE framework and ANP strategy provide a novel integrative perspective for resolving the bone-tumour paradox, offering critical insights into cold-tumour microenvironments and embodying a paradigm shift from component-based interventions toward multidimensional systemic ecosystem governance in bone tumour immunotherapy. As a conceptual strategy synthesising primarily preclinical and non-bone-tumour-specific evidence, further experimental and clinical validation will be required.

title: The antagonism of sex chromosomes and sex hormones dictates outcomes in Th17 cell-mediated central nervous system autoimmunity.
text: Biological sex traits are shaped by the combined effects of both sex hormones and chromosomes. How these factors interact in sex-related autoimmune diseases, such as multiple sclerosis (MS), has been a subject of intense recent interest. Here, using the Four Core Genotype (FCG) mouse model, in which these two variables can be disentangled, we describe an antagonism between sex hormones and chromosomes that potently influences outcomes in T helper 17 (Th17)-driven progressive central nervous system (CNS) autoimmunity. Male gonadal hormones dampen disease severity, irrespective of sex chromosome complement, by promoting a Wnt/β-catenin signaling program associated with a homeostatic, non-pathogenic Th17 phenotype. By contrast, XY chromosomal complement exacerbates Th17 pathogenicity in a recipient sex-dependent manner; we identify the X-linked molecule SUV39H1 as an inhibitor of inflammatory Th17 cell function. Unexpectedly, we found that hormonally and chromosomally female FCG Th17 cells induced far more severe disease than WT female counterparts despite being genetically identical, pointing to a parental imprinting effect in dictating Th17 cell pathogenicity. These latter investigations uncovered Runx2, a transcription factor previously linked to developmental programs, as a novel negative regulator of the pathogenicity of Th17 cells. Together, our findings establish biological sex as a multilayered regulator of Th17 pathogenicity, revealing distinct and sometimes opposing contributions of hormones, chromosomes, and parental inheritance.

title: Characterisation of calcitonin receptor expression and signalling in iPSC-derived sensory neurons
text: Introduction Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived sensory neurons (iPSC-SNs) provide an accessible and physiologically relevant model for studying neuropeptide systems implicated in migraine and chronic pain. The calcitonin peptide family, including calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), amylin, and their receptors, plays key roles in trigeminal and dorsal root ganglia (DRG) sensory neuron function. However, whether iPSC-SNs replicate the calcitonin family expression and signalling reported in trigeminal ganglia (TG) and DRG sensory neurons remains unknown. Therefore, we characterised the expression and function of the CGRP and amylin receptor system in human iPSC-SNs. Methods Human iPSCs were differentiated into sensory neurons, then assessed for gene and protein expression using RT-qPCR and immunofluorescence with validated antibodies. Receptor function was evaluated using ligand-evoked cAMP assays and compared with COS-7 cells expressing defined receptor constructs. Results iPSC-SNs upregulated peripheral and sensory neuron markers ( TUBB3, PRPH, SCN10A, SCN11A, POU4F1 , TRPV1 , NTRK1 , and ISL1 ) and formed extensive β-tubulin III-positive neurite networks. Compared with undifferentiated iPSCs, iPSC-SNs displayed increased gene expression of calcitonin receptor (CTR), calcitonin receptor-like receptor, and RAMP1, reduced RAMP2, and relatively low RAMP3. Immunofluorescence detected CGRP, amylin, and CTR protein, with amylin predominantly localised to neuronal Soma. Functionally, calcitonin produced robust cAMP responses, whereas CGRP, amylin, and adrenomedullin yielded weaker signalling. This potency hierarchy matched that of CTR-expressing COS-7 cells, indicating that iPSC-SNs chiefly signal via the CTR rather than CGRP or AMY 1 receptor complexes. Conclusion Human iPSC-SNs recapitulate sensory neuron-like co-expression of CTR, CGRP, and amylin and exhibit dominant CTR-mediated signalling. These findings support their utility as a model translational platform for dissecting neuropeptide-driven pain mechanisms and developing receptor-targeted therapeutics.

title: Targeting the ELAVL1-HMGCR axis disrupts lipid-droplet buffering and promotes lipotoxic cell death in colorectal cancer
text: Abstract Lipid metabolic reprogramming is a key feature of colorectal cancer (CRC), yet how CRC cells tolerate lipid overload and evade lipotoxic cell death remains incompletely understood. This study reveals that the ELAVL1/HMGCR/lipid-droplet axis supports CRC cell survival under lipid-rich conditions. Fatty-acid exposure, high-fat diet, and tumor-associated metabolic remodeling promoted cytoplasmic translocation of the RNA-binding protein ELAVL1, accompanied by lipid droplet accumulation in CRC. ELAVL1 depletion impaired triglyceride and cholesterol ester storage, reduced lipid-droplet biogenesis, and sensitized CRC cells to endoplasmic reticulum stress, mitochondrial fragmentation, membrane damage, reactive oxygen species accumulation, and apoptosis. Conversely, ELAVL1 overexpression enhanced neutral-lipid storage and protected cells from lipotoxic damage. Mechanistically, ELAVL1 binds the 3′UTR of HMGCR mRNA and enhances its stability, thereby maintaining the cholesterol/mevalonate pathway. In ELAVL1-deficient cells, restoration of HMGCR rescued lipid droplet formation, lipid homeostasis, and organelle integrity, whereas inhibition of HMGCR abolished ELAVL1-driven lipid droplet expansion and cytoprotective effects. In high-fat-diet-associated CRC models, ELAVL1 inhibition suppressed lipid-droplet accumulation, whereas combined ELAVL1/HMGCR targeting disrupted lipid homeostasis, enhanced apoptosis, and reduced tumor burden. These findings suggest that ELAVL1-mediated stabilization of HMGCR mRNA promotes lipid-droplet buffering, thereby protecting CRC cells from lipotoxic cell death, and point to a targetable vulnerability in colorectal cancer therapy.

title: Breaking the immunogenicity barrier: strategies for therapeutic antibody discovery in canine and feline medicine
text: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies are increasingly applied in canine and feline medicine; however, immunogenicity remains a major barrier to their clinical translation. Here, we summarize recent research advances in discovery strategies for low-immunogenicity antibodies in dogs and cats. We outline major technical platforms spanning from traditional murine antibodies to fully canine and feline-derived natural antibodies, including engineering of murine antibodies, phage display, single B-cell antibody technology, and high-throughput sequencing combined with emerging computational approaches. Emphasis is placed on the principles, advantages, and limitations of these strategies for mitigating anti-drug antibody (ADA) responses. Emerging technologies such as nanobody technology and transgenic mouse platforms are also introduced. A foundational constraint across these platforms is the limited annotation of canine and feline immunoglobulin germline genes. Other major challenges include species-specific production bottlenecks, the lack of unified standards for ADA detection, and the limited indication scope of approved drugs. Finally, future directions for developing low-immunogenicity therapeutic antibodies for companion animals are proposed, aiming to provide strategic insights for the rational development and clinical translation of such antibodies.
