title: Technology-Driven Prevention of Examination Paper Leaks in High-Stakes Educational Assessment to Support Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): A Bibliometric and Focused Literature Review
text: Examination paper leaks threaten educational equity, public trust, and merit-based selection in high-stakes educational assessment. This study examines technology-driven prevention of examination paper leaks to support Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through a bibliometric and focused literature review. The review discusses blockchain-based question paper management, artificial intelligence (AI) proctoring, biometric authentication, cryptographic protection, digital watermarking, zero-knowledge proof frameworks, and generative AI-related academic integrity risks. Layered and policy-integrated technological approaches are needed to strengthen secure, fair, accountable, and SDG-oriented assessment systems.

title: Reimagining Patient Care in the Digital Health Era: A Systematic Literature Review and Analytical Synthesis
text: Background. Telemedicine, electronic health records (EHRs), mobile and wearable devices, and artificial intelligence (AI) are widely presented as instruments for transforming patient care. The evidence for them is fragmented across technologies, disciplines and settings. Objective. To synthesise evidence on how digital health reshapes access, clinical decision-making, clinician workload, patient engagement, governance and equity, and to derive an integrative framework for reimagining patient care. Methods. A systematic literature review reported in line with PRISMA 2020, combined with an analytical synthesis. Two evidence streams were screened. The first was an author-supplied corpus of 117 records, of which 27 were retained. The second was a purposively assembled external stream of 47 sources. Data were extracted, tabulated and analysed thematically across seven themes and six stakeholder perspectives. Results. Seventy-four sources were synthesised. In a direct-observation study of US ambulatory practice, physicians spent 49.2% of the office day on EHR and desk work against 27.0% on face-to-face care. In same-sample imaging comparisons, deep-learning tools reached a pooled sensitivity of 87.0% against 86.4% for clinicians. A widely deployed sepsis-prediction model, however, achieved an external-validation AUC of only 0.63 and missed 67% of sepsis cases. Globally, 81% of urban residents but only 50% of rural residents used the Internet in 2023, and internet use was 93% in high-income countries against 27% in low-income countries. India's national digital mission had created 79.71 crore health accounts by July 2025. Conclusions. Digital tools improve care when they are embedded in redesigned workflows, validated locally, governed transparently and deployed with equity safeguards. Otherwise they shift burden or reproduce disparities. We propose a five-layer Reimagined Care Framework (Access, Intelligence, Workflow, Trust, Learning) aligned with the Quintuple Aim.

title: Towards biodiversity-relevant chemical risk assessment: insights from SETAC Europe 2025
text: A special session entitled “ Biodiversity and chemical hazard/risk assessment: regulatory frameworks, integrative approaches and research for a sustainable future ” was held at the SETAC Europe 2025 Annual Meeting. The session explored how environmental risk assessment (ERA) of chemicals can better support biodiversity protection, drawing on presentations, panel discussions and a live survey of over 100 participants. While existing prospective ERAs were recognised as providing a foundational framework for regulatory decision-making, the discussions highlighted persistent limitations in ecological realism. Key concerns included limited taxonomic coverage, insufficient consideration of indirect effects, and lack of integration of chemical mixtures and multiple stressors, alongside ongoing difficulties in translating laboratory findings into meaningful biodiversity-relevant outcomes in real-world ecosystems. Participants identified 105 barriers and proposed 95 solutions, leading to a set of strategic recommendations. Recommendations emerging from the discussions call for: (1) operationalising biodiversity protection goals into measurable endpoints aligned across policy frameworks; (2) increasing ecological realism and predictive capacity through modelling and integrative approaches; (3) embedding routine assessment of chemical mixtures and multiple stressors; (4) strengthening links between ERA and environmental monitoring (covering biota biodiversity, and chemicals), supported by findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable (FAIR) data infrastructures; and (5) improving governance and implementation to enable preventive and protective actions. Together, these priorities outline a pathway for advancing biodiversity-focused ERA that better reflects real-world complexity and supports sustainable chemical management.

title: Trust Adaptive Provenance Watermarking for Synthetic News Broadcasting
text: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence in digital news broadcasting has increased the production of synthetic news content, raising critical concerns regarding authenticity, source verification, content manipulation, and audience trust. This study proposes a trust-adaptive provenance watermarking framework designed to dynamically protect and verify AI-generated news content by integrating provenance information with trust-aware watermarking mechanisms throughout the broadcasting workflow. The proposed framework combines adaptive digital watermarking, provenance metadata, and a trust-scoring mechanism that adjusts watermark strength according to content sensitivity, source credibility, and manipulation risk. Experimental evaluation is conducted using synthetic news samples under common content transformations, including compression, resizing, cropping, re-encoding, and partial manipulation, while performance is assessed through watermark detection accuracy, robustness, content quality, and provenance verification reliability. The experimental findings demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves high watermark detectability while maintaining acceptable perceptual quality across different broadcasting transformations. The adaptive trust mechanism further improves provenance verification for high-risk synthetic content and enables more reliable identification of manipulated or unauthorized news assets compared with conventional fixed-strength watermarking approaches. The proposed trust-adaptive provenance watermarking framework provides a practical approach for strengthening authenticity, traceability, and accountability in synthetic news broadcasting, offering a foundation for trustworthy AI-enabled media ecosystems while supporting broadcasters, audiences, and digital platforms in mitigating misinformation and unauthorized content manipulation.

title: Becoming aware at the point of care: a context-aware architecture for bridging semantic representation and interpretation of inter-organizational patient information
text: Abstract Background Fragmented patient records across healthcare organizations limit clinicians’ awareness of relevant patient information, while increased information availability may complicate identifying and interpreting information relevant to the current clinical situation. Although interoperability standards enable data exchange between systems, they do not necessarily create awareness of, identify, or help interpret information relevant to the current clinical situation. This highlights a gap between semantic representation and clinicians’ interpretation and use of information in practice. This study investigates how context-aware information access and contextualization can help bridge this gap. Methods Guided by Design Science Research, we developed the Context Resolver architecture as a detailed architectural specification of a key component within a previously established information-centric architecture framework. The architecture combines vector-based semantic retrieval, lightweight information tokens, provenance-preserving mechanisms, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to support context-aware information access. A prototype was demonstrated through a multimorbid patient scenario using synthetic clinical data. Two ex-ante and one ex-post formative evaluations involving clinical and technical experts assessed problem relevance, architecture design, and the prototype’s representation of proposed architectural mechanisms. Results The Context Resolver architecture addressed requirements related to contextual cueing, provenance, adaptive summarization, and support for information interpretation. The architecture promotes awareness of relevant cross-organizational clinical activities before deeper information access. Vector-based retrieval provided mechanisms intended to support access to contextually relevant information, while bounded GenAI synthesis generated provenance-linked summaries designed to reduce information overload through contextual filtering and summarization. The evaluations suggested that the identified problem is clinically relevant and that the proposed architecture provides a plausible response aligned with stakeholder needs, governance requirements, and clinical information practice. Conclusions The Context Resolver illustrates an architectural approach that combines machine-readable information representation with mechanisms intended to support contextual interpretation and use of information in clinical practice. The study contributes a detailed architectural specification of the Context Resolver as socio-technical design knowledge for semantic interoperability in health information systems and illustrates how awareness, context-aware retrieval, provenance-preserving access, and responsible GenAI may support information access across organizational boundaries. The findings suggest that semantic interoperability can benefit from complementing machine-readable information exchange with mechanisms supporting awareness, contextualization, and interpretation in clinical practice.

Keywords / Index Terms**Artificial Intelligence, Precision Oncology, Deep Learning, Cancer Screening, Diagnostic Imaging, Multimodal Data Integration, Clinical Decision Support, Human-AI Collaboration, Health Equity, Andhra Pradesh, Low-Resource Settings, Regulatory Frameworks. --- ### Part 2: Detailed Description of the Research Paper **Abstract**The escalating global cancer burden, compounded by disparities in healthcare access, presents a critical challenge to oncological care. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping the cancer care continuum—from early detection to personalized treatment—by leveraging capabilities in image recognition, multimodal data integration, and clinical decision support. This paper systematically reviews key AI applications in oncology, including diagnostic imaging, pathology analysis, treatment optimization, and toxicity prediction. It contextualizes these advancements within real-world implementations, such as Andhra Pradesh's newly launched precision oncology ecosystem and the deployment of AI-powered pulmonary nodule screening. The review finds that while AI achieves performance comparable to specialist physicians in specific diagnostic tasks, its clinical value remains constrained by limited external validation, data heterogeneity, and the maturity of human-AI collaboration workflows. We argue that AI's appropriate role in oncology is to augment—not replace—clinical judgment, and that scalable impact depends on coordinated progress in infrastructure integration, regulatory frameworks, and continuous performance monitoring. **1. title: Digital intelligence for depression governance: an environome framework to bridge research and policy
text: Background Digital intelligence platforms are transforming how policymakers synthesize and translate mental health evidence into actionable strategies. Depression research is vast but highly fragmented, limiting its effective use in policy design. We introduce the Interactive Depression Dashboard (InDepDash), designed to integrate and operationalize multidisciplinary evidence on depression. Methods InDepDash aggregates and analyzes 139,761 depression-related studies (from 2005 to 2025) spanning clinical, social, and environmental domains. The platform maps evidence across multiple determinants of mental health, conceptualized as the “environome,” including personal, social, natural, and built factors. Ontology-based annotation, semantic search, and co-occurrence analysis enable real-time exploration of research trends, gaps, and priorities, while case study applications illustrate its policy relevance. Results The platform identified substantial imbalances in the evidence base. Natural and built environmental determinants represented 14.3% of the analyzed corpus; within this domain, climate-change-specific evidence was comparatively sparse. InDepDash effectively highlights underexplored domains and supports prioritization of interventions, including neuroinclusive policies, disaster resilience strategies, and climate-informed mental health planning. Conclusion Evidence-mapping platforms such as InDepDash provide critical infrastructure for adaptive and evidence-informed governance in mental health. By enhancing the accessibility, transparency, and integration of complex data, they enable policymakers to respond to emerging challenges with greater speed. This study supports the Trustworthiness, Reproducibility, Explainability, Applicability, and Transparency (TREAT) framework as a foundation for ethical AI deployment, addressing key gaps in research translation while working toward global mental health equity.

title: Digital Health Literacy and Healthcare Access Among Rural and Underserved Communities in India
text: Digital health has become an important component of healthcare delivery in India, particularly for extending services to rural and underserved populations. However, the availability of digital health platforms does not automatically guarantee equitable access. Digital health literacy, internet connectivity, affordability, language, disability, privacy concerns, social support and confidence in using technology influence whether individuals can effectively benefit from digital healthcare services. This review examines the relationship between digital health literacy and healthcare access among rural and underserved communities in India and discusses the potential contribution of community health nursing. Published literature and major policy and programme documents concerning digital health, telemedicine, digital health literacy, rural healthcare access and community based digital services were reviewed. The evidence indicates that digital technologies can reduce geographical barriers, facilitate remote consultations, support continuity of care and improve access to health information. However, persistent digital inequalities, limited awareness, inadequate infrastructure, low digital literacy and concerns regarding privacy and trust may restrict equitable utilization. Indian initiatives such as the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission and eSanjeevani demonstrate the potential of digital platforms to strengthen primary healthcare and connect underserved populations with health professionals. Community health nurses and other frontline health workers can act as important intermediaries by providing digital health education, assisting patients with digital services, promoting safe use of online health information and supporting continuity between digital and face to face care. Digital health equity therefore requires an integrated approach combining infrastructure, digital literacy, accessible technology, community participation, health workforce training, privacy protection and responsive public policy.

title: STRIDE-DB: A Structured, Risk-Aware and Intelligent Framework for Legacy Database Transformation in Hybrid Cloud Environments
text: Legacy database systems are still being required to support mission-critical applications, which need to be scalable, interoperable, resilient, governed, cloud-operated and more. The problem with modernizing these systems is that transforming the data from a database is not only hard to do because the data is much more than just schemas and data transfer, but also because of structural dependency, semantic correspondence, data quality, complexity of the transform, migration risk, resources required, deployment constraints, etc. Most of the current solutions address this issue individually, and not as part of a migration decisioning process. In this paper, the authors propose a hybrid cloud-based transformation framework for the evolution of the intelligent legacy database, called as Structured Transformation and Risk-aware Intelligent Database Evolution (STRIDE-DB). The intelligent cloud recommendation, automatic transformation and migration planning, validation tool, explainable AI, machine learning risk prediction, ensemble learning, business rule integrity, data quality, dependency discovery and verification, and metadata discovery are all features of the STRIDE-DB architecture. The following tests (BaseLine, SemanticStress, DataQualityStress, DependencyStress, CombinedStress and optimized migration) are run on a controlled experimental layer. The current implementation was tested with seven source tables with about 59825 records and 38 attributes of a relational database. The knowledge representation layer created 49 nodes and 43 edges, while the graph representation learning created 64-dimensional node embeddings. The pre-migration risk indicator was determined to be 0.1717 (low risk), and the transformation-complexity indicator was determined to be 0.2184 (low complexity). Out of 38 attribute mappings, 35 were chosen to be automatically transformed, and three were kept for further review due to a lack of confidence. The average target attribute coverage was 94.05% while the average target completeness was 99.66%. Furthermore, the framework offers a number of machine learning classifiers, multiple classifiers, ensemble learning, explanation using SHAP, auto-generated SQL and SQL-recommended and explanation for the hybrid cloud. The results show that the concept of integrated pipeline STRIDE-DB is viable for database modernization for structured and risk-aware databases. It is a small table-level data set, however, and is just a feasibility examination of the implementation stage, as a substitute for a generalization skill in the machine-learning evaluation. More large-scale, multi-dataset and multi-scenario evaluations to prove the predictive models are valid are required.

title: Awareness of Patient Rights in Digital Health Services
text: Abstract Objective The purpose of this study is to investigate the degree of understanding of the rights of patients in terms of the features of their socio-demographic status and how they use digital health tools. Materials and Models: This research is a descriptive, observational and cross-sectional survey of 300 adults who are over the age of 18 and who are either familiar with digital health or have previously used at least one digital health service. The data collection consisted of two methods: a demographic questionnaire covering socio-demographic and digital health use features and a Patient Rights Awareness Scale consisting of 20 items. Descriptive statistics, parametric/non-parametric analysis, correlations, and regression modeling were carried out to analyze the data. Results The study found that people were aware of the patients' rights at a good level, and using the scale demonstrated good internal consistency. There were found differences in patient rights awareness with respect to education level and some characteristics of digital health utilization. In addition, a positive correlation between digital health knowledge with the level of awareness of patient rights was established, and this variable demonstrated the highest degree of relationship with the variable of awareness in the correlation analysis. Moreover, in the multivariate analysis, the variable of digital health knowledge was the one that maintained its significant correlation with the level of patient rights awareness regardless of the influence from other sociodemographic and digital health utilization variables. Conclusion Knowledge of patient rights in the digital health environment is closely related to the level of individuals’ digital health literacy. The findings indicate that expanding digital health services is not adequate; individuals should be supported in understanding and applying their rights in the digital environment. The implementation of issues such as patients’ rights, guarantee of privacy, protection of health data, and informed consent in digital health literacy programs may help in providing patient-centered and rights-based digital health solutions.

title: Cross-border health care seeking among Somali nationals: a multi-country rapid evidence synthesis of determinants, outcome domains, economic burden and health-system implications, 2014–2026
text: Abstract Background Somali nationals travel abroad for care that the domestic health system cannot supply, yet the scale, clinical drivers, costs and outcomes of this movement have not been synthesised. We aimed to consolidate the available evidence on outbound medical travel from Somalia to India, Türkiye, Ethiopia and Egypt, to distinguish what is measured from what is not, and to draw implications for health financing and governance. Methods We conducted a rapid evidence synthesis of evidence from 2014 to 2026. Sources were Indian parliamentary and ministerial series, peer-reviewed studies, country-of-origin reports, health-financing documents and consular guidance. Synthesis was narrative because heterogeneity precluded pooling. Every statement was assigned to one of three evidence tiers: directly measured, credibly inferred or unquantifiable. Movement indicators count episodes, not unique patients, and expenditure envelopes are planning scenarios, not accounts. Results India is the only corridor with a nationality-specific public series: 13,585 medical-purpose arrivals in 2015–2017 and 47,880 medical visas in 2019–2024 (2018 unavailable), a minimum of 61,465 episodes. Medical visas peaked at 16,411 in 2023, 4.8 times the 2019 level, and fell to 12,261 in 2024. Türkiye offers a single anchor (2,742 Somali patients in 2019); Ethiopia and Egypt lack nationality-specific series. Demand concentrates in oncology, cardiovascular and renal disease, advanced diagnostics, reproductive medicine and orthopaedics. A snowball survey of 106 medical travellers in Garowe reported a mean direct cost of US$8,543 per episode. Out-of-pocket payments met 30.8% of current health expenditure in 2023. Applying published per-patient benchmarks to Indian visas gives US$88–105 million for 2024; a four-corridor central scenario gives approximately US$219 million, about 1.8% of projected gross domestic product. No pooled morbidity, complication or mortality rate can be derived, because outbound episodes are not linked to treatment or outcome. Conclusions Outbound travel functions as an unregulated, privately financed parallel tertiary-care system that is substantial in scale, financially consequential and largely unmeasured in outcome. We propose a minimum outbound-referral dataset, pooled catastrophic-illness protection linked to authorised referral, facilitator licensing, bilateral referral compacts and sequenced domestic investment in oncology diagnostics, chemotherapy, dialysis and imaging.

title: Real Money, Fake Models: Deceptive Model Claims in Shadow APIs
text: Access to frontier large language models (LLMs), such as GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5, is often hindered by high pricing, payment barriers, and regional restrictions. These limitations drive the proliferation of $\textit{shadow APIs}$, third-party services that claim to provide access to official model services without regional limitations via indirect access. Despite their widespread use, it remains unclear whether shadow APIs deliver outputs consistent with those of the official APIs, raising concerns about the reliability of downstream applications and the validity of research findings that depend on them. In this paper, we present the first systematic audit between official LLM APIs and corresponding shadow APIs. We first identify 17 shadow APIs that have been utilized in 187 academic papers, with the most popular one reaching 5,966 citations and 58,639 GitHub stars by December 6, 2025. Through multidimensional auditing of three representative shadow APIs across utility, safety, and model verification, we uncover both indirect and direct evidence of deception practices in shadow APIs. Specifically, we reveal performance divergence reaching up to $47.21\%$, significant unpredictability in safety behaviors, and identity verification failures in $45.83\%$ of fingerprint tests. These deceptive practices critically undermine the reproducibility and validity of scientific research, harm the interests of shadow API users, and damage the reputation of official model providers.

title: Statistical benchmarking of optimization methods for a variational quantum eigensolver under quantum noise
text: This work investigates the performance of numerical optimization algorithms applied to the State-Averaged Orbital-Optimized Variational Quantum Eigensolver for the H2 molecule under various quantum noise conditions. The goal is to assess the stability, accuracy, and computational efficiency of commonly used gradient-based, gradient-free, and global optimization strategies within the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum regime. We systematically compare six representative optimizers, BFGS, SLSQP, Nelder-Mead, Powell, COBYLA, and iSOMA, under ideal, stochastic, and decoherence noise models, including phase damping, depolarizing, and thermal relaxation channels. Each optimizer was tested over multiple noise intensities and measurement settings to characterize convergence behavior and sensitivity to noise-induced landscape distortions. The results show that BFGS consistently achieves the most accurate energies with minimal evaluations, maintaining robustness even under moderate decoherence. COBYLA performs well for low-cost approximations, while SLSQP exhibits instability in noisy regimes. Global approaches such as iSOMA show potential but are computationally expensive. These findings provide practical guidance for selecting suitable optimizers in variational quantum simulations, highlighting the importance of noise-aware optimization strategies for reliable and efficient quantum chemistry computations on current hardware.

title: Hyperbolic Large Language Models
text: Abstract. Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success and demonstrated superior performance across various tasks, including natural language processing (NLP), weather forecasting, biological protein folding, text generation, and solving mathematical problems. However, many real-world data exhibit highly non-Euclidean latent hierarchical anatomy, such as protein networks, transportation networks, financial networks, brain networks, and linguistic structures or syntactic trees in natural languages. Effectively learning intrinsic semantic entailment and hierarchical relationships from these raw, unstructured input data using LLMs remains an underexplored area. Due to its effectiveness in modeling tree-like hierarchical structures, hyperbolic geometry—a non-Euclidean space—has rapidly gained popularity as an expressive latent representation space for complex data modeling across domains such as graphs, images, languages, and multimodal data. Here, we provide a comprehensive and contextual exposition of recent advancements in LLMs that leverage hyperbolic geometry as a representation space to enhance semantic representation learning and multiscale reasoning. Specifically, the paper presents a taxonomy of the principal techniques of hyperbolic LLMs (HypLLMs) in terms of four main categories: (1) hyperbolic LLMs through exp/log maps; (2) hyperbolic fine-tuned models; (3) fully hyperbolic LLMs; and (4) hyperbolic state-space models. We also explore crucial potential applications and outline future research directions. A repository of key papers, models, datasets, and code implementations is available at https://github.com/sarangp2402/Hyperbolic-LLM-Models .

title: Scaling medical imaging report generation with multimodal reinforcement learning
text: Abstract In medical imaging report generation, supervised fine-tuning can overfit to superficial patterns and generalize poorly across institutions. We introduce Universal Report Generation (UNIRG), which adopts reinforcement learning to directly optimize clinically meaningful quality criteria. With this framework, we developed UNIRG-CXR, an 8-billion-parameter vision–language model trained on four public datasets (MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert Plus, ReXGradient-160k and IU-Xray) by supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning (group-relative policy optimization) against a composite lexical, semantic and clinical-error reward. We evaluated held-out test sets and an external proprietary dataset, with RadCliQ as primary metric and expert radiologist validation. Here we show that our method improves report quality and generalization: UNIRG-CXR surpasses prior models on the ReXrank benchmark across four datasets and two generation settings, exceeding the previous best score by over 50% on two test sets, and produces fewer clinically significant errors while maintaining performance on unseen data sources and across demographic subgroups.

title: Toward chemically accurate quantum simulations on quantum hardware: A quantum-HPC hybrid approach
text: We report one of the most comprehensive experimental demonstrations to date of quantum-computing-based molecular simulation on IQM's Sirius 24-qubit superconducting quantum processor, using up to 16 operational qubits. We employ Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) with the Local Unitary Cluster Jastrow (LUCJ) Ansatz to compute ground-state energies of benchmark molecular systems, including H2, LiH, BeH2, H2O, and NH3. We further introduce the linear-CNOT unitary coupled-cluster singles and doubles Ansatz within the SQD framework, reducing the classical pre-computation overhead at the cost of increased quantum circuit depth and demonstrate its effectiveness by accurately recovering the ground-state energies of H2, LiH, and BeH2. A comparative analysis of the two Ansätze is presented, highlighting their respective merits, demerits, and practical use cases in near-term quantum simulations. In addition, we perform one-dimensional potential energy surface (1D-PES) scans for H2 and HeH+ using STO-3G and 6-31G basis sets and for LiH and BeH2 using STO-3G. We also report the first experimental generation of a full two-dimensional potential energy surface (2D-PES) map, consisting of a 32 × 32 grid in bond length and bond angle, for the water molecule in the STO-3G basis on IQM quantum hardware. Beyond small-molecule benchmarks, we integrate Density Matrix Embedding Theory (DMET) with SQD(LUCJ) to obtain chemically accurate 4-electron-in-4-orbital active-space energies for eight ligand-like molecules, as well as for the pharmacologically relevant amantadine molecular system, representing the first of such experimental demonstrations. Across all studies, the majority of quantum-computed energies agree with reference full configuration interaction results and with DMET-complete active space CI energies for embedded systems, to within chemical accuracy for the chosen basis sets. These results demonstrate the robustness of quantum sampling-based classical diagonalization approaches while highlighting the promise of hybrid embedding strategies combined with near-term Ansätze for advancing quantum chemistry toward classically intractable molecular systems and establishing their practicality on current quantum hardware.

title: Information formatting in neuronal populations predicts differential functional contributions to behavior
text: Neurons throughout the brain encode essentially everything, so why have distinct areas? We proposed that areas format different information sources differently, implying their computational role. Here we compared the middle temporal (MT) area, involved in visual motion perception, and the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), implicated in decision-making and reward. In a task that required monkeys to combine motion and reward information, both regions encoded both motion and reward, but formatted differently. Area MT represented them separably, whereas the dlPFC combined them in a decision-related format. A recurrent network model trained to reproduce that formatting predicted a distinct effect of stimulating those areas. Consistent with predictions, MT stimulation biased choices whereas dlPFC stimulation produced ‘winner-take-all’ outcomes. Our findings suggest that a modular structure flexibly reformats information to enable complex behaviors. Using experiments in monkeys and modeling, the authors demonstrate that the formatting of population information predicts the contribution of different brain areas to behavior.

title: Large language models for mental health
text: Digital technologies have long been explored as a complement to standard procedure in mental health research and practice, ranging from the management of electronic health records to app-based interventions. The recent emergence of large language models (LLMs), both proprietary and open-source ones, represents a major new opportunity on that front. Yet there is still a divide between the community developing LLMs and the one which may benefit from them, thus hindering the beneficial translation of the technology into clinical use. This divide largely stems from the lack of a common language and understanding regarding the technology’s inner workings, capabilities, and risks. Our tutorial-style review attempts to bridge this gap by providing intuitive explanations behind the basic concepts related to contemporary LLMs.

title: MemPoison: Bypassing Selective Memory Mechanisms to Plant Backdoors in LLM Agents
text: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly leverage long-term memory to support persistent and autonomous task execution. However, this capability also introduces a new attack surface: memory poisoning, where adversaries can inject malicious information to influence future behavior. Existing memory poisoning attacks often assume that injected content can be stored directly in memory, overlooking the selective extraction and rewriting stages in modern memory pipelines. This makes prior methods ineffective under realistic settings. In this paper, we propose MemPoison, a novel memory poisoning attack that bypasses selective memory mechanisms in LLM agents, where an attacker can inject triggerable backdoors into the agent's long-term memory through dialogue interactions, thereby misleading its subsequent responses. MemPoison introduces three key components: (i) a semantic relational bridge that binds the trigger and payload into a coherent statement to ensure their co-extraction into memory; (ii) entity masquerading that optimizes triggers to mimic named entities, resisting rewriting; and (iii) joint embedding optimization that shapes trigger-injected texts into a tight cluster in the embedding space while maintaining isolation from benign embeddings for stealth. Evaluations across different agent domains and memory mechanisms show MemPoison achieves attack success rates up to 0.95, outperforming existing baselines. Mechanistic analysis reveals the exploitation of embedding-space anisotropy and attention redistribution, highlighting core vulnerabilities in selective memory systems. We evaluate multiple defense strategies and demonstrate their fundamental limitations in mitigating the attack. We release our code to facilitate further research.

title: MIRAGE: Misleading Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Black-box and Query-agnostic Poisoning Attacks
text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems enhance LLMs with external knowledge but introduce a critical attack surface: corpus poisoning. While recent studies have demonstrated the potential of such attacks, they typically rely on impractical assumptions, such as white-box access or known user queries, thereby underestimating the difficulty of real-world exploitation. In this paper, we bridge this gap by proposing MIRAGE, a novel multi-stage poisoning pipeline designed for strict black-box and query-agnostic environments. Operating on surrogate model feedback, MIRAGE functions as an automated optimization framework that integrates three key mechanisms: it utilizes persona-driven query synthesis to approximate latent user search distributions, employs semantic anchoring to imperceptibly embed these intents for high retrieval visibility, and leverages an adversarial variant of Test-Time Preference Optimization (TPO) to maximize persuasion. To rigorously evaluate this threat, we construct a new benchmark derived from three long-form, domain-specific datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MIRAGE significantly outperforms existing baselines in both attack efficacy and stealthiness, exhibiting remarkable transferability across diverse retriever-LLM configurations and highlighting the urgent need for robust defense strategies.

title: Diff-ANO: Towards fast high-resolution ultrasound computed tomography via conditional consistency models and adjoint neural operators
text: Abstract Ultrasound computed tomography (USCT) reconstructs sound speed from incomplete, noisy scattered-wave measurements. Its instability arises from the nonlinear inverse map and acquisition geometry. Generative models can supply learned priors that stabilize such partial differential equation (PDE)-constrained inversions. In this work, we introduce Diff-ANO (Diffusion-based models with adjoint neural operators), which alternates conditional consistency model (CM) refinement with surrogate measurement-gradient optimization. One forward multigrid neural operator (MgNO) predicts the transmitter/receiver source-field bank; a conjugated residual combination of those fields then forms the adjoint action and sound-speed gradient. Across four acquisition geometries, our method delivers strong reconstruction quality with a 6.75×online speedup over solver-based refinement in a matched computational-efficiency comparison. Independent finer-grid WaveSim measurements reduce potential convergent Born series (CBS) inverse crime and yield reconstruction trends consistent with the matched-CBS study. Together with additional evaluations of intermediate refinements and ablations, these results support efficient data-informed, measurement-guided USCT reconstruction and motivate extension to more realistic acquisition physics and measured data.

title: Individual differences in sequential decision-making
text: People differ widely in how they make decisions in uncertain environments. While many studies leverage this variability to measure differences in specific cognitive processes and parameters, the key dimension(s) of individual variability in uncertain decision-making tasks has not been identified. Here, we analyzed behavioral data from 1001 participants performing a restless three-armed bandit task, where reward probabilities fluctuated unpredictably over time. Using a novel analytical approach that controlled for the stochasticity in this tasks, we identified a dominant nonlinear axis of individual variability. We found that this primary axis of variability was strongly and selectively correlated with the probability of exploration, as inferred by latent state modeling. This suggests that the major factor shaping individual differences in bandit task performance is the tendency to explore (versus exploit), rather than personality characteristics, reinforcement learning model parameters, or low-level strategies. Certain demographic characteristics also predicted variance along this principle axis: participants at the exploratory end tended to be younger than participants at the exploitative end, and self-identified men were overrepresented at both extremes. Together, these findings offer a principled framework for understanding individual differences in task behavior while highlighting the cognitive and demographic factors that shape individual differences in decision-making under uncertainty.

title: Midbrain somatostatin-expressing cells control pain-suppression during defensive states
text: In threatening situations, animals exhibit a broad range of behavioral and autonomic responses. As such, a crucial adaptive response is the inhibition of pain, which facilitates relevant defensive behaviors that promote survival. Whereas the structures and mechanisms involved in fear and pain behaviors are well documented, little is known about the precise neuronal mechanisms mediating the emotional regulation of endogenous pain-suppression. Here, we used a combination of behavioral, anatomical, optogenetic, and electrophysiological approaches to investigate, in male mice, the role of somatostatin-expressing cells in the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray matter (SST + vlPAG cells) in the control of analgesia induced during defensive states. Our data indicate that optogenetic inhibition of SST + vlPAG cells promotes analgesia irrespective of animal defensive state. In contrast, optogenetic activation of long-range SST + vlPAG cells that project to the rostral ventromedial medulla (RVM) abolishes the analgesia mediated by fear behavior. Together, these results identify a novel circuit mechanism composed of long-range SST + vlPAG cells projecting to the RVM that regulate analgesia elicited during defensive states.
